chapters.html:
Mydei would argue that he was very attentive when it came to other people’s conversations. With how little input of his own he added, it was hard not to be.

Talking wasn’t his strong suit, not in the way his friends liked to. He’d throw in a comment every now and then, but listening was something he’s grown very familiar with. A fact that seems to shock others with how good his memory truly is, not that Mydei found it to be that impressive. Grasping what someone was saying wasn’t really that hard.

Yet in this moment, it was the hardest thing in the world.

It started fine initially, it really did. Cipher was responding to an issue he had and he was listening, because that’s what he does. After a while, everything just started to drown out because while he knew she had good intentions, none of her ideas seemed ideal given the situation.

A situation he knew he didn’t have the right to be picky with. At least that’s what he told himself in the beginning.

It wasn’t his fault everything had gone to shit. It wasn’t his fault his well-paying job let him go over something they had done, and it definitely wasn’t his fault that nowhere seemed to be hiring to solve his crisis.

Was it his fault for being picky? It was, but the score was still three to one.

“Mydei. Are you even paying attention?”

No, he really wasn’t.

Normally he had no problem telling things how they were to Cipher, because they have been friends for years and she knew him by now. He could very well turn down every proposal with a grunt without it actually offending her, but the reality of it all held him back. The last thing he wanted to do was seem unappreciative, especially considering she was taking time from her day to help him. She didn’t have to. She could’ve been with Castorice instead.

Mydei sighed. “Sorry.”

“Okay,” she drawled, her voice unsure. “And you’re apologizing. Maybe I should leave you alone.”

He couldn’t, however, hold back his scoff. “Why is that so surprising?”

“Maybe because you’re apologizing for nothing, something you love to get on Castorice about?” She was right, he hated when people apologized for things they shouldn’t be sorry for. Hated even more that he had to admit – albeit to himself – that Cipher was right. “Seriously, you can tell me you hate the ideas. It’s not going to crush my spirits.”

Well, not that he needed her permission but – “Really?” He asked after a long sigh, looking at her incredulously. “A lingerie store?”

“You asked if I knew of anyone that was hiring.”

Mydei scowled. “And I don’t really want to think about why you know that.”

“Then don’t,” she shrugged, resting her arms atop the table. He was lucky the cafe they occupied wasn’t all that busy. The fewer people around to likely hear about his struggles, the better. “But you did come to me with something and the least you could do is throw me a bone by narrowing the options.”

He fought back another scoff. It was bad enough that he had to swallow his pride just to ask for her help.

“I can’t be picky.”

“Translation,” Cipher said. “‘I want to be picky.’”

Obviously he wanted to be picky. This was a job for crying out loud, a real life commitment. Something he’d have to rely on to pay his bills. The least it could be was enjoyable.

“Are you going to help me or not?” Maybe he should’ve told Castorice instead, he doubted the girl would relay the information back to Cipher if he asked her not to.

Unfortunately, Cipher’s previous comment reminded him of why he didn’t do that.

Because no one rivaled Mydei for being a blunt person other than Cipher herself, and that’s exactly what he needed right now. Someone to give it to him straight, like calling him out for wanting to be picky.

She took a sip of her drink, shaking her head as she brought the cup away from her face. “Why don’t you just take on a few small jobs? Personal service jobs, for example. I do it.”

Mydei deadpanned, because out of all the ridiculous ideas she’s given him today, this just might be the worst.

“You want me to dog sit.”

Cipher tilted her head forward. “I did not say dog sit.”

“You heavily implied it with that last part.”

“And would it be so bad if I did?”

Mydei is not subjecting himself to watching and walking other people’s dogs. To hell with not being picky. “I’m not a dog person. I don’t even know why you are.”

Cipher snorted. “I’m not. Cats don’t necessarily need babysitters, though.”

Precisely why he liked them so much, especially over dogs.

That still didn’t mean he was willing to consider her offer. Besides, it wasn’t even something she did full time. They were side gigs to occupy the moments when she wasn’t working. At her actual job.

It wouldn’t have been enough anyway.

He wished it would have been, maybe he wouldn’t have to think so hard about it. He’d bite the bullet and watch a couple of dogs, because how hard could it be, and live his stable life. Far cry from what it is now, because there was only so much he could pull from his savings before it got to a point.

“Thanks, but I’ll need something more.”

Cipher sighed. “Yeah, I figured.” Well this was a bust. He still owed her for taking the time, but the conversation only led him back to square one with no idea of where to go next. Life changing jobs don’t just appear out of thin air, whether he turns to his know-it-all friend or not. “Hey,” she continued, leaning forward on the table. “How about we do some manifesting?”

“Like a ritual?”

“Like a trip to the mall,” she said. “We buy you a fancy outfit with the intention of it being for an interview and bam. You’ll have one before you know it.”

Ideally, avoiding spending unnecessary money was his best course of action. Not to mention he had plenty of nice outfits. However, he was no stranger to his friend or her games. “You can want to go shopping without using my struggles as an excuse.”

“Must you suck the fun out of everything?” He rolled his eyes, taking a sip of his own drink before she continued. “Do you have anywhere to be after this?”

“Was that a joke?”

Cipher nodded slowly. “Right. No job. Sorry.”

She wasn’t sorry. Unfortunately she wasn’t wrong either. “No, I don’t have anywhere to be. I guess nothing says ‘financial crisis’ like going to the one place I shouldn’t.”

“See, you get it,” she teased, waving him off with a smile. “At least you’re making light of the situation. Speaking of light, will you be able to cover your electricity bill?”

Mydei wasn’t aware they reached the part where this was funny to her. “I hope you realize I’m jobless, not broke.”

“Yet.”

“Yet,” he quietly agreed underneath his breath, followed by a deep exhale. He wasn’t one for speaking things into existence, but Mydei hasn’t had a lot of things in his life to feel hopeful for to be familiar with the concept. “Hey. Cipher.”

“No,” she said abruptly, catching him off guard. He didn’t even ask anything. “I’m not going to tell Castorice about your situation.” He opened his mouth to speak, being cut off with a finger in his face. “Don’t start. I know you. Like I said, I’m not going to tell her, but if things start to get more serious, you can trust her too.”

He knew that. It wasn’t about trust. It was about spending years trying to prove that he could support himself just for it all to potentially blow up in his face.

‘Maybe if you just accepted your fathers money.’

What a joke.

“I know that.”

“Good,” Cipher nodded, sitting back in her seat. “Now hurry and drink that. I want to go shopping.” Straightforward and blunt, the reason Mydei went to her to begin with.

That didn’t stop him from shaking his head at her.

The second they stepped foot into the mall, Mydei should've known Cipher wouldn’t stick by his side. Luckily for him he wasn’t new to this, already aware that his main reason for being there was to carry her bags as they bounced between stores.

As he was currently doing right now, standing in the middle of a shoe store while his friend did her share of browsing. At this point, he was just walking aimlessly until he could finally be free of this.

His thoughts began to wander down the path of his predicament, unknowingly causing him to pace down an aisle while he tried to come up with a solution. That nagging voice kept buzzing in the back of his head, reminding him that he could fix all of this with one simple call. His problems would be nonexistent and money would be the least of his concerns.

He wasn’t going to do that.

Mydei didn’t spend the last few years ignoring his family’s money just to turn around and use it when it benefited him the most.

He wasn’t that far gone.

He was twenty-three. A grown adult who could figure this out, who had an entire degree backing him up. Even if the only job he’s ever seen himself progressing further in turned out to be total shit.

Again, not his fault.

He appreciated Cipher’s help earlier, he did, but a good job didn’t come overnight. No where seemed to be taking applicants either, so there wasn’t a lot he was left with. He knew what he wanted to do in life, very confident in his ability to do so, but he needed something to keep him grounded while he made it happen.

Mydei knew he couldn’t force it. A good career isn’t going to waltz into his life because he wants it to. No matter how much he would really like for that to be the case.

“Excuse me?”

A small, high pitched voice dragged him out of his thoughts. Turning around, his eyes landed on the child standing a few feet away from him.

Mydei looked around confused.

She didn’t appear wary of him, if anything she seemed rather composed. In a way that didn’t make him think she was lost, or any of the scenarios that would cause a random little girl to approach a stranger.

“Your hair,” she continued, pointing in his direction. His brows only pressed further together. “It’s pretty.”

The statement caught Mydei off guard, his eyes widening slightly. It wasn't often that he received compliments from children, and they had never been about his hair.

Well. He supposed it was rather sweet of her.

“Thank you,” he nodded, offering the hints of a smile so she understood that he took it well.

He fully expected for that to be it, because kids were random like that. They’d say what they needed to and leave. However, the girl remained where she stood. “Last time I asked daddy if I could dye my hair, he was so betrayed. I think it’s because he wants to match with me forever.”

That’s… okay, well Mydei didn’t know what to say to that. He began to find slight humor in it all, an amused huff falling from his lips before he shook his head. “Sounds like a buzzkill. Do you need help finding him?”

“Oh,” she shook her head. “I’m not lost. I walked away from him.”

Why would she do that? And why would he not keep a closer eye? “Well that’s not very safe.”

“But I’m safe right now?” Fair point. He was a little concerned about how fast she had come to that conclusion, though.

“He didn’t notice you leave?”

She shook her head again. “He was firing my old babysitter on the phone.” Mydei pursed his lips, attempting to hold back another laugh because what was it with kids and oversharing?

“I see why he needs a babysitter, then.”

“Can you?”

Confusion washed over Mydei’s features once more, causing him to address her with concern. What was she asking? Up until now, he was under the belief that she didn’t need help and was only wandering around because of defiance. “Can I what?”

“Can you be my new babysitter?”

His thoughts came to a halt.

Way too many years have passed for Mydei to vividly remember his childhood. However, he can confidently say that nothing has ever possessed him to approach someone with the intent of them being his caretaker. He liked to think the authority figures in his life would advise him to not even talk to strangers, so it was hard to hide his shock at the sudden question. What was he supposed to say? No?

She wasn’t going to start crying if he did, would she?

“Uh…”

By some miracle, he didn’t have to think about it for long.

A man in a suit suddenly emerged in the aisle they were standing in, rushing towards them once he noticed the little girl. The father, Mydei presumed. Thank the Titans, anything to avoid an awkward rejection at such a random request. He’d hate to crush her spirits after she just complimented his hair.

“Clara!” The man’s voice was far from angry, more so relieved as he finally stood beside her. “Why’d you run off like that?”

The girl, Clara, shrugged. “I was bored.”

The man tilted his head. “Now what if I left your tea parties every time I was bored?”

She lightly slapped his arm. “You say they’re fun all the time!”

“So you would obviously be hurt, right?”

Mydei, being the bystander he was, watched the scene in amusement. It was a shame Cipher was missing out, wherever in the store she might be.

“Whatever,” Clara said, crossing her arms. “I was over here talking to my new babysitter.”

The humor died in an instant.

Mydei’s eyes went wide again, especially now that the man’s gaze was set on him. It also gave the former a chance to really take in his appearance, realizing that he looked awfully young to be a dad. He was tall, probably slightly taller than Mydei, with an impressive build that showed he really took care of his body. However, the tussled white hair and soft features gave a sort of vibe that said he couldn’t have been older than thirty.

White hair.

‘I think it’s because he wants to match with me forever.’

That would make sense. They’re practically identical.

He had other things to worry about right now though, like the fact that Clara’s false accusation probably made him look suspicious.

Mydei didn’t agree to it. He didn’t even have a chance to answer her question before her father showed up.

It also didn’t help that said father was ridiculously attractive, looking at Mydei with anything but distaste in his eyes. Was it curiosity? Mydei didn’t know, but it wasn’t anger and he realized right away that this family was way too trusting.

Then again, it’s not like hedid anything.

“And who might this be?” The man finally asked. Clara didn’t say anything, which made sense seeing as she didn’t know his name. She had only talked about her life in those brief moments and asked him a question no child should ask a stranger.

“Not her babysitter,” Mydei was quick to say, jumping at the chance to assure the father that he was the innocent one in all of this. “Or… anyone’s babysitter.”

“Aw,” she pouted, though it didn’t appear as if she were genuinely upset by it. Meaning she wasn’t going to cry, and that was enough. This could end well and he’d finally leave to go find Cipher.

The man looked down at his daughter. “Did you ask him to be your babysitter?”

“Maybe,” she drawled. “You never let me choose.”

“Duh. Adult opinion, remember?”

She placed two hands on her hips. “Why don’t they stay then?”

What an interesting relationship.

“Because,” the man began, trailing off when he presumably came up blank. At least that’s how it looked to Mydei. He didn’t understand these two and highly doubted it was his place to try. “Guess you’re right then. Well,” he turned to address Mydei, which the latter inferred was to offer an apology for the suddenness of it all. “Feel like being a babysitter?”

Excuse him?

That was clearly not what he was supposed to ask. Mydei could’ve brushed the question off when it came from Clara, kids were impulsive like that. How could the father possibly say the same thing, seemingly trusting his young daughter’s judgment over the basic rules of human interaction.

“I… I’m already looking for another job.” You don’t even know me, rang in the back of his mind as well, but it probably wouldn’t hold much weight. Dysfunctional apple, dysfunctional tree.

“I can match it. The pay.”

Match it? Mydei didn’t even say there was anything specific, how could he match pay with a job that didn’t exist yet? That didn’t seem possible either, there’s no way a babysitting gig could hold a candle to what an actual job could do for him.

“I’m looking for something more official,” he said, not bothering to sugarcoat. It’s not like he owed it to the man.

“Five days a week,” the girl’s father countered. “For the entire summer. One million credits a month.”

Mydei’s eyes went wider than they had all day.

Holy shit.

“What?” He shot back, staring at the man in disbelief. “You can’t be serious.” Surely the man was joking. He was already full of surprises, something as small as this shouldn’t have stunned Mydei. Yet this wasn’t small at all, because one million a month seemed like way too much for a babysitter and Mydei really had to question what this man’s deal was.

Better yet, what was wrong with him.

He shook his head, an almost pleading look on his face. “You don’t understand, we’ve been looking for a solid sitter for weeks now. They never stay.”

For one million a month? They must have been crazier than the man himself. “You… you can’t just ask a random stranger to be a babysitter.” He could excuse it when it was a little girl asking. The father though? “You’re not setting a good example.”

“See! That responsible way of thinking is why I trust you. Clara does too, right?”

She nodded far too eagerly. “Mhm.”

That wasn’t the point. “So just like that. No interview, no questions. You jump to the conclusion that I’m best suited for your needs.” Mydei hoped he didn’t look like the insane one here. The whole conversation started to make his head hurt, maybe his best bet was to find Cipher and go.

“Are you a criminal?” The man asked.

Mydei scowled. “What? Of course not.”

“Have you ever babysat before?”

“Not really.” He might’ve helped Castorice watch her niece, but that didn’t count as any experience. He was just there.

“Can you drive?”

Why was he being questioned in the middle of a shoe store again? “Obviously.”

“Alright then. What’s your favorite fruit?”

His… okay, this was ridiculous. “What.”

Clara took the liberty in speaking up this time. “It’s a sensitive topic at home.” It caught Mydei off guard for the umpteenth time in that interaction. He didn’t even know she was old enough to understand what a sensitive topic was. Then again, it was about fruit so maybe staying away from the dysfunctional father-daughter duo would be wise.

Still, he sighed. “Pomegranates.”

“Hm,” Clara hummed, looking up at her father. Mydei paid that no mind, trying to decipher why the man was staring at him like that. Like Mydei was the perfect fit he was looking for, which is absurd because the former never prepared for this. He was pretty much forced into the hiring room.

Fortunately, the man seemed to gain what little senses Mydei hoped he had, addressing him seriously this time. Even if he still wore a soft smile, as well as that look on his face that showed zero social awareness.

“You can say no.”

Mydei knew that. That’s not what came out of his mouth, though. “Rubbing a price like that in front of my face kinda makes it hard to say no.”

“Okay good,” the father breathed out, as if Mydei’s hesitation was physically killing him. “It’s not everyday that she’s willingly vouching for someone to watch her. I decided maybe I should trust her judgement this time.”

She’s a child. “Hers?”

“Maybe mine too,” the man said, rubbing sheepishly at the back of his neck with a grin. Mydei would have found it to be an endearing sight if the reality of the situation didn’t hinder those thoughts.

“You don’t know me.”

“There’s a process for this. I usually take the people I hire out for lunch, get to know them a bit.”

Clara frowned, looking up at him once more. “No you don’t.”

“Hey,” the man gritted through his teeth, forcing a smile at his daughter. “Work with me here.” The little girl said nothing in return, giving a simple shrug before looking back at Mydei.

Great.

“I…” By this point, Mydei wasn’t even sure how to proceed himself. What was he supposed to do, turn down a deal like that? What would be a good reasoning? ‘Dysfunctional family’ wouldn’t cut it, he could already tell they’d be no problem. No matter how much they threw him for a loop. “I’ve never babysat before.”

Much less for five days a week, for the whole summer.

Definitely not for one million a month.

“My girl’s pretty low maintenance.” Mydei wanted to argue that any child who willingly ran off to question strangers might be the exact opposite, but he kept his mouth shut. “She’d be your new best friend. Monday through Friday. Nine to Five.”

Speaking of best friend...

Where the hell was Cipher?

“Work?” Mydei asked, hoping the father would understand what he meant. Luckily, he caught on right away.

“Yeah,” the man sighed, his demeanor changing entirely. The mention of work brought something new out of him, one that basically demonstrated why he was alright with asking a random man to step in and make his life a little easier. “It’s been rough. It doesn’t help that no one ever stays.”

Mydei remembered him mentioning that. Maybe he should be concerned. “How come?”

“Different reasons.” Wonderful, even better. Mydei braced himself for the worst. “Couldn’t commit to the time, couldn’t do simple favors. Some would ignore her, some would straight up be rude to her. I take my daughter very seriously.”

Doesn’t explain why she was able to escape his grasp earlier and walk up to Mydei. “So I’m a lifeline.”

“No!” The man assured, shaking his head. Mydei didn’t know where the eagerness came from, it's not like he was offended. Like he said, they didn’t know each other. “Of course not. I bet you're great! Clara probably thinks so too. She’s not really the trustworthy type either, so.”

Could’ve fooled him.

The more he stood there, the more he started to consider the possibility in front of him. It wasn’t exactly how he expected his next job offer to go, but it was Mydei that told himself he couldn’t force a career. That it should come naturally, and if this was the universe’s way of laughing at him and proving his point?

Then maybe he should swallow his pride.

“One million is a lot.”

The man smiled. “Money isn’t an issue.” He must’ve come across terrible contenders, then. Anyone with money like that could easily find a well enough babysitter. Or maybe not, according to the father. “Trust me, my money is where my mouth is.”

Exactly what Mydei needed.

He was prepared to give another hesitant answer when a voice sounded from behind him.

“I'm finished, Mydei. Time to bounce.”

What terrible timing she had.

He didn’t bother turning to face Cipher, giving her the chance to walk up beside him instead. There was no use in hiding this, he’d have to share the details with her eventually once he inevitably accepted the job.

“Mydei,” the man in front of him said, as if testing the waters. “That’s a nice name.”

“Pretty,” Clara added.

Mydei didn’t know how to respond to that.

“Whatchya doing?” Cipher asked, standing shoulder to shoulder with him. “Aw, who’s this cutie?” For his sake, Mydei really hoped she was referring to the child, not the father. The woman had no filter and he didn’t really want to think about how attractive said father was right now.

“Clara,” the little girl answered with confidence. “Mydei’s my new babysitter.”

Already somewhat used to their personality, Mydei wasn’t taken aback this time.

Cipher raised her brows. “Is he now?” He could feel her teasing eyes fall on him, her quiet way of saying ‘I told you so’ from their earlier conversation. Mydei still stood by his opinion, and she shouldn’t get him wrong. He wasn’t the one actively seeking out a spot in personal care services.

It just… walked up to him. In a shoe store.

“Guess so,” he breathed out, looking at the man. “Was hard to say no.”

The father simply smiled, a proud and cocky thing. “This is great! You just saved my life, Mydei.” Hearing his name roll off his tongue so easily had odd effects on Mydei, but he didn’t allow himself to think about that. Not when the man was kind — and persistent — enough to help him in his time of need. “Can I get your phone number? That way we can discuss when you’d start and everything else.”

“Like taking him to lunch?” Clara asked, poking at her father.

Her father spoke through his smile. "Adults are speaking.”

The little girl rolled her eyes.

Mydei looked down at the man’s phone he was offering. He assumed it wasn’t that crazy of a request, a rather plausible one if anything. He couldn’t start a job without knowing the basic requirements, not to mention Mydei would be watching this stranger’s daughter. Simple communication between the two of them was important.

He finally grabbed the device, slowly typing his number into the contact page. As he did so, the man continued. “My name is Phainon, by the way. Probably should’ve said that by now.

“Probably,” Mydei agreed, handing the phone back to him. He'd have to admit, it was nice to finally put a name to the face. A dangerous thing, too, considering both things were more than just nice in Mydei’s eyes.

“Well this is exciting!” Phainon exclaimed, clasping his hands together. Was it? Mydei wasn’t sure he got the memo. “I’ll text you later with details. Also, um…”

Mydei eyed him carefully. “What now?”

Phainon started rubbing the back of his neck again. “I was kind of serious about lunch, too.” Mydei didn’t miss the little girl trying to hold back a smile, all the while failing to do so. “I don’t normally! But you seem different and I wouldn’t want to jump into this. Plus, believe it or not, I’m a pretty protective dad.”

Pretty trusting one, too. “Alright.” A slight shift from his left reminded him that Cipher was still here and that he should probably cut his conversation short. Phainon already had his number, he doubted there was more to say. “I guess I’ll see you guys later.”

Phainon held his device up. “Wait by the phone for that text!”

Mydei was not going to do that. “Mhm.”

“See you later, Mydei!” Clara beamed, waving at him enthusiastically as he turned to walk off. The least he offered her was a smile and wave of his own.

Cipher didn’t say anything as they left, waiting to exit the aisle before she deemed the coast to be clear. Mydei internally counted in his head, knowing it was only a matter of time.

Like clockwork, the woman slapped his arm.

“Okay! I leave you alone for five minutes.” It was definitely more than five minutes. “You need to tell me everything.”

Sure. Maybe they could process it together. “In the car.”

That must’ve been enough for now. She didn’t press further, though she didn’t hide her amusement and Mydei immediately realized he was already regretting this.

Phainon stood frozen in place.

His god awful work day? He didn’t remember. His not so pleasant conversation he had with his old babysitter over the phone as he was firing her? He didn’t remember. As a matter of fact, he didn’t remember anything right now other than blonde hair and amber eyes that were unlike anything he’s ever seen before.

He expected the worst earlier when he turned to his side to notice his daughter’s absence. He had been scolding the previous babysitter for not being attentive when he realized he did the same, ending the call right away to go and find her. Phainon knew she was smart enough not to walk up to just anyone, but she was also his daughter and he knew she liked to make judgement calls on her behalf.

In hindsight, her judgement was incredible for a six year old.

While he wasn’t keen on her approaching a stranger, it was hard to be upset when even Phainon didn’t perceive the man as a threat. He didn’t perceive him in any kind of negative light, too busy wondering how this man could be real and how his daughter happened to stumble across him.

He was pretty much perfect.

It was easy to grow less weary the more the stranger talked. He kept a respectable distance, even scolded Phainon for being so trusting even if it meant diminishing his own character. It didn’t, of course. Phainon didn’t think there was anything about this man that would make him any less of a sight.

After that, the rest was history.

His mouth moved faster than his brain, and the next thing he knew he was throwing out a job for a lot more than he usually did. He wasn’t lying when he said money wasn’t an issue, his well paying corporate job was proof of that, but his usual deal was acceptable enough. However, with Mydei saying the offer was hard to refuse, Phainon regretted nothing.

Mydei.

Clara hadn’t been lying, the name really was pretty.

Speaking of Clara.

“Okay,” Phainon said, crouching down beside his daughter. “Team meeting.”

She fiddled with her hands. “Are you going to get mad at me over stranger-danger?”

“What?” Phainon asked in disbelief. “Are you kidding me? For that, I was going to see if you wanted ice cream for dinner.”

Her eyes lit up, her nervous demeanor dissipating in an instant. “Really? With extra sprinkles?”

“Oh we can get all the sprinkles you want, baby.” He took pride in the way she got excited, knowing it was well-deserved considering where her judgment had gotten them both. “But, yeah,” Phainon continued, more serious than before. He had to remind himself he was a father, after all. “You shouldn’t go up to strangers like that.”

Clara tilted her head. “I knew he was nice.”

Phainon cocked a brow. “Really? How come?”

“Because he looks like someone you would think is nice.”

He narrowed his eyes before smiling. He couldn’t exactly say she was wrong. “You’re pretty alright, boss.”

“Uh huh,” she nodded in agreement. “Can I still have ice cream for dinner?”

“No.” Clara crossed her arms, eyeing him with a challenging glare. “We are having ice cream for dinner. We can talk about your new babysitter.” Phainon didn’t think he ever wanted to stop talking about the new babysitter, but he wouldn’t admit that to his daughter.

His thoughts went back to their interaction, as well as the woman who joined once it was coming to its end. She seemed close to him, close enough to stand idly by without it being awkward. Girlfriend, maybe?

Phainon shook his head.

He couldn’t think like that.

He shouldn’t.

It was hard to find a committed babysitter that both he and his daughter approved of. A rather impossible feat, honestly. He wasn’t about to mess it up just because this stranger happened to be gorgeous, one of the most beautiful men Phainon has ever seen. He’d swallow all of that down if it meant finally being in a position where he didn’t have to worry about him or Clara.

For example, if his eyes accidentally lingered on the other man’s ass as he walked off?

That was just an accident.

Besides, it was never going to happen. Babysitting wasn’t the only thing people couldn’t commit to. He doubted anyone would be serious about Phainon if it meant being serious about his child too.

So professional thoughts from now on. He could admire from a distance, but as long as everyone was happy, so was he.

“Long story short, Mydei’s messing with a DILF.”

Titans strike him down now.

Castorice’s eyes went partially wide, turning to Mydei for confirmation.

After telling Cipher about the situation at the shoe store, the reality of it all started to settle with him. Meaning he had a job now and it wasn’t something he could keep from Castorice anymore. There was no reason to, because he had an answer to his problem and coming to her didn’t mean showing vulnerability.

He supposed he had Phainon to thank for that. However insane the man might be.

“I took a babysitting job,” was all Mydei could say in clarification. He couldn’t recall how many times Cipher had said the word ‘DILF’ in the past hour, glad she could find humor in a rather serious situation. “It was offered to me with good pay, I took it.”

“You took it, alright,” Cipher said, giving a teasing nod. “You took it hard from that DILF.”

This was ridiculous. “I doubt he’s even past thirty.”

She rolled her eyes. “Age doesn’t make the DILF.” For someone in the presence of her girlfriend, she was pretty confident in saying all of this. Maybe it was because it didn’t come from her own thoughts, and instead came purely from her desire to make Mydei’s life hell. “Looks do, and by the looks on him? I’d say you’re in deep shit, little prince.”

“I’m not thinking of my boss that way.” He refused to let one million a month go down the drain because he grew warm at the idea of Phainon being a DILF.

Cipher smirked. “Your boss, huh? Kinky.”

Castorice chimed in. “Are you sure it’s safe to just… take the job?”

Mydei didn’t see why not. He took both the father and daughter at face value, perceiving them as nothing short of dysfunctional. It was hard to feel threatened. “For one million a month, I could probably handle the worst.”

“Does that technically make you a sugar baby?”

“It quite literally does not.”

Castorice ignored them both. “Just be careful and know we're behind you no matter what.” It was nice to hear considering all he’s gotten were jokes regarding the matter. He was also glad Castorice wasn’t offended by not knowing his situation initially, basically telling him she understood why he never brought it up.

He wonders where he would be if he had.

Not under the promise of one million a month, that’s for sure.

He still couldn’t wrap his head around it.

He has other things to worry about right now, like the inevitable moment where Phainon finally texts him or how that lunch would go. The suggestion made sense, Mydei only hoped this was the man’s way of correctly going about the hiring process. It happened way too easy before.

Cipher shrugged. “I just think it’s funny how you weren’t interested in care services until now.”

He wasn’t. Probably still isn’t. “Back when it was ten thousand a week.”

“It’s not ten thousand a week and you know that.”

“It’s not one million a month either.”

Cipher let out a long sigh. “Whatever. Just say you want to be the proverbial sugar baby and quit beating around the bush, dude.”

Sometimes she really made no sense. “How am I a sugar baby if I’m getting paid for a service?” Considering the suggestive look that appeared on her face, he figured that was probably the worst way to word it. “Whatever. He can’t even be that much older than me.”

“My bets are on twenty-eight.”

Mydei deadpanned. “Five year difference. The horror.”

“Five year difference with a child included,” Cipher said. “Children age you. The man is practically forty now.”

“Are you done?”

She was wrong, anyway. The man didn’t allude to the personality of a forty year old at all. Even thirty was pushing it.

It wasn’t his problem to worry about Phainon’s age. His job was to take care of the man’s daughter while he was away at work, not focus on if he was old enough to be considered a sugar-daddy or a DILF. Though the second option…

No.

“It was just the father, right?” Castorice asked. Mydei furrowed his brows, unaware of what she was getting at. “No other parent with her?”

Cipher looked off to the side. “Shit, I didn’t even think about that.”

He didn’t even know why it mattered. “Just the father. I’m not going to pry either on why. If he tells me, he tells me.” As much as Mydei wanted to be curious as to why the mother wasn’t in the picture, it wasn’t his place to. Phainon would bring it up at lunch if it was important enough for him to know, because Mydei certainly wasn’t going to be the one asking.

Speaking of Phainon, the man picked the most convenient time to finally shoot him a message.

At least that’s what he assumed when he heard his phone go off. He ignored Cipher’s looks long enough to check.

XXX-496-XXXX: It’s Phainon!
XXX-496-XXXX: I was wondering when you’d be free for lunch :)

“What’s he saying?” Cipher questioned, sounding way too intrigued for Mydei’s liking. He said nothing, instead saving a contact for the man.

Mydei: i’m free saturday

Without a job, he was practically free anytime. He didn’t know if it was his own pride or Cipher’s teasing, but he wasn’t going to disclose that so willingly.

Phainon: Perfecft! Ambrosia’s at noon?

That was… a pretty nice place for somewhere as simple as lunch.

Phainon must’ve read his mind.

Phainon: Lunch is on me, like I said money is no problem

God, he really was starting to feel like a sugar baby.

Phainon: Clara’s coming too

However, that was precisely the reason why he wasn’t one. Mydei was here for her, not Phainon.

Mydei: sounds good. see you then

He received a thumbs up on his response, assuming that was the last of the conversation. Not that he was complaining, he wasn’t sure how long he could ignore that teasing glint in Cipher’s eyes.

He placed his phone down, unbothering to hide what had just happened. It would only bite him in the ass if he did. “We’re meeting for lunch on Saturday to go over work stuff.”

“Uh huh,” Cipher nodded. “Keep telling yourself that.”

“He’s bringing his daughter.”

“Mhm.”

Mydei shook his head. There was no reasoning with her.

Castorice turned to him. “Should we help you figure out something to wear?” Mydei sent her a look that said ‘not you too,’ one that she picked up on instantly. “It’s technically an interview, right? It’s not that I’m saying you should look nice for him, but making yourself look presentable is a good step.”

Mydei thought he always looked presentable. “I suppose.”

“She’s right,” Cipher agreed. “We need something that screams step-mother.”

Mydei inhaled deeply, closing his eyes.

Four outfit decisions later, Mydei realized that trying to look ‘presentable’ was ridiculous and he should just dress how he wants to dress.

He turned down the girl’s help with picking an outfit for him, fully aware that his experience with style didn’t call for it. That was until he stood in his closet, mulling over his best options while the distant thought of what would catch Phainon off guard the most sat in the back of his mind.

He wasn’t going to impress the man. He was there to properly complete the hiring process.

In the end, he decided on black slacks and a matching, tucked short sleeve dress shirt, opting for leaving the two buttons at the collar undone. Both articles of clothing hugged his frame perfectly, a seemingly fitting option for an unofficial job interview as well as a place like Ambrosia’s. There was no point in hiding his tattoos either, Phainon’s already seen enough and Mydei wouldn’t bother to cover them anyway.

He had a few minutes to kill before eventually heading out, purposely ignoring Cipher’s good luck texts knowing they weren’t genuine. She was just trying to tease him some more, and the last thing Mydei needed was to think about that before he could even have lunch with the man.

The drive to Ambrosia’s wasn’t all that bad. Traffic was usually worse around this time of day but thankfully the universe didn’t let it hinder him. Not that he thought Phainon would care, but he’d hate to be late. It would only make him look unreliable.

Mydei stepped inside the restaurant, looking around as he admired the place. He hadn’t been here much, his key memory being from the job offer they sent out to him years ago. He had gone with another restaurant instead, though he couldn’t help but wonder how different things would’ve been if he chose the former.

Maybe he’d be further into his career by now.

This felt like a slap in the face.

“Excuse me,” a young woman said, approaching Mydei with a smile. “Are you here with the Khaslana family?”

Was he?

“I’m…” He trailed off, following her line of sight to a booth that sat against the far side of the place. Sure enough, Phainon and Clara were occupying it, caught up in a conversation. “Yes. I am.”

“Perfect. Follow me.”

He did so, allowing her to lead the way as he got closer to the family. He barely made it to the table when they finally noticed his presence, both of their eyes lighting up in the process. Clara moved her hand in an excited motion, Mydei reciprocating the action with a small wave of his own. The hostess bid them a good meal as he sat across from the two, leaving them to their own devices.

“It’s good to see you again,” Phainon said, that same damn smile from before. Mydei could practically hear Cipher’s voice in his head.

“Told you I would be here, didn’t I?”

Phainon laughed. “You did. I ordered water for you but please get anything else you want.”

“Water’s fine, thanks.”

Mydei wasn’t sure if he imagined it or not, how aware he seemed to be of Phainon’s eyes landing on his unbuttoned collar. Was it too much? His collarbones were pretty much in view, but collarbones shouldn’t have been that much of a distraction.

Fortunately, those eyes averted.

“I like your tattoos,” Clara said, pointing to his forearm.

He gave a short nod. “Thank you.”

“Can I get tattoos?” She asked, turning towards her father.

“Sure,” Phainon shrugged. “If you let me wear that sweater of mine out in public.”

Clara groaned. “It’s so ugly, though! You need to throw it away.”

He shrugged. “This is a transactional relationship, boss. Give a little, get a little.”

Mydei was only half aware of this in the shoe store, but looking at it now? They had a pretty good relationship. At least from what he could see. He spoke to his daughter in a lighthearted manner, obviously making her feel comfortable enough for her to do so as well. It was clear Phainon was a good father.

‘Long story short, Mydei’s messing with a DILF.’

What?

He forced that thought away as quickly as it came, focusing on the two in front of him.

“So Mydei,” Phainon said, directing his attention to the blonde. “Tell us a little about yourself. Don’t hold back, either. The more the merrier. For interview purposes, of course.” That shit eating grin on his face told Mydei it wasn’t strictly for the job, more so for Phainon’s own curiosity.

Well, here goes.

“There’s… not much.” He thought about it, reminding himself that this was a professional lunch and the least he could do was try. “Okay. I’m twenty-three with a four year degree in culinary. I plan on owning a restaurant one day, I was working my way up at my last job but—” He stopped, briefly wondering if he was sharing too much.

Phainon gave him a curious look. “But what?”

Mydei sighed. “But they screwed me over.” He wanted to add the part where that’s why he needed a new job in the first place, but assumed it went without saying.

“Then they didn’t deserve you.” There were some days when Mydei didn’t think so either. He still was relatively content in the place though, not to mention it was a stepping stone for his career. “Besides, you’re too good to need their help. I bet you’re going to open your own restaurant one day.”

Mydei wanted to scoff in amusement. ‘Too good to need their help.’ Who was he kidding, Phainon didn’t even know him yet.

“That’s the plan.”

Clara perked up. “Will you let me and daddy visit?”

He failed to hold back a smile. “Yeah, you two can come anytime you like.” He brought his cup to his lips, preparing to take a sip.

Phainon smiled. “Better make it worth my while, then.”

Mydei choked.

Fortunately it wasn’t enough to send him in a coughing fit, but he did clear his throat in a desperate attempt to ground himself after hearing Phainon’s words. Why did he have to say it like that? And why couldn’t he get that stupid four letter word that Cipher kept nagging him with out of his brain.

“Are you okay?” Phainon asked, sitting up a little.

Mydei nodded, clearing his throat once more. “Fine. Went down the wrong way.”

The man laughed. “You scared me there for a minute! I’d hate to lose you before you can even work for me.” One, what a drama queen. It was water, it’s not like his entire throat was constricting on him. Two, going out like that might’ve been for the best. If that’s how he reacted over an innocent comment, maybe Cipher wasn’t all that wrong.

Mydei wasn’t blind. It was obvious Phainon was attractive. However, like he’s said numerous times, he was here for the child. He doubted the man even had time to incorporate someone in his life. Let alone a man, Phainon could’ve been straight for all Mydei knew.

“Hey Mydei,” Clara spoke, hopefully preparing to change the topic completely. “Does wanting to own a restaurant mean you know how to cook?”

“I would like to think so. Others do too.”

She sighed, almost in relief. “Thank goodness. Daddy can’t cook.”

“Hey!” Phainon whined. Grown ass man. Mydei wanted to snort.

Clara ignored him. “We have to go to Aglaea’s every time I want real food.”

Aglaea.

That was a new name.

“I see,” Mydei said slowly. “Well just tell me your favorite foods and I can try to make it happen.”

That was apparently the right thing to say seeing as the girl turned to her father with a smile. “He said he will cook for me. Please tell me we can keep him.”

Phainon chuckled softly before looking at Mydei, using his previous words against him. “That’s the plan.”

Titans, spare him.

The child. Not the father. That’s what he’s here for.

He awkwardly averted his gaze to Clara. “You’re pretty well-spoken, you know.” It was a genuine compliment, though it was only meant to change the conversation so that Mydei didn’t have to think about the other stuff. That stuff being Phainon’s dorky way of presenting himself, and how Mydei failed to be affected by it.

“Thank you,” she said, beaming with praise. “I get it from Aglaea.”

Phainon pouted. “Why do you hate me?”

Mydei’s mouth moved faster than his brain.

“Is that your mother?”

Phainon grimaced, answering for her. “Ew, no. God no. Aunt at most, and that’s more so towards me.”

Right. Mydei didn’t even know why he asked.

He decided he’d blame it on his conversation with Cipher and Castorice earlier, how it was getting to his head. Now since that question was answered, Mydei told himself that he wouldn’t concern himself about the mother any more.

Again, not his place.

“I don’t know my mom.”

It was almost worse than Mydei choking on his water. At least then the atmosphere didn’t grow completely awkward.

Clara’s words seemed to shut both him and Phainon up, though Mydei wondered how the other man felt about it. After all, it wasn’t his daughter that just openly admitted something like that. Mydei wasn’t sure how he was supposed to respond, was that a sensitive topic in their home as well? With how tense Phainon seemed, it clearly wasn’t something they joked about.

Eventually, Phainon forced out a laugh. “That’s… it was a mutual decision, really.” It was clear there was something he was holding in. Whether it was to spare his daughters feelings or to not overshare, Mydei wasn’t certain.

“It’s alright. You don’t have to explain anything.” In fact, Mydei felt guilty for even being curious over the topic to begin with.

“Did I ruin everything?” The little girl asked, sounding nervous.

Mydei gave an amused huff, shaking his head. “Of course not.”

That seemed to satisfy Phainon as well, if the smile on his face was any indication.

The lunch carried on fine after that, with the three of them getting to know each other better. It was mainly Phainon asking Mydei the questions, though there was the occasional moment where Clara would throw in a fact about them, Mydei making sure to take mental notes of everything. He was a good listener after all, and remembering this stuff would probably help him in the long run.

At least he hopes so. He’s never babysat before, so he’s not sure.

He clinged to the little he learned about Phainon as well. The man had his degree in aerospace engineering, catering to the business aspect of it all seeing as it kept him remote and close to Clara. It was a well paying job and considering Phainon’s position, it was safe to say he was good at what he did. That he spent his time climbing the ranks.

Mydei was almost envious.

Almost, because he knew who he was and had one hundred percent confidence in himself as always.

He also learned that not only was Phainon was in fact twenty-eight, his assumptions were right and Clara was six as well. He found out she was born in Phainon’s last year of university, though he was careful not to say anything else so Mydei didn’t pry. He simply did as he always would, listening and hanging on to whatever they said.

Professional reasons, of course. He’d be working for this man after all.

Which meant he’d do well to hang on to whatever Clara said too, whether it was her favorite color or what she had for dinner two nights ago.

It was ice cream, by the way.

Taking one look at Phainon, Mydei couldn’t say he was surprised.

Phainon hadn’t gone through a background check for Mydei, something the latter was willing to do — considering it was morally correct — but he didn’t bring it up. The man was putting his trust in Mydei, the least he could do was prove Phainon right and not give him a reason to question anything.

Their outing was coming to its close when the check hit the table, and Mydei watched as Phainon grabbed it with zero hesitation.

Surely he only offered to pay to get Mydei to come out. The blonde had no issue in settling his own bill this time.

“I can cover mine.”

Phainon shook his head. “I don’t mind. Today was nice, thank you.”

Why was he thanking him? Wasn’t this lunch related to Mydei’s upcoming job? A necessary process? “Sure. So I’ll start Monday?”

“Yes. Oh!” Phainon exclaimed, turning to his daughter. “Hand me your bag, I need to give Mydei the thing.” She nodded with wide eyes and a smile, supposedly knowing what he was getting at. Mydei watched as he dug in his daughter’s small purse before pulling out an envelope.

Then he held it out for Mydei.

Mydei eyed it suspiciously. “What is that?”

“Your first check,” Phainon said, like it was the most obvious thing in the world.

Clearly it wasn’t.

His ‘first check?’ The last Mydei remembered, Phainon’s original offer was one million a month and there was no way that's what the man was giving him. Not right now, not before Mydei could even finish a day of watching his daughter.

“I… what?”

“One million credits,” Clara added.

Like it didn’t phase either of them.

Mydei glanced around the restaurant before his eyes landed on Phainon again, halfway in a glare. The other half remained shocked. “Are you insane? Have you truly lost it?”

Phainon tilted his head with a smirk. “You know, Mydei, most people don’t ask that question when there’s money in front of their face.” Mydei wanted to argue that most people probably wouldn’t be in a situation like this to begin with, but maybe Phainon was too crazy to understand that.

“I haven’t even worked for you yet.” Phainon’s confidence in him was almost terrifying. What happened to this man’s survival instincts? “I could take this and never show up again.”

The man frowned. “Well don’t do that.”

“I’m not going to,” Mydei refuted, harsher than he intended on sounding. “If you’re doing this because you think I need it, keep it until the end of the month. Take the price down for all I care.” He didn’t mean to get so defensive. Phainon must’ve not expected it either considering the way he slightly recoiled at Mydei’s words.

Keyword ‘slightly,’ because it didn’t take long for that gentle smile to return.

“I’m giving you this because I’m serious about it, and I know you are too.” Being serious about things didn’t automatically put money in Mydei’s pockets, but he didn’t say that. “This isn’t some babysitting gig to me. You’re watching my daughter five days a week, you don’t realize what that does for me.”

He figured there was no point in trying to deny it any further. He was bound to get the money at some point. Even after a month passes, the idea of Phainon paying that much still wouldn’t make sense to him.

“Alright,” Mydei relented, slowly grabbing the envelope. At least he wouldn’t have to feel weird about it again for another thirty days.

“Thank you.” Once again, Mydei didn’t know what he was being thanked for. All he had done was take the money. “It was better if I gave it to you in advance. You already promised the boss you’d cook for her, and groceries aren’t cheap.”

Mydei glared. “I’m not broke.”

“I know you’re not,” Phainon nodded. “But you’re working for me. It’s my job to take care of you.”

Nikador strike him down.

“Mhm,” Mydei managed to get out, a rather unimpressed thing. A complete and total contrast from how strained it felt. “How kind of you. Truly a saint.”

Mydei was at least seventy percent sure he couldn’t look Cipher in the eyes after this.

Phainon chuckled. “What kind of man would I be if I didn’t?” An ideal man, in this scenario. Mydei wouldn’t have to force specific thoughts away if that would’ve been the case.

Once the bill was paid for, the three of them stood and said their respective goodbyes. Phainon was all too eager at the idea of seeing him again on Monday, which made no sense given he’d be working most of the day. The only time he would have to interact with Mydei is when he leaves and gets home.

Now that Mydei thought about it, that worked out in his favor quite a bit.

Mydei stared at the envelope in his hand as he left the restaurant and made his way to his car, hesitant to finally open it. He wasn't an idiot, Phainon was very willing towards this whole situation for Mydei to assume it wasn’t the money. Seeing it for the first time just made everything real, like it would be too good to be true and come crashing down at some point.

With firm hands, he opened the contents.

One million credits.

Why him, of all people.

Phainon really meant it when he promised to take care of Mydei, and the latter realized it was more of a dangerous thought than the man let on.

It wasn’t about the money, it was how he acted towards Mydei.

Mydei should’ve been put off by it.

There were times where his own daughter showed more maturity than Phainon himself, not to mention he was more like a puppy than a man. Pouting and arguing with a literal six year old. That alone should’ve been enough for Mydei to see how absurd all of this truly is.

Maybe he was a dog person after all. The universe loved to contradict him anyway, what was one more time?

He pulled out his phone with a grunt.

Mydei: think you might’ve been right
Mydei: enjoy it becausei’m not saying it again

The response came in an instant.

Cipher ^. .^: LMAOOO
Cipher ^. .^: about which one. sugar daddy or dilf
Cipher ^. .^: or both

Mydei grimaced to himself.

Mydei: not both.
Mydei: … the second one.

Definitely not the first. He was being paid for his service, because this was a job.

Cipher ^. .^: oh little prince
Cipher ^. .^: what to do what to do.

He sighed, setting his phone down.

What to do indeed.

Chapter End Notes

Yes Mydei that 28 year old man CAN be a dilf

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Denial and deflection, and all the other d words
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei can't ignore the issue if the issue is so blatantly making himself known.

Chapter Notes

I had like half of this written when I published chapter one but I also write really fast so... update time

Also if you guys are interested you can find me on Twitter. Let's yap

Mydei had a problem.

Two problems actually, if he wanted to get specific, but only one that mattered.

How the hell did one successfully babysit?

He wasn’t lying when he told Phainon he’s never done it before. Not in a situation where he was strictly the caretaker, so it’s not like he had prior experience to pull from. He had no siblings either, which probably would’ve benefitted him in more ways than one if he did. At least maybe his father wouldn’t have expected so much from him.

But this wasn't about that right now.

It was about the fact that he didn’t know what to do.

Cipher liked to joke around and say he didn’t have the most outgoing personality, that he resembled a very feisty kitty at times. It clearly didn’t bother him, he was who he was and wouldn’t change himself just to cater to anyone else. Besides, at least he had Castorice in the other ear saying he was a big softie at heart.

The only problem was that this wasn’t an adult he was dealing with. It was a child.

Fortunately Clara wasn’t like any child. She had enough emotional maturity to poke fun at her father, which would no doubt earn a pout in response and Mydei swore the man was too old to be doing all of that. Whether he found it endearing or not wasn’t up for debate at the moment. What was debatable, however, was whether his personality would be too much for Clara herself.

Then again, she never was put off when Mydei would do his fair share of poking fun at Phainon. In fact, she would smile, clearly finding humor in it. If Phainon got offended enough from said joke, she might even laugh.

That has to mean something.

“You sound like you’re thinking hard over there.”

Mydei rolled his eyes, hands firm as he turned the wheel. “Shut up. I’m just looking at the directions.”

“Oh,” Cipher said through the speakers, dragging the word out. “Well if you ask me, it sounded like you were fantasizing what position he’d put you in first.”

“That’s why I didn’t ask you.”

The woman sucked her teeth. “It’s okay, little prince. I understand the kind of pressure you might be under right now.” She actually didn’t, seeing as his worries were revolving more so around Clara than her father. It wasn’t Phainon he was spending the entire day with. “He may have his DILF degree, but I’m sure you can handle it.”

Mydei smirked. “Actually, he has an aerospace engineering degree.”

“Uh, yeah. Whatever that means.”

She never failed to impress him. Contrary to how it sounded, Mydei wasn’t sure if that was a good thing. “Look. Just because I agreed that… that’s he’s…”

“A DILF?” She interjected, finishing the thought he had trailed off on. “It’s not a bad word, Mydei. You can say it.”

“Please quit talking.” He knew he could say it. He also knew that he didn’t want to say it, because saying it invoked images he’d rather not see appear in his mind right now. And mentioning positions Phainon would have him in too? What was wrong with her? “Anyway, it’s not important. I think I need to focus on his kid liking me.”

Cipher gasped. “You’re right! That way you can get in close with her and start asking sneaky questions about her father. Smart choice, little prince.”

“That’s not—” Mydei then cut himself off, lowering his voice because this was not the time to play into her nonsense. “I’m not doing that. At all.”

“Why, because you know it might work?” She was awfully confident in a kid she didn’t even know. “Kids are an open book with this kind of stuff. No filter at all.”

Then again, she had a point. Clara loved to share random things about her and Phainon, so it wasn’t outside the realm of possibility. That still didn’t mean Mydei was going to consider it, because maintaining a good relationship with her is what got him paid. Not finding out things he shouldn't even care for.

“You’re insane.”

“Probably. You know, I never envisioned you to be the stepmom type.”

Mydei glanced over at the directions. Five more minutes. Perfect. The sooner he got there, the sooner he could get out of this conversation where clearly nothing coming from his mouth was being heard. “I would say go bother Castorice, but I wouldn’t subject her to that.”

“It’s fine,” another voice added, exasperation in her tone. “I’d say I’m used to it.”

He froze.

When the hell did Castorice get there?

Mydei’s brows pressed together. “Cipher. Were we in a three-way this whole time?”

“Maybe?” She truly had nothing but the nerve. Mydei was glad they could find entertainment in this, over something that will never happen. “You may call it a three-way, but I call it being inclusive. I can't be the only one sending you off on your big day.”

Great, now she was mocking him. ‘Inclusiveness’ his ass, that still didn’t take away from the fact that it was a three-way and Mydei realized he didn’t have to wait five minutes at all. All he needed was the extra push to finally end the call. “I’m hanging up now. Goodbye.”

“Wait, Mydei—”

Whatever Cipher was going to say next, he would never know. Castorice would have to just not take it personal.

He tried to brush off the conversation for now, focusing on the issue at hand as he got closer to Phainon’s place. He had no idea what to expect as far as the house itself goes, Phainon had no issue waving a shitload of money in his face so surely the home would match the attitude.

At the same time, Phainon didn’t seem like the pretentious type at all. He only assured Mydei that money wasn’t an issue, never once did he try to uplift his character with it.

As far as Mydei knew, he was simply a down to earth kind of man. Who just so happens to be a D–

Determined guy. Different kind of guy. No other ‘D’ word, of course.

Who was Mydei kidding. Metaphorically, he was fucked.

Definitely not literally.

He arrived at Phainon’s place sooner than he thought, blaming that all too familiar path his brain seemed to go down for making the time fly by. Granted it was only three minutes, give or take, but they could’ve been spent coming up with a gameplan for the day. Not denying an obvious attraction for an intangible man.

No more unrelated thoughts. This was strictly business.

Fortunately he didn’t have to think about that any longer, too busy realizing how utterly wrong he had been. The house was nice, don’t get him wrong. Mydei wasn’t that picky to where he’d judge that kind of thing anyway.

It’s just the fact that it was… a pretty average house.

Not unnecessarily large, not perfectly sculpted with the finest bricks and stone. A simple, white-paneled home – one story, might he add – that almost resembled something that would be found on a ranch.

So that was Phainon’s style.

Mydei couldn’t say he saw that coming.

With one final glance at the place, he left his car and made his way to the porch, preparing to knock before he could talk himself out of the whole thing period. It was new territory, but Mydei was not a goddamn quitter. Screw all of the other stuff.

He was going to be the best babysitter that girl has ever seen.

The door swung open before Mydei even had the chance to knock, revealing a far too eager Phainon standing on the other side. Was he waiting for him? It’s not like he was running late.

“Mydei! You made it.”

Mydei huffed, walking past the threshold once Phainon stepped aside for him. “I told you Saturday. I’m not going to leave with your money.”

The interior of the house gave the same vibe as the outside, a country style theme that Mydei couldn’t imagine would represent the man. The slight untidiness that came with it, maybe, but Phainon also had a kid and a full time job so Mydei didn’t think too hard about that part.

“I would probably let you,” Phainon said, closing the door.

Mydei scowled, shaking his head in disapproval. That would actually make him a sugar baby. “What is wrong with you?”

“Clara says there’s a lot.”

Of course she did. Good to know that kid had some sense of awareness, even if her approaching a stranger could contradict that. “Well she would be right.”

Speaking of Clara, Mydei could hear quick footsteps padding through the hallway, cutting off whatever either of them could’ve said next. In a matter of seconds, the girl was approaching them at full speed, beaming when she saw Mydei.

“You’re here! You didn’t take daddy’s money and leave!”

As heartwarming as her enthusiasm was, he looked at Phainon in question. “Is that a common thing or something?”

“No,” the girl answered for her father. “But he kept freaking out and thought you would leave with his money. I’m the one who had to tell him that you wouldn’t do that.”

Mydei was glad she had that much confidence in him. He gave her a quick smile before shooting Phainon another glance, parroting his words from earlier. “‘I would probably let you.’”

“I would!” Phainon defended. “It would suck, yeah, but I would have actually been honored.” Mydei nodded slowly, not buying it. “How about we talk about the fact that you’re actually here? Did we leave that much of an impression on you?”

Too much of an impression, if he really thought about it. One that inserted unwelcome thoughts in his head. He wouldn’t say that, of course. “Clara did. I’m still deciding with you.”

Phainon’s jaw dropped, feigning hurt as if that was supposed to make Mydei change his mind. How ridiculous. Getting so worked up over this man who was more sensitive than his six year old daughter.

Clara walked up to Mydei and grabbed his arm. “I’m so happy you’re finally here. Can I show you my room? I spent all morning cleaning.”

Phainon, to no one’s surprise, looked offended. “What? I’ve been trying to get you to clean your room for weeks.”

Her head shot back, giving him a pointed glare. “You’re embarrassing me.”

Mydei did his best to hold his laugh.

“Yeah, yeah,” Phainon said, waving her off. “Let me give Mydei the rundown before you go off and forget I ever existed. Since I mean that little to you.” How dramatic. Clara nodded nonetheless, scurrying off to the couch to give the adults some space. Phainon’s eyes found Mydei immediately. “Ready for this?”

Mydei smirked. “To forget you ever existed? Or to watch her?”

“Preferrably the second option. Please.”

“Too late.”

It was Phainon’s turn to send him a cocky grin. “Forget me? Like you’d ever.” Unfortunately, he might be right. “But seriously, help yourself to anything. I mean anything. You’re doing me a big favor, the least I could do is offer up my house.”

“You sure do love offering things.”

“I’d offer anything to you.” Mydei’s eyes went wide, brain scrambling for barely a second because whywould he say it like that? “I mean, since you’re doing this for me,” Phainon continued, laughing sheepishly. “You’re my superhero, so. Yeah. Help yourself to anything.”

Right, right.

“Okay then.”

Phainon gave a firm nod, averting his gaze as quickly as possible. Weird. “You have my contact information if anything goes wrong, but if I don’t answer, I left Aglaea’s and my sister’s number on the counter. My sister is about two hours away, but she will rush down here in a heartbeat.”

Mydei felt awkward even at the idea of talking to Phainon’s sister. He wasn’t sure why. “Got it.”

“But that should be it. Like I said, please make yourself at home. I want you to feel welcomed here, because you are.” Flatterer. He pretty much already said that. Mydei didn’t say anything in response, letting his slight hums of confirmation do the talking. Phainon should know enough about him to not expect more. “Alright, am I missing anything?”

Clara shot up from the couch. “Wait! You didn’t show him the surprise we got for him!”

Mydei cocked a brow. “I get a surprise?”

“That’s right,” Phainon whispered, more so to himself. “Come here.”

Mydei followed them into the kitchen, unaware of what might be waiting for him. Mydei didn’t think there was something he could have said to ensure a surprise, unless Phainon jumped the gun again and handed him another envelope full of money.

One he would refuse to accept right now, thank you.

Much to his surprise, it wasn’t another early payment.

Clara extended her arms out, presenting his ‘surprise.’ “Tada!”

Mydei blinked. “You got me pomegranates.”

An entire bowl of them.

“Mhm,” Clara nodded proudly. “It was my idea, but daddy was the one who stood there for an hour to make sure he got ripe ones.”

Mydei turned his head towards Phainon slowly, looking at the man in what could’ve been horror. It might as well be, considering no one in their right mind does something like that. Especially for someone they have had two interactions with.

Phainon’s eyes went wide. “Okay, it was not an hour. Thirty minutes tops. You know kids and their terrible perception of time.”

Mydei honestly didn’t know who believed more. Considering the man could be pretty irrational, his money was probably on Clara.

What an insane thing to do.

Then again, no one has done that for him. Ever. Cipher and Castorice didn’t eat pomegranates, so they would argue that ripeness didn’t matter. For all he knew, Phainon didn’t much care for them either. Still, Mydei couldn’t help but picture him standing in the produce section, brows pressed together as he picked the perfect fruit for Mydei.

Inspecting it closely.

Turning and tossing it around.

Making sure it was ready to be eaten.

That… was kind of hot.

No. It literally wasn’t. It was fruit for crying out loud.

“Please tell me I had good judgement.”

Phainon’s voice snapped him out of those terrible thoughts, causing Mydei to deflect on the situation entirely. No one but him had to know. “Considering how poor your judgement can be, I should probably check.”

From a distance, the fruit looked fine. He just needed to do something other than think.

He picked up a pomegranate, pretending to examine it before gently placing it back in the bowl. “It’ll do.”

Phainon sighed. “I knew there were better options.” On the contrary, Phainon made perfect choices. Mydei just wasn’t willing to admit that out loud. “I’ll get better ones next time. I promise. Or maybe you’ll just have to go to the store with me. So I can see how you do it.” Mydei narrowed his eyes. Clara did the same. “No? Terrible idea? I should shut up forever?”

Clara rolled her eyes. “You’re going to be late for work.”

That’s right. Why was Phainon still here? Who cares if it was his house, Mydei needed a second to himself.

“Fine, fine. I’ll leave now.” Mydei watched as Phainon squatted down to Clara’s level, addressing her with softness this time. “You’ll behave for Mydei, right? You’ll listen to him and be respectful?”

Fuck. Mydei was so, so screwed.

“I will,” she said with a nod. “I swear.”

Mydei then watched as they did a quick handshake, something that must’ve been pre-established but all he could think about was how dizzy he got over seeing Phainon in father mode. It was bad enough that he was losing it over pomegranates, but this definitely wasn’t any better. He needed Phainon to get to work immediately.

What was wrong with him.

Phainon said one last goodbye to them before heading out, though not without another reassurance that Mydei can reach out any time and he should make himself comfortable. The latter didn’t bother holding back the amused eye roll.

Mydei took a seat on the couch, followed by Clara who sat right beside him. He was touched by how quickly she warmed up to him, so he figured the least he could do was stay on her good side. It would do him well seeing as he’d be spending the most time with her throughout the week.

Starting with one thing they both had in common?

Easy.

“So,” Mydei began, the corner of his lips tugging upwards. “Did he really spend an hour in the store over pomegranates?”

The little girl groaned. “Yes. I think he was trying to one up my surprise. Now look at him, he didn’t even get them ripe!”

Mydei laughed. “He did. I just said that so he wouldn’t get a big head. Don’t tell him though.”

She held her pinky finger out. “I won’t. Promise.”

Okay. So this is what he was doing now.

Oh, what the hell. A pinky promise was nothing.

With a smile, he locked their pinkies together, giving a quick shake.

“That haikas. Can’t believe he’d do something so foolish.”

Clara tilted her head at him. “Hikes? What’s that word mean?”

“Haikas,” he corrected. It wasn’t a bad word, and she was bound to hear it someday. It was only a matter of time before Phainon did something to earn the name. “It means scoundrel in my native language. It can also mean hyena.”

She giggled. “I like it.”

This was good. There was no reason he should have overthought this. Clara didn’t gravitate towards him because of some faux exterior he put up, playing the role of an overbearing babysitter. She liked him because he jokingly insulted her father while simultaneously making her laugh. He was simply just being himself.

“Since I’m new to this, how about you decide how we spend today?”

Because as good as they could get along, eight hours was still a long time and they couldn’t just sit around for the entirety of it.

She hummed, tapping a finger to her chin. “Can we go to the park?”

Not too bad, Mydei could do that. Still– “is that something your father is usually okay with?”

Titans. Even referring to Phainon as a father made him feel things.

A smile slowly formed on her face. “You really are a good babysitter.”

“What makes you say that?”

Clara shrugged. “Because they never ask that. They just say yes because it means they don’t have to talk to me for a few hours.” Is that seriously what these two have been dealing with? Mydei doesn’t have any experience to declare himself the best babysitter, but he’d never take a child somewhere if it meant getting away from them.

“That’s… a terrible thing to do.”

She didn’t seem bothered by it. If anything, she looked like it was something she was used to and that didn’t sit right with Mydei. “They just want daddy’s money. They were never really there for me.” He couldn’t help but frown, and she noticed right away. “It’s okay. That’s why daddy fires them.”

So Phainon meant it when he said he was protective over his daughter. That counted for complete negligence too.

Maybe his judgment wasn’t so bad.

“How about this,” Mydei said, sitting up straight. “We get milkshakes and then go to the park. That way if enough time passes, we can feed the ducks.”

The idea must’ve been a good one with how quick she was to gasp. “Yes, yes, yes. Can you make something tasty for dinner too?”

Right, Mydei almost forgot they had talked about this before. “Of course. How about I make a gnocchi skillet?”

She tilted her head again, furrowing her brows. “A know what now?” Mydei snorted, though she continued before he could clarify. “Will it make me big and muscular like you?”

“Well that depends. Do you want to be big and muscular like me?”

She gave him an incredulous look. “Duh. I want to be just like you.”

Mydei smiled. “Then yes.”

“Okay!” She exclaimed, standing from the couch immediately. “I’ll go get my shoes then.”

He was ready to give the okay when he glanced around the room again, taking in the state once more. He knew it wasn’t his place, but the area wasn’t that messy and with how little time Phainon seemed to have, it shouldn’t do any harm. If anything, he was just doing another favor for him.

“Wait.” Clara stopped, turning around. “Before we do any of that, how about we do something for Phainon.”

She crossed her arms, eyeing him suspiciously. “I’m listening.”

“Let’s tidy the living room up a little.” He then realized that kids didn’t really cater to the idea of doing any kind of cleaning, the look on her face saying it all. She probably already did as much as she wanted to with her room. “We’ll make it a competition. Whoever does the best gets the bigger milkshake.”

Just like that, her distaste seemed to disappear. He laughed as she hurriedly began picking up items before joining her.

And if Mydei purposely did a mediocre job so she could achieve that victory? She didn’t have to know.

“You’re freakishly in a good mood.”

The comment didn’t put Phainon off. Instead, his grin might have gotten wider. “Can’t a man feel good?”

“I guess,” Hyacine said slowly, as if she were unsure of that herself. “Usually you’re complaining about higher ups or, quote unquote, unreliable partners. I was just surprised, that’s all.”

She wasn’t wrong. By lunch, Phainon would have plenty to say about the people he worked with. They leave him with no choice, honestly! It’s not like he could actively speak his mind at work. It just piled until he could finally get away, and he’d feel bad about complaining to Hyacine if it actually bothered her. From what he knew, his work nonsense was practically gossip for her.

Today, however, Phainon didn’t even think his coworkers' incompetence could get him down.

“It’s been a good morning.” He began to take a bite of his sandwich.

“Mhm. Did you get laid?”

He froze, mid bite.

“What?” He asked, coming out slightly muffled.

‘I wish’ was what he really wanted to say. With the blonde haired beauty waiting for him at home, how could he not? Unfortunately, Mydei wasn’t waiting for him at all. He was there for Clara, Phainon was just the one left out in all of this.

So, naturally, he couldn’t say that.

Hyacine shrugged. “I’m just saying. You’re usually never this giddy and you usually never get laid. I thought maybe that couldn’t be a coincidence.”

He dropped his sandwich on his plate. “Hey! I—” Who was he kidding, he didn’t get laid. Phainon’s been abstinent for the past six years, because he knew someone wouldn’t want him as a packaged deal. He didn’t care much for casual hookups either. “Whatever.”

Besides, until now, there’s never been anyone to have him even consider being interested.

What a dangerous thought.

“Thought so.”

He shook his head. “I didn’t get laid.”

She narrowed her eyes. “So you just feel good.”

“Yep.”

“No reason why.”

“Uh huh. Spending time with my best friend, why wouldn’t I?”

It wasn’t completely a lie. He was grateful that they could manage to make time for lunch two days out of the week. They had conflicting schedules, but they had always been close so Phainon looked forward to Monday’s and Thursday’s. At the very least, today it meant more since he could enjoy the afternoon knowing his daughter was in capable hands.

Gorgeous, flawless, capable hands.

Despite his chipper tone and expression, Hyacine didn’t buy it. “Whatever you say. How’s Clara? Has she warmed up to Sylvia any?”

For a brief moment, Phainon almost forgot that he’s had babysitters before Mydei. Countless of them. It was kind of easy when none of them have ever made Phainon grow speechless at the initial sight of them. “So about that.”

“Phainon.”

“I fired her last Thursday.”

“Phainon.”

In his defense, he had good reasoning. He always did, because he takes his daughter very seriously and all he needs is one complaint from her for Phainon to let them go. She may be spoiled in that department, but at least he’s trying to make her happy. “It was Clara’s call.”

Hyacine frowned. “That’s the third one this summer.” He knew that. If he’s lucky, he won’t ever have to see the fifth one. “Well whoever it is now, I at least hope you reviewed their application thoroughly.”

Phainon braced himself. “So don’t get mad.”

“Titans, what now.”

The best he could offer was a weak smile. “This one didn’t really apply apply.”

“And what does that mean?”

First of all, it meant his daughter came across the find of a lifetime and he felt like he owed her one forever. He wasn’t sure Hyacine would understand that much right away, so the least he could start with were the basics. It wasn’t that crazy of a story. “Well, I came across him in the mall.”

“You—” She cut herself off, blinking rapidly at him as if she couldn’t process his words. “Like, on a babysitting ad?”

“Like in a shoe store.” She pinched the bridge of her nose instantly and he quickly jumped to defend himself. “Okay, look! Clara found him, and Clara doesn’t talk to most people! You know how she is. If she hasn’t warmed up to any of those babysitters, who proved to be a waste of time in the end, surely her perception skills aren’t that bad.”

Hyacine sighed. “She’s six.”

“And smart as hell.”

She shook her head. “I can’t even blame her for this. You’re the one who hired some random guy to watch your kid.”

Yes, it sounds bad in theory, but Hyacine wasn’t there! She didn’t see Mydei practically scold him for not following basic social etiquette by offering a total stranger a job. If anything, Mydei was the one weary of him. “Mydei is not just some random guy. He’s… how do I put this? He’s pretty much perfect.”

Hyacine deadpanned. “Oh, goodie. He has a name. I wouldn’t put it past you to completely forget that part after letting the stranger into your home.”

“You’re not seeing the bigger picture.”
