“Oh I’m seeing it alright.” Phainon didn’t think she would be able to see it unless she could realize how gorgeous Mydei truly was. How behind that rough exterior, he was a man who probably wouldn’t hurt a fly. “You better be glad I somewhat trust that kid’s judgment. Way more than yours.”

That was good enough for now. “Thank you.”

“Don’t thank me yet,” she said, voice stern. “I want a review next week. If this one even lasts that long.”

Phainon looked off to the side. That was a fair point, actually. He wondered how long Mydei could last.

Wait, no.

Phainon swallowed. “Sure. I’ll give you weekly reports, actually.”

She gave a dry smile. “I’m good, thanks. Anyway, it’s clear now that there’s a reason behind that cheerful mood of yours. Didn’t know it took a little bit of irresponsibility and irrational decisions but at least it’s something.”

Mydei was definitely something. Something so new that even thinking about him like this could potentially ruin everything, but Phainon’s never dealt with this before. Everyone before Mydei had always been the same. People who put up a front to ensure their checks and earn a spot in Phainon’s home.

Mydei wasn’t like that. Mydei was down to earth, he called everything like he saw it. He didn’t pretend to be something else.

Phainon’s never wanted something so bad before.

However, he knew what he needed. It was for Clara to finally have a babysitter she could warm up to, because her happiness meant more than his own. That was why he’d swallow whatever urges he felt towards Mydei.

Not a task for the weak, that’s for sure.

And Phainon was a weak, weak man.

“It’s not like that,” he assured, because it wasn’t. “He’s… I don’t know how to explain it.”

“Try,” she said. “Give me something about him. Older or younger than you?”

“Younger. Five years.” Another reason he couldn’t pile this into Mydei’s life. He was around the same age Phainon had been when Clara was born, which wasn’t planned. He wouldn’t trade it for the world, but no one really expects something like that before they have a chance to live their life. It wouldn’t be fair to Mydei to pursue anything while he was aware of that.

She nodded slowly. “Nice?”

Phainon huffed in amusement. “It’s complicated.”

“How? He’s either nice or not.”

Or the weird middle ground that Mydei stood in. Whatever it was called. “He’s direct, but rational. He seems like the type to be a softie at heart, though.” He’s always addressed Clara respectfully too. He’s never once demeaned her or made her feel unnoticed. A far cry from the others.

“And you’re sure Clara likes him?”

It was the one thing Phainon could be sure about. “Absolutely.”

“Okay then.” She still sounded skeptical, though thankfully she didn’t press any further. As long as she trusted him for now, he could very well prove the judgment of a six year old wasn’t that questionable after all. “I still expect that report next week.”

“Yep. Anything else?”

“Yes.” Phainon said nothing, his silence prompting her to continue. “Are you interested in him?” His eyes went wide, feeling put on the spot by the sudden question. “You said it wasn’t like that and I would assume not since you just met him, but is there something more?”

Phainon wishes.

He would jump at the chance to say so too, because his attraction for the man wasn’t something he’d hide, but it was more complicated than that. He knew how it could look, he was paying Mydei to watch his daughter. In a way, that almost made Phainon his boss.

“I… don’t know.”

Hyacine tilted her head. “I’m not going to judge if you say yes.”

“You’re not?” It was surprising, because honestly Phainon had been hoping that maybe she would set him straight. At least he wouldn’t have to go through mental turmoil about it.

Correction, he would try not to go through mental turmoil.

“No,” she shook her head. “I’m mainly just looking out for you. Say this Mydei feels the same. He can be her babysitter and he can be with you, but those lines might start to cross and Clara could get the wrong idea. I… just don’t know if he can be both without it affecting someone.”

She was right. Being Clara’s caretaker in the babysitting sense was different from being her caretaker because he was a part of Phainon’s life too. The two of them being involved might make that happen, and Phainon couldn’t put that responsibly on Mydei. It wasn’t fair.

“I know.”

“But Phainon?” Hyacine asked, offering a gentle smile. “I don’t know him. I can’t speak for him, this is purely just me being your friend.”

Phainon knew that too. That was why it was better for him not to acknowledge it completely.

“So what I’m hearing is you want to meet him?”

“You—” She stopped, sighing at Phainon’s devious smirk. “Whatever. Sure. If the opportunity presents itself, I’ll meet him.” All he had to do was make the opportunity present itself and he might get her seal of approval from more than just a report.

Mydei stood in front of the stove, feeling less out of place than he did twenty minutes ago.

It couldn’t be helped at first, he was cooking in a kitchen he wasn’t familiar with for people he wasn’t entirely familiar with. Then again, he’s done it for years at the restaurant so he quickly reminded himself that this was nothing. Once he got in the swing of things, it was easy to remember why he wanted to do this for so long.

He just simply enjoyed it.

Whether it was the process or the idea of people appreciating his food, he wasn’t sure which he liked better, but both motivated him. It was something a perfectionist like him could be precise about, but he also loved knowing that the results would always end up pleasing whoever he served.

He hoped the case was the same this time around.

Kids could be picky eaters, so appealing to Clara might be the hard part. He’d try to leave before Phainon had the chance to dig in, so he didn’t worry too much about what the other man would think.

A small part of him did want Phainon to be impressed, though.

A minuscule part of him wanted Phainon to praise his food.

Whatever that could mean.

He hummed quietly to himself as he continued to cook, only doing so seeing as the kitchen was empty. Clara had told him she had things to ‘take care’ of in her room, and he said he’d get her when it was time for her to eat.

If Mydei thought the kid had warmed up to him before, today might have solidified it. It was presumptuous to say it after day one, yet he couldn’t pinpoint a moment where she looked like she wasn’t enjoying herself. She was an open book all day, from the pond where they fed the ducks to the grocery store where Mydei bought his ingredients. Nothing seemed to dampen her spirits, so he must have been doing something right.

If things stayed exactly as they were, this might not be a bad job after all.

The sound of the front door closing in the distance caused him to glance at the clock, confirming that it would be likely for Phainon to be home now. Mydei would have preferred to get the extra food packed before the man arrived, but Phainon was the one who said he could use the kitchen.

So what if he found Mydei doing exactly that?

It took a while for Mydei to finally hear footsteps approaching, immediately realizing what could have caused the delay.

He and Clara cleaned today.

That wasn’t too much, was it?

He didn’t have much time to ponder over it when he finally heard Phainon walk into the kitchen, ignoring that small worry long enough to glance back. Just in acknowledgment, not to actually get a good read at Phainon’s face.

“Hey, just making dinner. For Clara.”

Phainon said nothing.

Okay then.

“There will be plenty leftover,” he continued, tending to the pan in front of him. “I’ll leave it here with you.”

Still nothing.

So the man who somehow always had something to say suddenly couldn’t speak? Mydei finally turned around this time, allowing himself to see the kind of expression on Phainon's face.

He wasn’t expecting him to be utterly dumbfounded.

“Earth to Phainon.”

Phainon didn’t move, seemingly frozen in place. “You’re cooking.”

Mydei scoffed. “Good job, genius. You have eyes. You have ears too and I know they work, so I’ll assume you heard what I said before.”

Phainon finally smiled at that, even if it was faint.

He was so weird.

“No one ever… I’ve never…”

Shaking his head, Mydei directed his attention back to the food. “What, none of the other babysitters have offered you the leftovers before?” A good chef always made enough for leftovers. Mydei was rather confident in his abilities, so why wouldn’t he give people the chance to go back for more?

“No other babysitters have cooked for us before.”

Oh.

Mydei didn’t turn around this time, though he did press his brows together. “None? You’re kidding.”

“I’m not. They’ve never gone through the effort.”

‘Effort.’ Who exactly was he dealing with before? “Making sure people eat is hardly an effort.”

The sound of keys hitting the floor made him jump.

His head shot back, eyes falling on Phainon once more. The man didn’t even make a move to pick them up, just staring at Mydei like he was speaking a language he didn’t understand. Was work that bad? Was his brain fried to the point where he couldn’t form a coherent sentence or thought?

“What is wrong with you.”

“A lot,” Clara answered for him, joining them into the kitchen. “Daddy, why are your keys on the floor?”

Her presence seemed to snap Phainon out of whatever trance he was in. He gave a short laugh, reaching down to grab them. “The food smelled so good, they slipped from my hands.”

Clara placed her hands on her hips, shaking her head at her father. “Such a haikas.”

Mydei snorted, immediately turning back to the pan.

Confusion washed over Phainon. “What does that even mean?”

Ignoring his question, Mydei looked back just enough to nod proudly at Clara. “Nice job, by the way.” Really, because like he said, it was only a matter of time before he dropped that word on Phainon himself. It coming from his daughter made things ten times more comical.

“Thanks. I was in my room practicing.”

Phainon sighed dramatically. “Whatever. Gonna assume it means the best father to ever walk this earth.”

Mydei deadpanned, facing the man. “It means scoundrel. She was calling you a scoundrel.”

“Or sometimes hyena,” Clara countered.

“Or sometimes hyena,” Mydei agreed.

Phainon had the gall to act deflated. “Great. Yet another word she can use against me. You know what this means.” He took a seat by the table before swooping Clara into his lap, tickling her relentlessly as laughter filled the room. “Now you have to apologize!”

Mydei made the mistake of looking back.

Especially when he knew how dangerous of a sight Phainon was in father mode.

“No! Quit it!” Clara pleaded in between giggles, desperately trying to squeeze out of his grasp. “Mydei said it first! T-tickle him!”

That was a terrible idea. “You can’t tickle me, who’s gonna cook the food?”

Phainon showed her no mercy. “Only evil six year olds who hate their dad get tickled!” Mydei was too caught up in the ridiculousness of it all to acknowledge the wide smile on his own face.

“No! I love him! I don’t hate him at all!”

The laughter stopped. “Love you too, baby,” Phainon said, followed by a sound that was no doubt him kissing her head. Mydei needed to get out of here as soon as possible. It wasn’t safe to cook while feeling dizzy and that’s all Phainon made him feel right now. “Now go tickle Mydei since you got that word from him.”

Well that’s one way to get rid of the dizziness.

Mydei held the spatula out towards them with a stern glare. “Do not even think about it. Unless you want to be eating gnocchi off the floor because I will drop it.”

He watched as Clara and Phainon shared an unimpressed look before simultaneously speaking.

“Buzzkill.”

‘Buzzkill’ his ass. If they wanted their dinner to be perfect, then they would let him do his thing. “I’m the one cooking here.”

“Speaking of,” Phainon began, standing from his chair to walk towards Mydei. He leaned his against the counter, his entire body facing the latter. Why did he have to be so close? “You are staying for dinner, right?”

Mydei kept his eyes on Phainon’s, definitely not on the distance between them. Or in his case, the lack thereof. “I didn’t plan on it.”

“Can you plan on it?”

He was perfectly fine finishing up and leaving the rest to them. After all, he told Clara he’d make this for her. That didn’t ensure him staying as well, because this was something he could make any time. At his own place. “I’m sure you two want to enjoy your dinner alone.”

“Come on,” Clara drawled, giving puppy dog eyes that Phainon had the audacity to mimic. “Eat with us. We never have people over for dinner.”

Phainon pointed towards her with his thumb. “She said it’ll break her heart if you don’t.”

“Tch. Stop putting words in her mouth.”

Phainon leaned in closer, almost tempting Mydei to cave in and agree because that was a really dangerous thing right now. He smelled exactly as he did this morning, strong enough to overpower the food that was literally in front of them and it pissed Mydei off. How can one smell that good?

“Please. For me?”

An image of Phainon appeared in his mind, that same desperation looking up at him as he held onto Mydei’s closed thighs.

‘Please open them. For me?’

What…

The fuck.

He wasn’t sure what snapped him out of it first. The sting in his hand that he was slowly gaining awareness of, or Phainon’s gasp.

“Are you okay?” He asked in panic. Mydei fought the urge to roll his eyes. It was a pretty minor burn, definitely not from the hottest part he could’ve touched. The least it would do is leave redness and while it stung a little, he’s experienced worse in the kitchen. If anything, he was slightly glad for the sudden reality check.

It was Phainon’s fault. He was standing so close, and his stupid smell was messing with Mydei’s ability to think straight.

If he wanted to be spiteful, he could’ve made it Cipher’s fault too. Somehow.

“I’m fine,” he muttered, turning his attention back to the stove. “Comes with the territory.”

Clara chimed in. “Daddy, leave him alone. You made him burn himself.”

Smart kid. Mydei owed her one.

Fortunately Phainon listened, returning to his previous spot at the table. “As a compensation for burning yourself, you should eat dinner with us.” That wasn’t compensation at all. That was potential for even more thoughts and Mydei couldn’t deal with that right now. Why would he willingly comply?

“How many restaurants do you go into where the chef joins you for your meal?”

Phainon laughed. “How many restaurants are lucky to have a chef like you?”

Mydei sighed. “None right now, unfortunately.”

“Exactly!” The man beamed. Exactly what? How could there possibly be something to take from that? “So that just means since you’re one of a kind, we get privileges no one else does. Which includes you joining us for dinner, you said it yourself Mydei.”

He was one hundred percent sure he didn’t say that at all. “Why is eating with me a privilege?” And why was Phainon so adamant about it? He already got lunch out of him when, according to Clara, that wasn’t something he did for potential hires. Mydei just went along with it because it gave Phainon the chance to properly interview him.

What would eating dinner do now?

“Just is,” Phainon shrugged, looking at Clara. “Help me out here?”

She nodded. “Daddy’s right. We won’t see you again for a long time.”

Mydei cocked a brow. “You’ll see me in the morning.”

“And that’s a long time,” Phainon complained. “You can’t just go home and eat all by yourself. What kind of person would I be if I let you? It will keep me up all night and I won’t get any sleep.” Clearly nothing Mydei said was hindering their spirits, the two of them extremely focused on getting him to stay. Even if it meant throwing out ridiculous excuses.

“Drama queen.”

Phainon spoke carefully. “So does that mean you will eat with us?”

He sure did love to apply his own meanings to things. Mydei wasn’t any better by enabling it. “Only because Clara asked.”

Clara giggled. “I knew you liked me better.”

Phainon crossed his arms, shooting her a childish look. “He’s just saying that to make you feel better.”

She held an ‘L’ shape with her fingers over her forehead. “Stay mad, haikas.”

Mydei rolled his eyes, shaking his head with a smile.

What the hell did he just get himself into.

Mydei was making things ten times harder for Phainon and yes, he meant that in the literal sense too.

He was beyond screwed.

He thought the conversation with Hyacine today could’ve calmed him down a little, at least forcing him to accept the reality so that he wouldn’t get so lost in thought when he saw the man.

Then he came home and the living room was pretty much spotless.

Phainon tried not to think too much about it at first, it was bad enough that he had to envision the idea of Mydei going out of his way to do something so minimal for him. It was another thing completely for him to walk into his kitchen, being met with the sight of the most gorgeous back right in front of his face.

Standing in front of his stove.

Making dinner.

Like it was nothing, because according to Mydei, it wasn’t. He didn’t see it as an effort or something he felt forced to do, he said it himself. So yeah, Phainon dropped his keys, because how is he supposed to react when a man so perfect is treating him so…

Phainon didn’t even know the word. It’s not like he’s gone through this before.

As surreal as it all had been, he was only a man. A very perverted man, it seems, as he had to fight not to let his reaction tell through a potential tent in his pants. Whether it was thinking of his incompetent coworkers or his demanding boss, he did anything to derail his mind from the situation at hand.

Fortunately, Clara coming into the kitchen had been the perfect reality check.

It reminded him that Mydei was not someone he could ogle just because he looked too good with that apron tight around his waist. Mydei was someone who was watching his daughter, who deserved his utmost respect and not Phainon’s pervertedness.

Like he said, Mydei sure did make it hard though.

Phainon told himself that asking Mydei to stay for dinner was the right thing to do, that no one should cook just to leave once the food was finally finished. Deep down he knew it was his own selfish desires causing him to make the offer, but Mydei already accepted before Phainon could think twice about it.

In short, dinner was amazing.

It wasn’t like their outing last week. It didn’t feel like a necessity, there wasn’t the looming subject of a job revolving around their conversations. Mydei and Clara told him what they did today, Phainon lightly brushed over things at work, they bantered like it was the most natural thing in the world.

If Phainon wasn’t careful, he could really end up getting used to it.

If he wasn’t already, that is. Which wasn’t fair because one, it’s only been a day and two, Mydei was not bound to cook for them all of the time. The man was a chef but surely he had his days where he preferred to do something simple instead, like ordering takeout or getting Clara some pizza.

It still didn’t diminish the idea of sharing another dinner with him.

Phainon needed to stop. He explicitly told Hyacine that it wasn’t like that, and getting so sentimental over something as simple as dinner was a bit much, even for him.

He just couldn’t help that Mydei seemed to have no flaws.

Phainon sighed, approaching Clara’s bedroom door quietly before giving a few light taps. When he got the go ahead to enter, he pushed it open with a smile.

“Hey boss.”

“Hi,” she said from her bed, appearing as if she were waiting for him to come tell her goodnight.

He walked slowly towards the bed before taking a seat on the edge beside her. “All set for the night? Was dinner good?” Who was he kidding, the dinner was so good that it clearly made Phainon’s mind work overtime. Clara didn’t seem to have any complaints at the table either.

“It was amazing,” she nodded. “Mydei really knows how to cook.”

Phainon laughed. “He does, huh. So you really had a good time with him today?”

According to her and Mydei, they fed ducks at the park and got milkshakes, providing Phainon with the very sudden image of Mydei sipping on the treat. He could imagine the straw slightly grazing his lips, leaving just enough of the drink there for Phainon to reach his thumb out and–

“Mhm. It was the best day ever.”

Phainon really needed to get a grip. Shaking away that though, he tipped his head forward. “Does that mean he's a keeper?”

“Duh,” she said, like it should’ve been obvious and if that didn’t make Phainon happy, he wasn’t sure what could. It wasn’t just about Mydei this time, it was about the fact that she could confidently tell Phainon she enjoyed her babysitter. All of her answers up until now had been neutral or negative.

Mydei was one of a kind.

“Good,” he nodded, giving her hand a gentle squeeze. He was prepared to tell her goodnight when she tilted her head, looking up at him in question.

“Do you like him?”

Phainon’s eyes went wide. He knew his daughter was smart, but she couldn’t see his inner turmoil, could she? Hyacine was different, she was his best friend who liked to tease him any chance she got. Maybe Clara was just making sure Phainon was on the same page. That he enjoyed Mydei’s company as the babysitter too.

“Of course I like Mydei. I would hope we both do since he’s staying.

Clara shook her head, looking down at her lap. “That’s not what I–” She stopped, taking a second as if she were thinking before meeting his eyes once more. She gave him a small smile. “Yeah, I like him too.”

Phainon wasn’t going to question it further.

“Good.” He leaned forward, planting a kiss on the top of her head. “Get some sleep, I’m down the hall if you need anything.” He stood from the bed, ready to go to his own room so he could get his thoughts in order.

They said their quick goodnights and Phainon left, nervously biting at the inside of his lip as he walked down the hallway. He had no idea what Clara could’ve said in that moment, but if she were noticing things too then it was obvious his plan of ‘ignoring the problem’ wasn’t all that effective.

Now in the comfort of his own room, at least he could think about it freely.

It wasn’t just Mydei cooking or cleaning for them that set him off. It was everything that came with it, from his already strong relationship with Clara to how much he seemed to care about the job. Phainon couldn’t remember a time where previous babysitters had taken his daughter out to engage in an activity with her.

As far as he knew, they saw it as the chance to get away from her for a few hours.

Not Mydei, though. He gave her a fun first day and made her a delicious meal, one that Phainon was allowed to enjoy as well. They ate together and bantered like they’ve known each other forever, never once feeling out of place. In fact, Phainon was almost hesitant to send Mydei off once they were finished. He didn’t want him to leave yet.

Phainon flopped down onto his bed, thinking about what Hyacine and Clara asked him today.

Holy shit.

He just might actually like Mydei.

It was Mydei’s fault! He shouldn’t be so perfect if he didn’t want a weak man like Phainon driving himself crazy over him. It was fine before when Phainon was sure it was just attraction, because Mydei also happened to be the hottest person he’s ever seen and that was something anyone could notice.

Now that he was the whole package?

Phainon was very, very screwed.

He was also very, very hard.

He felt like such a pervert. Thinking back to Mydei’s ass as he cooked. Envisioning wiping excess milkshake off his lips. Licking it off, which couldn’t hold a candle to how Mydei probably tasted.

This wasn’t right. Mydei was his daughter’s babysitter, Phainon shouldn’t be thinking of him like this.

Forcing himself to his feet, he went to take a shower. A cold one, but it didn’t have the effect he wanted it to and if his hand ended up in places it shouldn’t be?

That wasn’t his problem tonight.

Mydei stared aimlessly at the wall.

The entire day played on loop in his head during the car ride home. Getting closer with Clara, laughing with her while chatting over the smallest things. Or the dinner, how persistent they were in him joining them. Phainon especially,

It… wasn’t so bad.

Mydei wasn’t in a rush to leave once it actually started, falling into a comfortable rhythm as they ate. It felt even better knowing they openly enjoyed his food, which is something he has no doubt heard a lot of in his line of work but it didn’t stop him from feeling less shy.

Maybe it meant more that they liked it. He wasn’t sure why.

Things were fine until it came time to clean, which he assured Phainon he had no issue in doing. The man, stubborn as he is, only agreed if he was able to help. So of course, Mydei let him help. All was well.

Until they just kept brushing against each other.

It was the faintest of touches at first, just enough for Mydei to quickly avert his gaze and go on about his task. Then Phainon truly caught him off guard once, causing Mydei to slightly lose his balance before a strong hand wrapped around his side to stabilize him.

“Sorry,” Phainon had said, practically right in his ear. Mydei just shook his head and assured him it was fine before moving to the opposite end of the kitchen.

Now, much to his dismay, he knew what Phainon’s hands felt like. On him.

He remembers the small squeeze like it happened two seconds ago, the phantom touch sending his mind down a dark path. He couldn’t help but wonder how hard that hand could truly grip, and the mark it would leave afterwards.

Phainon seemed like the type to like marks.

Apparently, Mydei seemed like the type to thirst over men he barely knew.

It’s why he deflected so much. If Phainon thought that Mydei saw him as ridiculous, then he wouldn’t know what really goes on inside his head.

He also wouldn’t begin to think that Mydei was staring at his bedside table right now, pondering over the object that was inside. The one that could ease some of the tension inside of him and make him feel good. Good like Phainon’s hands on him earlier.

One time wouldn’t hurt.

He’d allow himself one time before he forced himself to get over it, because Phainon wasn’t the bigger picture. He was just pent up, that was all this was. The man invoking certain thoughts in him was proof of nothing.

Mydei needed to remember that he had a job to do, just like Phainon had other things to think about.

Chapter End Notes

Left that last part up for interpretation but to me, Mydei definitely grabbed that toy and went HAM. Probably said Phainon's name too

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

The one where Mother Nature decides to throw her two cents in.

Mydei leaned back against the pillows with a smirk.

“You’re really going to make me work for it?” Phainon asked, crawling towards him with a grin of his own. One that completely contradicted the nature of the question, as if it weren’t evident the man was enjoying this.

“Thought you preferred it that way?”

Phainon stopped, placing himself in between Mydei’s legs with enough distance that their bodies weren’t touching. Yet. It was only a matter of time before he caved, because for some reason Mydei couldn’t comprehend, it always ended with Phainon’s hands on him. He wasn’t in a spot to complain, not with how his eyes were practically daring him to.

Every time.

Phainon tilted his head, speaking quietly. “What makes you say that?”

Mydei shrugged. “Gut feeling. You’re a hard working man, Phainon.” He emphasized his words by shifting his leg, carefully placing his foot over Phainon’s bulge. It must’ve been so painful, his pants looked so tight. Mydei gave a slow, experimental rub. “This should be nothing to you.”

He wanted to test the man. To see how long Phainon could teeter on the edge before dragging Mydei down with him, their pleasure intertwining as they finally fell. Mydei wanted to be broken apart, to have Phainon guide him the rest of the way just to get back up and repeat the process over…

And over.

And over.

“Nothing?” Phainon repeated, shaking his head with a laugh. “This isn’t nothing to me, baby. This?” He grabbed Mydei’s foot, moving the latter’s leg so that it now rested atop his shoulder. “Is mine.”

If it wasn’t for Mydei’s pants, Phainon would’ve seen how wet that had gotten him.

But he couldn’t, so giving the man an early victory wasn’t ideal for him right now.

“Who told you that?”

Phainon chuckled, not bothering to answer before he moved up, finally slotting himself against Mydei. “No one had to tell me anything.” The blonde could feel that hardness press against his thigh, knowing Phainon deliberately avoided being where Mydei really needed him. This is how their game worked, before one inevitably surrendered so they could get what they both wanted.

It was always Mydei.

This time didn’t seem any different.

He clenched his teeth. “Get… on with it.”

“When’d you get so needy?” Phainon asked lightheartedly.

Cocky bastard. “When did your precision get so bad?” Mydei looked down to clarify, hoping his silent way of telling Phainon to move worked. Knowing his luck, the latter would keep going until Mydei was forced to beg for it, or at the very least say ‘please.’

This time, he had a different idea.

“Who said my precision was bad?”

Mydei didn’t bother answering his question, not when Phainon ended up moving anyway. A soft sigh fell from his lips as he felt Phainon’s clothed cock finally press against him, causing Mydei to clench around nothing. He was so wet right and if his pants were any lighter, Phainon would’ve known.

Who was he kidding, Phainon already knew. It’s why he was looking down at him like he was ready to eat.

Mydei would let him feast until he couldn’t anymore.

Unfortunately, Phainon correctly adjusting himself didn’t mean Mydei would get the relief he craved for. Not when the other man remained still, giving Mydei that stupid smile as if he didn’t know what he was doing.

Mydei had waited long enough.

“Phainon,” he said and Phainon hummed, his lack of a verbal response only making Mydei grow more frustrated. “Phainon.”

“Yes?” The man answered slowly, almost feigning innocence. It would’ve been believable if his cock wasn’t currently prodding at Mydei through their clothes, giving them both a taste of what was to come. Mydei was here to make sure they quit wasting time so it happened sooner than he hoped.

“Come here.”

Phainon laughed. “Where? I’d say we’re pretty close right now.”

“Lean down,” Mydei bit out, his heated eyes boring into blue ones. “Wanna tell you something.”

Curiosity washed over Phainon as he leaned down, almost burying his head in Mydei’s neck. Instinct seemed to take over him at the moment, mouthing at the skin in front of him. Mydei was lucky his neck wasn’t the most sensitive part of him, but that was something Phainon was also aware of which meant Mydei needed to act before he lost the upper hand.

He tipped his head just enough for his lips to graze Phainon’s ear, allowing a few more kisses down his shoulder before Mydei finally whispered.

“I wanna give you another baby.”

Phainon’s mouth was no longer on him.

Mydei could still feel it though, hovering over his shoulder. A warm breath fell out before Phainon could stop it, followed by a drawn out moan and before Mydei knew it, those hips began to move.

“Fuck,” Phainon said underneath his breath, hiding his face further into Mydei’s neck. “Fuck, Mydei. Say it again.”

Mydei smiled, biting his lip while Phainon quickened the pace. “Say what?” The man above him grunted, pressing further into Mydei. Pressure that grazed his clit just the right way, causing him to let out a small whine before continuing. “Don’t wanna knock me up?”

“Fuck… fuck, Mydei.”

A simple sentence, and that was all it took for Phainon to unravel.

Mydei closed his eyes, arms reaching up to wrap around Phainon, locking them both in place. “Don’t stop…”

“Mydei… Mydei.”

Their voices were barely whispers now, now bordering short and broken breaths. “Don’t stop, Phainon. Keep going.”

“Mydei.”

He wasn’t sure if the heat of the moment began to warp his senses or Phainon’s voice, though the part of his brain that hadn’t fallen off the edge already could tell it did sound different. The rutting against him never stopped, so it wasn’t enough for Mydei to pull away and rob himself of the feeling he’s been longing for.

“Mydei.”

He kept his eyes closed and furrowed his brows. Phainon’s voice had grown faint this time around, mingling with someone else’s. Mydei’s breaths concealed most of the sound for him to know where it came from, so he remained in place and allowed that force to continue rocking against him.

Just one more—

“Mydei!”

His eyes opened and he shot up in an instant.

He wasn’t in Phainon’s room anymore. Where the space had been dimly lit before, sunlight now peeked through the curtains. Where he had previously been fully clothed, he was now naked save for his underwear that, thankfully, was concealed by the covers. Where Phainon had been hovering over him before…

Cipher now stood by his bed instead.

With enough coherency, Mydei realized that his current situation was getting ridiculous.

Two weeks. Two weeks had passed since Mydei started watching Clara. One would think that would be enough time to get over whatever spell Phainon seemed to have him under. Clearly not, seeing as this wasn’t the first time he woke up in a sweat after vivid dreams of the man handling his body so thoroughly. It was pure and utter torture.

It was even worse that as much build up these dreams seemed to have, they were always cut short before he could get to the part he wanted to.

Maybe it was a sign.

Once the initial shock wore off, Mydei slowly turned his head to the left, glaring daggers at the woman who didn’t even seem phased. He could’ve blamed it on being tired, that he was still feeling hazy from his dream and this wasn’t real.

Too bad Mydei’s luck ran out long ago.

“One.”

Cipher cocked a brow. “One what?”

“One good reason why you’re standing in my room at…” He trailed off, leaning over to check the alarm clock at the other side of the bed, “Seven in the morning, Cipher are you kidding me? I wasn’t supposed to be up for another thirty minutes.” It was one thing to pull him from his sleep, it was another to break into his house just to do it because where the hell did she even get the key?

“You weren’t answering your phone,” she said, walking aimlessly around as she began to pick up things she probably didn’t care about, observing them nonetheless. “You didn’t answer, so I did the next best thing.”

Mydei rubbed his temples, closing his eyes. It was too early for this. “Some would call it a crime. How did you even get in?”

“Uh,” she drawled, plopping down in his desk chair. “I think the question you should be asking is ‘how is it so easy to break into my apartment?’” Whatever, his best guess was she had gotten the key he gave Castorice in case of emergency. He should’ve known refusing to give her one wouldn’t do any good in the long run.

“Can you just tell me what you want.”

She shrugged. “Sure. Something is wrong with my car.”

Mydei’s eyes opened and he turned to her slowly once more, staring incredulously at her for a few seconds. He spoke very carefully, desperately hoping he hadn’t heard her right. “You came to my house… over a problem… that a licensed mechanic could fix.”

“That is correct.”

“And your bright idea is to ruin my sleep to achieve this.”

She nodded slowly. “Yes. I thought that was pretty clear.” Perfect, beautiful even. Not only did Mydei have to be up earlier than usual, but he had to drag himself outside over a problem that was likely not even a problem at all. “Must’ve been a good sleep, damn. What were you even dreaming about anyway?”

Mydei went still. “Why, what did you hear?”

Cipher examined him closely before smirking. “Who said I heard anything?” Mydei rolled his eyes and she continued. “Relax, little prince. I didn’t hear anything. If DILF of the year had you in twenty different positions all the way until Saturday, I would have never known.”

“Goodness,” Mydei muttered.

“But come,” she said, pushing herself to her feet. “I was polite enough to wake you up thirty minutes before so that you weren’t late.” ‘Polite,’ because that’s the word he would use to describe her right now. “Or maybe you would want that. Maybe you wanna be punished by him. Damn, should I have waited longer?”

“Cipher.”

“Yes?”

“Get out of my room.”

Fortunately she did, albeit laughing on her way out. It took everything for Mydei not to lie back down for the remainder of the time left just to spite her, though he knew it wouldn’t be that easy. She would just wake him up again and he didn’t even think sleeping was all that worth it now.

With a sigh, he got out of bed and threw some clothes on. As much as he wanted to take his sweet time, the last thing he would’ve wanted was for the problem to take longer than expected and push him back. In the past two weeks he’s been babysitting, he hasn’t been late once. He wasn’t going to start now just because he wanted to stick it to Cipher.

Apparently not all of Mydei’s luck had run out.

Cipher’s issue did end up being real, much to his surprise, though it wasn’t severe enough to take up most of his time. Just a clogged air filter that Mydei fixed without a hitch, before sending her on his way so he could prepare for his ‘shift.’

However, after two weeks, Mydei was tempted to say it felt less like a job. Now it was just something he enjoyed, something he seemed to be a natural at.

He just so happened to get paid for it too.

Excluding his very inappropriate thoughts regarding his technical boss, the three of them fell into a rhythm really easily. Mydei would have his interactions with Phainon before the man left for work, where he would then spend the rest of the day strengthening his bond with Clara. On days where he cooked dinner, Phainon would immediately ask him to stay over and as much as Mydei feigned reluctance, he always agreed.

It wasn’t just when Mydei cooked, though. There was one time Phainon had ordered takeout and convinced Mydei to stay.

It was weird. A good weird, because as much as Phainon would ramble on or complain about his day, Mydei never once felt out of place.

It was comfortable.

He learned a lot about Clara within the two weeks as well. Some would argue that they weren’t things of great significance, but Mydei enjoyed her presence a lot and clung to everything she said. The gift bag sitting in the passenger seat was proof of that. She loved to express the things she was interested in, giving Mydei the perfect opportunity to really know her.

There was always one thing that never got brought up, though.

It was also the one thing Mydei vowed not to ask about, because the situation regarding her mother wasn’t his business. Any time the curiosity would arise, he’d push it aside and remind himself that it doesn’t get brought up for a reason.

So yeah, it was safe to say he got used to things pretty quickly.

Mydei pulled into the all too familiar driveway, grabbing the gift bag before making his way to the porch. He didn’t bother to knock, digging out the key because that seemed to happen too. He should’ve been concerned as to why Phainon made him his own copy after only a week, but he couldn’t be surprised anymore.

Phainon was the same man who picked up a random babysitter in a shoe store, after all.

Speak of the devil.

Neat.

Fast.

Phainon’s mother, Mydei presumed. The first he’s ever heard of the woman. “Used to? She doesn’t anymore?”

That… was horrible.

Oh.

It was just the result of a conscious decision Mydei made four years ago.

Understatement. They haven’t spoken for a long time now.

Clara frowned. “I’m sorry. Is she mad at you for something?”

It’s why he never could fully live with it until he proved them wrong, until he got on his own proper footing and paved a life that he influenced.

Clara didn’t respond, though her serious expression remained as she pushed away from the counter and walked towards Mydei. He had no time to prepare when small arms wrapped around his neck, pulling him into a soft hug.

“It’s okay. I'm sure it wasn’t your fault.”

Mydei couldn’t move, nor could he offer any words back.

She was too kind, because in hindsight, it probably was his fault.

Clara waited a few more seconds before finally letting go, giving Mydei a warm smile before returning to her spot at the kitchen sink. Mydei felt the corner of his own lips tug upwards, realizing that was the first kind of contact they had since he took this job. He must’ve been doing something right, because that was all he needed to know how comfortable she felt around him.

Despite Phainon’s frequent foolishness, Mydei could say one thing for certain.

He sure did know how to raise a child.

Mydei would occasionally glance over at the clock, telling himself that Phainon should be home soon, though the man never showed. Clara didn’t say anything, though Mydei could tell she was tense too.

She moved locations once they were done in the kitchen, now seated on the couch as she peeked through the curtains. Her back was facing him, but Mydei didn’t have to guess that her father being late was making her worry as well.

The storm only got worse, now with the winds picking up.

If Mydei didn’t at least try to offer the girl comfort, then he might end up staring out of the window with her.

When, not if.

With great reluctance, Clara nodded and pulled away from the couch, walking into the kitchen. They worked in silence, presumably so they could hear the inevitable moment Phainon finally walked through the door.

After what felt like a century, Mydei could faintly pick up on the sound of the lock clicking. He dropped the icing bag without another thought, marching back towards the living room. Clara followed quickly behind.

“Oh, hey Mydei—”

That… felt good to get out.

Good. Mydei nodded. “And the other stuff?”

Promising he wouldn’t do it again.

'How’s it feel, princess?’

“Hey Mydei.”

No, but you can put me to sleep. In any way you like.

This time, Mydei didn’t deflect. He just ignored the question entirely before allowing Clara to lead him away. He could hear Phainon’s laugh from the living room.

“Dei?” Mydei looked down, raising his brow in question. “I’m really glad you’re staying over.”

It was a really sweet thing to hear.

Mydei just didn’t know how to respond to it.

He couldn’t exactly say he was too, at least entirely, not when his thoughts were all over the place because of her father. He knew he couldn’t blame it entirely on Phainon, it’s not like he was openly asking to get ogled and have everything he said taken as an innuendo. Mydei just wanted to assume the man knew some of what he was doing.

Or maybe he didn’t. Maybe Mydei was just the freak who couldn’t keep it under control.

On the other hand, it’s not that he didn’t enjoy the idea of spending the night. It was nice to know his presence warranted the request, proving the family was just as familiar with him. It also allowed him to do things like this, telling his favorite six year old goodnight because she wanted him to be the one doing so.

In the end, Mydei just nodded, giving a soft smile and hoping that said enough.

As much as he wished he would’ve been wrong, Mydei couldn’t get any sleep.

The first two hours he tried were spent tossing and turning, attempting to find a comfortable position but to no avail. He then moved to lie on his back, allowing his thoughts to be the thing that finally pulled him into a slumber. It’s usually what happened any other night, and it might provoke some explicit dreams later on but at least he’d be able to sleep.

It might have been the location. He could peacefully give into whatever his mind conjured up in the comfort of his own home. Now it was annoying, because he couldn’t help but feel guilty seeing as this wasn’t even his bed.

It wasn’t Phainon’s either, but it was close enough.

With a frustrated grunt, he kicked the covers off and briefly checked the time.

Two in the morning. Mydei had to be up in about five hours.

There was no point in forcing it right now. He quietly left the room and made his way to the kitchen, careful not to make any noises that would wake the others up. He ignored his original intent of getting water when he saw the cupcakes from earlier on the counter, even though normally Mydei wouldn’t indulge this late at night.

Sweets just made him tired, and he was getting pretty desperate.

He grabbed a cupcake, standing in front of the sink as he took a bite in silence. His mind went back to dinner, unknowingly smiling at the memory of Phainon complimenting the job Mydei and Clara had done. He also remembered jokingly limiting the man to one, before the latter pulled out those stupid puppy eyes that had Mydei relenting immediately.

Not without his shield of annoyance, of course.

Mydei prepared to take another bite when the sound of slow footsteps could be heard. He stared straight ahead outside the kitchen window, waiting for whoever it was to make themselves known. He wanted to hope it was just Clara, who might have woken up to the sound of Mydei rummaging in the kitchen. He’d put her back to bed and that would be that.

You know what they say about hope.

It didn’t take much for him to know it was Phainon when those footsteps finally reached the room. He wouldn’t go as far as to say he could sense that kind of thing, but that was not the sound of a little girl walking.

“I thought I heard something in here,” Phainon said, and Mydei could practically hear his smirk.

He still didn’t look away from the window. “The rain finally let up.” The timing sure was inconvenient, too.

Phainon chuckled, stepping closer to him. “Don’t tell me you’re planning on leaving now.”

It wasn’t that bad of an idea. Considering Mydei wasn’t tired and couldn’t sleep, he wouldn’t have to worry about passing out at the wheel. “And if I were?”

“Well, then I would go outside and purposefully try to piss Mother Nature off again.”

Mydei attempted to scoff. It came out more like a laugh. “Idiot.”

He didn’t have to look to know Phainon had smiled at that.

“Hey.” The man’s voice shifted into something different, something more serious, yet gentle. Mydei finally turned his head, watching as the man leaned his back against the counter right beside the sink. It wasn’t hard to notice the few inches between them now, even if Mydei tried not to. “Were you really worried earlier?”

Mydei fought to focus on nothing but his face. Not the fact that while the glasses may be gone, the compression shirt stayed, paired with those big arms that looked even bigger up close.

“Clara was.”

Phainon slightly tipped his head forward. “Clara wasn’t the one reprimanding me.”

“She would have. I just did the honors for her.”

“Right, right,” Phainon nodded, obviously not buying it. For some reason, Mydei didn’t feel the urge to try and back his case. “Thank you, though. For being concerned.”

Mydei didn’t know what to say to that, and Phainon stared back at him as if he were waiting on something. It didn’t matter. If Mydei couldn’t get something as simple as sleep, Phainon couldn’t get what he wanted either.

“Mhm,” he hummed, pursing his lips. Phainon continued looking at him, irritating Mydei to no end. What else was he supposed to give? He quickly averted his gaze, shaking his head. “Are you in here to get a cupcake or something? Or are you just bothering me.”

“Sure,” Phainon shrugged, taking Mydei’s defensiveness lightly. Mydei could feel him barely lean in, presumably to reach behind him and grab the container. He wasn’t sure why Phainon didn’t walk to the other side, like a normal person, but he also had little time to really question it.

In a swift movement, Phainon ducked down to sneak a bite at the cupcake in Mydei’s hand.

Mydei’s eyes widened the second it happened.

He spoke his next words very slowly.

“What… is wrong with you.”

Phainon leaned back up with false innocence, covering his mouth. “What? You asked if I wanted to get one.” All Mydei could do was glare as Phainon finished his bite, taken aback by the absolute gall of this man.

If his eyes lingered to Phainon’s tongue that darted out to lick his lips, no one would have to know.

“Your own, haikas!” Mydei scolded, pulling the rest of his cupcake back so Phainon didn’t get any more bright ideas. “Not lean down like a dog and steal from mine.”

Phainon pouted. “But I wanted to eat yours instead.”

Mydei could’ve dropped the cupcake.

He didn’t, of course. He felt his body slightly go rigid, a familiar feeling creeping its way into his gut. The way Phainon was looking at him paired with the way his words sounded was a dangerous combo. It didn’t take long for images to appear into Mydei’s head, Phainon pleading to eat something else rather than the stupid cupcake.

He wasn’t able to indulge in those thoughts for long, because for the first time, Mydei could see it.

Phainon’s eyes slightly shifted.

He knew what Mydei was thinking.

There was no other reason for it. When this usually happened, Mydei would be able to snap out of it quick enough to retort back and Phainon would be none the wiser.

They were never standing this close before, so of course Phainon would see it all.

But… he wasn’t moving away. He didn’t bring it up like Mydei assumed he would, because making a remark about it seemed his style. He just remained silent, eyes locked in place and Mydei thinks he would rather have the joke instead. That way he could bite back and forget this ever happened.

Before Mydei could contemplate how to get out of this one, Phainon’s gaze fell on his lips. Mydei’s breath caught in his throat when a thumb slowly reached out, barely grazing the corner of his mouth.

“Had a little bit of icing,” Phainon whispered.

But his thumb didn’t retreat. Mydei didn’t pull away either.

Instead, it pressed against him just a little more, moving from its spot so it could now run along Mydei’s bottom lip. The latter didn’t dare to move, unaware if he ended up falling asleep after all and this was all some dream. It wouldn’t be that absurd, things between them always initiated this easily in his subconscious.

This was real. He knew that, because his heart wouldn’t be pounding this much if it weren’t.

He gained enough control to open his mouth just a little, a silent invitation for whatever game they were playing right now. Phainon noticed it. He could see Phainon noticing it, though the man never once went any further. The most he could do was lightly pull Mydei’s bottom lip down, applying a bit more pressure.

Mydei made the mistake of trying to catch that finger himself.

The second he angled his head down to get more, Phainon blinked rapidly, breaking out of whatever trance the two of them had been in.

Mydei quickly looked away.

“Sorry,” Phainon said, awkwardly clearing his throat. He apparently couldn’t look at Mydei either. “That… wow, that was really unprofessional of me.”

Unprofessional.

Right.

‘It’s fine,” Mydei muttered. It wasn’t fine, because it was him who had been unprofessional all along. He’s been the one lusting after Phainon this whole time. The worst part was after tonight, Mydei knew it wouldn’t stop.

It would probably increase tenfold.

‘I’m, uh… I’m gonna head back to sleep.” Mydei would love to say he would do the same, but there was no way that would be possible tonight. Not anymore, even if he had sweets in his system. “Help yourself. To anything in here, I mean.”

Yeah, because Mydei really needed the clarification after that. As if he would really try helping himself to Phainon.

Mydei said nothing, though Phainon didn’t wait for a response this time around. He hurried out of the kitchen, and as bad as Mydei felt doing it to something he worked on with Clara, he trashed the rest of his cupcake.

He wasn’t really that hungry anymore.

He made his way back to the guest room, taking a seat on the bed while he tried to process what the hell just happened. And what was Phainon’s problem? Mydei can excuse the man calling it unprofessional, because it was, but no one asked him to put his thumb on Mydei’s lip. No one asked him to keep it there, that was a conscious decision he made on his own.

If it was so unprofessional, what was the point?

Mydei let out an irritated sigh as he grabbed his phone, wasting no time in finding his messages.

Mydei: are you awake.
Mydei: i have a weird question. and be serious
Mydei: don’t make me regret this either

He was already regretting it.

Cipher ^. .^: yes mydei. i WILL take sexy polaroids of you to gift to your dilf

Point proven.

Mydei: i said be serious.

Cipher ^. .^: i am

Mydei: bye

Maybe this was a sign that he’d just have to deal with it himself, until the inevitable moment where he saw Phainon again in the morning.

Cipher ^. .^: okok fine
Cipher ^. .^: what’s up

Mydei stared off into space, internally questioning how he would word everything. It was already bad enough that he was considering telling Cipher when he knew she would have plenty to say about it. He only needed to explain it well enough so she could at least understand it all.

Mydei: phainon touched my lip and idk how to take it

That probably could’ve been said better. Going into the details just meant remembering the details, and right now? He’d rather not.

Cipher ^. .^: what do you mean

Mydei frowned.

Mydei: ??? i just said what i mean

Cipher ^. .^: did he randomly just start poking at your lip or something…?
Cipher ^. .^: did he shush you?
Cipher ^. .^: touching your lip can mean a lot of things dude

As annoying as it felt to further elaborate, any of those she mentioned would’ve been ideal. They’d be less serious than whatever the hell Phainon pulled a few minutes ago.

Mydei: his thumb.

Surely that was enough.

Cipher ^. .^: THAT kind of touching
Cipher ^. .^: holy shit
Cipher ^. .^: when

He was not telling Cipher that he was staying over. That was a separate can of worms he wasn’t prepared to get into right now.

Mydei: a while ago in the kitchen

Cipher ^. .^: why were you in the kitchen together

Mydei was in the kitchen because he couldn’t sleep. He doesn’t know why Phainon stayed as long as he did, and who cared if it was his house.

Mydei: not the point. it happened and i’m not sure how to take it

Cipher ^. .^: that’s erotic as hell you know
Cipher ^. .^: straight up folding you over the kitchen counter would’ve been less erotic than that

It wasn’t a bad thought.

Phainon would call it an unprofessional one, though.

Mydei: it doesn’t matter, he pulled away and apologized for being unprofessional.
Mydei: so like i said, i don’t know how to take it

He didn’t even know if he had icing on his mouth to begin with. They had been staring at each other long enough for Phainon to reach out earlier if that really had been the case. Not to mention, he would’ve pulled away the second it was gone. Instead he just kept his finger there, leaving Mydei wanting to do nothing but suck it into his mouth right then and there.

Cipher ^. .^: well then that just makes it a million times more erotic

Mydei: ?

Cipher ^. .^: oh my little prince
Cipher ^. .^: if he sees it that way then it’s clearly something he wanted to do
Mydei: the whole taboo of it all

It wasn’t taboo. It wasn’t forbidden, just not appropriate given their current circumstance.

Mydei: it’s phainon. for some reason, i don’t think that’s true

Cipher ^. .^: dude
Cipher ^. .^: if the only thing he can say is it was unprofessional then the ball is more in your court than you realize

That didn’t make any sense. If the ball was in his court, he would’ve had that thumb in his mouth and possibly even something else. All he got was the reminder that he shouldn’t be lusting over the guy who’s paying him to watch his daughter. Phainon’s own indulgence aside.

Mydei: it was an innocent conversation that turned into that

Cipher ^. .^: highly doubt it was innocent if you were involved

She wasn’t wrong. It only started because Mydei couldn’t help but think perverted thoughts over a meaningless comment Phainon made about his cupcake.

Cipher ^. .^: you think things will be awkward in the morning?

He didn’t know. He honestly didn’t want to think that far ahead.

Mydei: not sure

Cipher ^. .^: better not be
Cipher ^. .^: mydei you have the opportunity of a lifetime and i’m gonna need you not to mess it up

Mydei: the hell are you talking about

Cipher ^. .^: if the mutual attraction has already been established then you just gotta get past the professionalism part
Cipher ^. .^: act indifferent about it and let the man come to you
Cipher ^. .^: you’re kind of a brat so i doubt it’ll take late before he breaks

There were only a few issues with that. First of all, mutual attraction has never been established. Mydei thirsted over the man day and night but Phainon running his thumb on his lip didn’t mean he felt the same. For all he knew, it was a simple action meant to catch Mydei off guard.

Second, acting indifferent would’ve been easy if he had been doing that already. Indecent thoughts just loved to appear at the worst times, and Mydei always fell victim to them.

It was never going to work.

Mydei: kind of a brat?

Cipher ^. .^: good point. you’re a brat through and through

Mydei rolled his eyes.

Cipher ^. .^: seriously though. let that dilf chase you
Cipher ^. .^: he pulled away so obviously it’s not on you to worry. you’re not the one making the next move, he is
Cipher ^. .^: aw and maybe you can give clara a sibling
Cipher ^. .^: aunt cipher will take care of them on weekends but only if you pay me

His head was starting to hurt.

Mydei: bye. goodnight.

Cipher ^. .^: night baby mama

He was half tempted to block her. Just for the night.

Mydei set his phone down, falling back against the pillows. He briefly wondered if she had a point. Mydei’s never been in the position where he was practically rejected, and definitely not by someone who was paying him. It wouldn’t just be a normal cat and mouse game. It would be a cat and mouse game with the looming thought that Phainon might not drop the professionalism at all.

Which meant… Cipher was right. It wasn’t his place to worry about it, not until Phainon made the next move. If he didn’t? At least Mydei still had a well paying job, one he really enjoyed.

He could get his lusting under control. At the very least, file it away for material he may or may not use later. It wouldn’t be easy, but if all it took was indifference to potentially crack at Phainon’s facade?

There was no harm in trying.

Despite barely sleeping, Mydei didn’t feel that tired in the morning.

He wouldn’t lie and say he was fine with facing Phainon now. Mydei had no clue what Phainon would say to him, if he even bothered to go into what happened at all. If things were awkward, Mydei hoped at least one of them would be mindful enough to fix it before Clara could notice.

So, as nonchalantly as he could, Mydei walked into the kitchen.

He could see Phainon through his peripherals, the man turning his head and freezing at the sight of him. Mydei paid it no mind, simply filling up a glass of water. Phainon cleared his throat.

“Good morning, Mydei.”

It’s not on you to worry about it.

“Morning,” Mydei muttered, finally turning to face him. “Do you mind if I cook some breakfast? Figured it might give Clara something to wake up to.”

Phainon’s eyes widened for a split second, taken aback by the question. Maybe it was just Mydei’s dismissive attitude in general, but he didn’t make any attempts to point it out. Instead, he nodded with a smile. “Of course. None for me?”

Great. Good to see he could act the same too.

Mydei scoffed. “Calm down. I’m not going to let you starve. Obviously you’ll get the scraps.”

Phainon crossed his arms, cocking a brow. Mydei tried not to think too hard about those arms. They may be in a button up shirt now, but he could never get the sight of them bare out of his mind. Or the lingering fantasies that came alone with it. “What am I, a dog?”

How ironic.

“Some would say.”

He could feel Phainon staring at him as he moved throughout the kitchen, preparing the ingredients for breakfast. There was no telling what was on the man’s mind right now, but if it was the same as what was going through Mydei’s, then it was better for them to stand in silence.

With how easy it was to fall back into their natural rhythm, talking about last night wasn’t exactly ideal.

So, Mydei wouldn’t. He’d go on about his day, taking whatever chance he could with Clara to poke fun at Phainon before spending the rest of the day with her. At least his job was the one thing he never had to be uncertain of, because there was no doubt about his bond with Clara.

Mydei enjoyed what he did. He wouldn’t jeopardize it over one moment with Phainon, especially not until the man came to him about it. If it happens, it happens.

If it doesn’t…

Then it doesn’t.
