Phainon liked to claim he was a lot of different things. A good friend, a great father…

A world class overthinker, apparently.

It’s not like he welcomed the idea of potentially messing something up in his mind. It just liked to creep in and hide there, reminding him that he always has the ability to. It’s why he puts in so much effort into the things closest to him, because he’d never be able to live with himself if he was the one to throw it all away.

The only problem was, regarding his current dilemma, nothing had been thrown away at all. The overthinker in Phainon told him it was too good to be true.

Phainon knew it would have been fair if he did mess everything up. After all, he would’ve been at fault.

Even if Mydei’s lips looked so inviting.

Even if Mydei looked like he wanted it.

Despite it all, Phainon was aware that no one other than himself caused him to react so suddenly. Seeing Mydei like that, seeing that heated stare that immobilized him, none of that was a good enough excuse. There was nothing else to blame other than Phainon’s lack of self control.

Self control that he thought he had enough of.

Every little thing Mydei did threw Phainon for a loop. Even when the former had scolded him for being late two weeks ago, as much as Phainon wanted to reach out to those pouty lips, he didn’t. He couldn’t, and that was something he always reminded himself. All it took was that night where they had been alone in the kitchen for everything to snap.

That’s when Phainon realized he might not be as strong as he believed.

Mydei knew it too now, a thought he had to live with every time he saw the man. No matter how much they brushed the subject aside, Phainon was forced to remember that Mydei was aware of how weak he was.

The worst part?

Phainon can’t stop thinking about it.

He can’t stop mulling over what might’ve happened if he indulged, if he slipped his thumb in that mouth for even the briefest of moments. Mydei would give him that same stare, eyes wide and focused on nothing but Phainon. The finger would slide deeper, pressing down against Mydei’s tongue while he sucked.

Phainon thought he was doing himself a favor when he apologized for being unprofessional. At the very least, saying it out loud would’ve reminded him that he was. It would’ve been more effective if Phainon’s perverted mind didn’t fall back to that memory, or what else he could do to ever have Mydei like that again.

Considering he didn’t want to mess everything up, that probably wasn’t going to happen.

It was nothing he hadn’t done before. Admiring Mydei from a distance was something he was used to by now. Even if he had to do it with the constant memory of how Mydei’s lips felt.

“You look like you’re hurting yourself thinking.”

Truth be told, he kinda was.

Phainon sighed, shaking his head. It was more so directed towards himself, partially ashamed for going quiet during his outing with Hyacine. “It’s nothing. Work and all.”

Because yeah, Mydei could be a real piece of work. Even if he didn’t realize it.

Hyacine hummed, taking a sip of her drink. “I see. So it’s about Mydei.”

Phainon went still. “I didn’t even—”

“Say that?” She finished, shooting him an incredulous look. “I’m aware. I’m also aware that if it actually was about work, you wouldn’t be sitting there brooding. You’d be ranting my head off so I’m only gonna ask once, what did you do?”

“Huh? What do you mean? Who said I did anything?”

Hyacine rolled her eyes. “Because I know whatever you did, poor Mydei probably doesn’t get paid enough for it.”

First of all, she didn’t know that at all. Second of all, “do you remember when you didn’t trust him at first? I remember that. Do you remember that?”

“Do you want me to not trust him?”

He’d be lying to himself if he said she didn’t have a point. “No, that’s not allowed. He could do no wrong.” It wasn’t far from the truth anyway, especially with Phainon’s predicament. Mydei was just the innocent bystander in the perverted thoughts swarming through Phainon’s mind. “But, since you asked, it’s complicated.”

“We haven’t had lunch in two weeks. How could you have possibly made things complicated?”

He didn’t necessarily want to prove her right. Unfortunately, admitting what happened meant doing so and Phainon would just have to bite the bullet with that one.

“I did something.”

“Famous last words,” Hyacine muttered. “Go on.”

What was he supposed to say, that he almost shoved his thumb in Mydei’s mouth? That Mydei pretty much chased it himself before Phainon finally grew the courage to walk away? It wasn’t his proudest moment, sure, but saying that out loud wasn’t that simple. Especially to Hyacine.

In the end, all he could go with was, “I almost made a move on him. In my kitchen.” And really, if Phainon was lucky enough to always get his way? Things would’ve played out much differently.

He’s only dreamt of the possibilities since the night it didn’t happen.

“You didn’t,” she began, disappointment growing in her tone. Or maybe it was pity, maybe she could already tell he had fucked up.

“Just hear me out,” Phainon quickly defended, and Hyacine exhaled before giving him the chance to continue. “I didn’t— okay, it’s not like it was random. It wasn’t some out of the blue thing. It was dark, we were alone. I read his facial expressions and the next thing I know, I’m reaching out.”

Hyacine nodded dryly. “Wow Phainon, I didn’t know you could read facial expressions now. Maybe you can tell me what mine says.”

He frowned. “Well I’m going to assume it’s not a good one.”

“Huh, guess you are good at that.” Her voice was laced with sarcasm, pretty much shaming his lack of well thought out choices. “You do know the rule of thumb is to act when you’re one hundred percent sure you’re reading them right. Not because your lust-filled eyes are telling your mind something else.”

Phainon shook his head. “That’s exactly my point. I did read everything right. My lust-filled eyes were not deceiving me.”

Mydei being the one to lean in made that hard to be the case. Phainon could never wipe that image from his brain even if he tried. In the following days after it happened, all he could see when he looked at the blond was those pretty lips opening wider. Expecting more.

Phainon would do anything to give him more.

“Wait.” Hyacine tilted her head, eyeing him with concern. “So… you guys went through with it?”

A man could dream. “Not exactly.”

“I’m a bit confused.”

Phainon was glad to know he wasn’t the only one. “He wanted it too. I could see it, Hyacine.” Phainon was ninety percent sure this made him a terrible boss. Letting his mind fall back to Mydei’s sinful expression wasn’t exactly the moral thing to do right now. “But nothing happened. I stopped once I realized what was going on, apologized for being unprofessional, and that was that.”

‘Unprofessional.’

As if Phainon hadn’t crossed that bridge already.

Unfortunately, it didn’t make any more sense to Hyacine than it did a few seconds ago. “Okay… Well, are you saying things are awkward now? Since you pulled away?”

Things weren’t awkward at all, everything was normal. Mydei continued his job like nothing happened, and Phainon continued to eat his words of professionalism every time he saw the man.

“No. They’re not.”

Hyacine sat upright, waving her hand in disbelief. “Let me get this straight. You almost made a move, and instead of Mydei being mad at you for it, you guys were able to move on and be normal?" That was exactly it, surely she could see the issue now. “No offense, but you are probably the only person in the world to see that as a problem.”

Guess not.

“It’s not about being normal.” It wasn’t, because normal would be Phainon simply thinking about those perverted thoughts. Now, with memory of what Mydei felt like, all he had were real urges. He always wondered if Mydei had them too. “It feels too easy. It’s like I’m waiting for the other shoe to drop.”

Hyacine furrowed her brows. “Him bringing it up?”

“Him leaving.”

Hyacine wasn’t the only one shocked by the statement.

Phainon was aware he viewed Mydei in a good light. Which was a bit of an understatement, considering he’s never met anyone like him. He would always say that Clara hit the lottery finding Mydei in the shoe store, that the universe sent him an angel after past babysitter mishaps. He knew his daughter felt the same, and it would kill her to see Mydei leave.

It hadn’t occurred to Phainon just how heavily he shared the sentiment.

He’s never had to worry about Mydei leaving before. They had a comfortable rhythm that was easy to fall into, even from week one. Phainon should’ve kept things like that.

Instead, he made things ultimately worse. For both himself and his dick.

“Phainon.” Hyacine reached forward, placing a gentle hand over his arm. “If Mydei hasn’t left already, what makes you think he will?”

Phainon wasn’t sure. He’d be willing to bet it would be due to Mydei realizing just how horny Phainon is, because apparently the latter couldn’t hide something like that.

“Intuition.”

She huffed in amusement. “Your intuition told you to hire a random guy you found at the mall, so that doesn’t count.”

Phainon smirked. “Worked out in the end though, right? And I didn’t find him, Clara did. Take that up with her intuition.” Hyacine rolled her eyes with a laugh and he kept going. “Say it’s more than Mydei leaving, though. I can not stop thinking about it. Surely that’s going to blow up in my face.”

Every time he closed his eyes, all he could envision was how soft and plump Mydei’s bottom lip felt. Instead of reaching forward to get the icing, Phainon wished he could’ve licked it up. He’d take his sweet time before finding Mydei’s mouth with his own, until they inevitably defiled every piece of furniture in the kitchen.

“Can I ask you something?”

Phainon grew hesitant. “Go ahead…”

“What do you see when you look at Mydei?”

Phainon froze, surprised by the sudden question. “Pardon?”

“Don’t be like that. You know what I’m asking you.” If Phainon was being honest, he didn’t know what she was asking. Phainon was well aware of what he saw when he laid eyes on Mydei, he just didn’t know if that’s something he should be sharing to her. Out loud. In public.

Phainon chose the safer route.

“I see the most perfect person I’ve ever met.” From Mydei’s flawless appearance, to the way he carried himself and never once dared to change for anyone’s sake. Phainon wanted him so badly, but he knew it wasn’t his place to because at the end of the day— “I see the best babysitter Clara’s ever had, and me doing nothing to take that away from her.”

He refused to take that away from her.

Hyacine pursed her lips, appearing as if she were lost in thought for a second. Phainon didn’t blame her, frankly he didn’t know what to say either.

“You’re so confusing.”

Phainon pouted. “Hey.”

“I’m serious,” she nodded. “But I get it. You haven’t thirsted over someone for who knows how long. You’re bound to be a bit of a mess. A twenty-eight year old mess, sure, but who am I to judge?”

He didn’t want to be a mess. He just wanted to be able to look Mydei in the eye without being tempted to repeat that night. “You sure do have a way with words.”

She smiled. “It’s what I do”

Phainon averted his gaze, letting everything she said register. It was a bit ridiculous, he’s been pretty stable as far as keeping to himself and his daughter. It was just his luck that the one person he’s ever needed this badly was the same person he had to keep around for Clara.

Hyacine could have had a point.

If Mydei hadn’t left already, who’s to say the other shoe will drop?

All Mydei had done was move on and act like nothing happened. It only frustrated Phainon in an overly sexual way, because he didn’t want to forget it. He didn’t think he could, and watching Mydei walk around like he didn’t try to suck Phainon’s finger was torture.

But, Phainon can see why it might have been a good thing too. If Mydei saw no reason to let it ruin what they had built, then there was no reason for Phainon to be so messed up about it.

As long as Phainon kept his urges to himself, he could be hopeful enough to think that nothing was ruined yet.

“How long have you done this?”

Mydei huffed in amusement, focusing on the section of hair he was currently braiding. Clara had come to him abruptly saying that she wanted to match with him, and who was Mydei to refuse such a request? “Since I was a kid. Probably about your age.”

Clara hummed. “Have you always had long hair?”

“I have.”

“Because it looked pretty?” Clara asked with a giggle.

Mydei simply nodded, smiling. “Sure, let’s go with that.”

He knew it was a silly thing to think about, but Mydei never imagined himself doing something like this. He’s never given himself a second to consider the idea of sharing something as little as his hairstyle with a kid, or how nice it could feel. He’s only known the girl for a month, but he didn’t see anything worth doing that could potentially break the bond they’ve built.

In hindsight, it was a good thing Phainon pulled away that night.

Nothing ever went away. Mydei still looked at him the same as before, with want for a man that could never truly act on what was there. He couldn’t, because doing so put Phainon in a position where he had to worry about the integrity of Mydei’s job. The latter didn’t see that happening, that comment about unprofessionalism was enough proof.

Still, if they weren’t able to move on from it, he might not have had the chance to sit here and do this. As sinful as his thoughts could get, he could live with them.

“You should braid daddy’s hair,” Clara suggested. “He can have a short one.”

Mydei snorted at the thought. “But then I wouldn’t be able to see him feel left out.”

“You’re right,” she said, dragging the last word out. “Okay, we will have the braids and he will have to deal with us being better than him.”

Honestly, Mydei just didn’t want to get anywhere near Phainon’s hair. Especially when all he’s wanted to do is reach out and mess it up even more. “Sounds like a plan.” He secured the band to keep the braid intact, carefully placing it against her shoulder. “Alright, all done. Do you want to go see?”

Clara shot up from the couch. “Yes! Be right back.”

Mydei watched with a soft smile as she ran to her room, the sound of the door closing behind her. Part of him really was curious as to how Phainon would react, though knowing the man, him wanting the same thing done wasn’t a far stretch. He’d try to talk his way into it until Mydei caved.

Mydei wouldn’t cave. Ultimately, Mydei would try not to budge for a lot of Phainon’s antics. Cipher’s words still burned in the back of his mind.

‘Act indifferent about it and let the man come to you.’

He wasn’t sure what the end goal was with that. All he knew was that she had a point and Mydei wouldn’t let his guard down another second. Not unless the off chance made Phainon do it first.

The sound of a key in the front door brought him out of his thoughts. From the couch, he turned his head towards the entrance, brows pressed together as he contemplated who could’ve been showing up. Phainon never stopped by when he worked, entrusting the well-being of his daughter to Mydei fully. He’s never forgotten anything either.

Mydei wasn’t sure who else had a key. Phainon was far too eager to give him one his first week, so maybe the man did the same with people he was close to.

Aglaea was in the area. He hasn’t met the woman yet, but she was a big part of their lives. Surely she had a key to his home as well. He’d know once she finally walked in, because while he hadn't seen her in person, pictures provided him with enough of an image.

Standing up with caution, just in case, he watched the door slowly open.

It… was not Aglaea.

The pink-haired woman slowly crept in, not even noticing his presence at first. Should he say something? That might startle her, and he wasn’t quite sure where to start either. This wasn’t his house and if she had a key, she had as much of a reason to be here as he did.

Mydei’s eyes widened when it finally hit him.

Phainon didn’t have a lot of pictures up on the wall, but he had a few and when Mydei had absent-mindedly asked about the woman with pink hair?

Titans, save him now.

He barely had any time to process the realization before she finally turned towards him, freezing with wide eyes. For a moment, neither one of them said a word. A small part of Mydei hoped for Clara to run back in there and make the situation less weird.

After all, this was her aunt.

“Oh my god,” the woman finally spoke, bringing a hand to her chest. “I… am so sorry, I didn’t know— I just—” Mydei wasn’t sure where the sudden apologetic tone came from. She was Phainon’s sister, why would she say sorry for showing up? “You… are obviously not Sylvia.”

Sylvia? Phainon’s old babysitter? Mydei shook his head steadily. “No, I’m not.”

“I just barged in on you. That was incredibly rude of me, wow.” Mydei still didn’t see the issue, she had more of a right than him to the place. He wasn’t acting so off guard because he didn’t want her to show up, he just hadn’t planned on meeting Clara’s aunt anytime soon. “I would’ve sent a text, I just figured… Sorry, I didn’t know Phainon was seeing someone.”

Mydei visibly recoiled.

“What?” He asked in disbelief, before quickly assuring her, “no, I’m not— It’s not like that.” Mydei blamed the door being open a second ago for why he suddenly felt so warm. Definitely not the idea of this woman seeing him as someone Phainon was involved with.

Now it was her time to appear confused. “Wait, what?” This was clearly going well, not that Mydei ever thought about how this situation could actually play out. “Are… you sure? You look like someone my brother would go crazy over.”

What.

Mydei needed a second. Or for Clara to come back. Any of the two would work just fine.

“I’m his babysitter.”

Just the babysitter.

Her eyes widened and she gaped at his words. Did she really not know? “You’re… his babysitter?”

That sounded bad. “Clara’s,” Mydei corrected, forcing away the idea of being Phainon’s. It was bad enough his brain was failing him in the presence of the man’s sister. “For a month.”

“He didn’t tell me had a new babysitter.”

From how she looked, Mydei could see that she really didn’t know. Phainon had no problem telling her about Sylvia, a woman who barely lasted two weeks, but couldn’t mention the stable sitter he’s had for a month? How the hell was Mydei supposed to take that? Not to mention it left him with the responsibility of telling the full story.

“Okay,” she continued, shaking her head. “This was a bad first impression. I’m Cyrene, Phainon’s sister. Even if I didn’t know you existed, it’s nice to meet you…”

He finished that statement for her. “Mydei. The babysitter.”

“Mydei the babysitter,” she repeated. “I would like to apologize on behalf of my brother. He can be a real pain sometimes. You would think he’d mention something like this but I guess I still have some sense to knock into him.”

For the first time that interaction, Mydei felt like he could laugh. “I’ve been trying for a month. I don’t think it’s going to happen.”

Cyrene smiled. “Definitely not.” She took a deep breath before addressing him more seriously. “I really am sorry for barging in like this. I would have sent a text, but like I said, I didn’t know he found a new babysitter.”

Obviously it was Phainon’s business, and he shouldn’t be bothered as to why the man didn’t mention it.

It sure did make him wonder, though.

“Don’t worry about it. We can just blame Phainon.”

Cyrene nodded. “You’re right. This is all his fault.”

Well, this wasn’t so bad now. Mydei still couldn’t stop remembering that, allegedly, he is someone Phainon would ‘go crazy’ over. As if Mydei hasn’t been losing his mind over the man for the better part of a month.

Mydei questioned if he should leave. He wasn’t sure what exactly she had driven a couple hours for, but she likely didn’t plan on leaving before Phainon got home. That meant Mydei wouldn’t be needed, because Clara would have her aunt to watch over her for the day.

Speaking of Clara, she finally decided to run back into the living room.

“Aunt Rene!” She exclaimed, throwing her arms around the woman. Cyrene gasped, squatting down slightly so that she could be on the child’s level before returning the hug. “I missed you.”

Cyrene pulled away enough to face her. “I missed you too, honey! How have you been?”

Clara’s smile grew as she pointed towards Mydei. “Amazing. I got a new babysitter who’s pretty much my best friend now. He even did my hair like his.” For emphasis, she picked the braided hair up to show it off. The corners of Mydei’s lips tugged upwards.

“I see that,” Cyrene said brightly, glancing back and forth between the two. More specifically, their hair. “Your dad didn’t tell me he found a new babysitter.”

The little girl put both hands on her hips. “That’s because he didn’t find him. I did, at the mall.”

Mydei froze.

“Uh,” Cyrene drawled, furrowing her brows.

Mydei offered the best he could. Considering this was all technically Phainon’s fault, he could let the man do the explaining. “It’s a long story.”

“Daddy will tell you later,” Clara added. Mydei internally thanked her.

Cyrene sighed. “I suppose. He owes me a lot of explanations anyway.”

As entertaining as it would’ve been to see her scold Phainon, Mydei couldn’t help but ask, “Should I go? I don’t want to interfere with your family time, and Phainon should be home in a few hours.”

Cyrene seemed to be taken aback by the suggestion. “Of course not! You’re the sitter, I would never try to run you out.” Mydei didn’t really see it as ‘running him out.’ He just thought he'd be able to get away from introductions that he never planned for.

Clara frowned. “Yeah, Mydei. You’re family too.” Mydei didn’t know that. Didn’t know how to process her seeing it that way, either. “You can make Aunt Rene that gnocchi me and daddy like. Then we can team up against him at the dinner table and make his life miserable.”

Mydei couldn’t say no to that, it was one of the best parts about the dinners he shared with the family.

“You can cook?” Cyrene asked.

Clara answered for him. “He’s the best at it. Daddy said when Mydei finally opens his restaurant, he will be there every day just to have Mydei’s food.”

Yet another thing Mydei was not aware of. He knew they enjoyed his cooking, Phainon had always made that known. He also knew that having a restaurant meant potentially not needing to babysit anymore and despite that, Phainon still planned on being a frequent part of his life.

How exactly was Mydei supposed to feel?

Cyrene looked down at Clara. “You guys sure did luck out then, huh?” The little girl nodded proudly. Mydei just stood there awkwardly, unaware of how to respond to all the praise. “Well, I’d be delighted to try your food as well. If you’re willing.”

Mydei couldn’t turn her down, not when Clara had talked him up so much. Doing so would just make him look bad, like he didn’t care to stick around for Cyrene. He may have not expected to see her, but she was still Phainon’s sister.

He’s just… never met the sister of a man he thirsted over, that’s all.

“Gnocchi it is,” he finally said. Clara gave him a triumphant smile, and he felt himself return the gesture. Things may be awkward but at the very least, he’d be making her happy. “I’ll run to the store and give you two time to catch up.”

To also give himself a breather, but he couldn’t add that part.

“Perfect! Don’t try to run away, either.” Mydei was aware that Cyrene only said it as a joke, though it wasn’t a bad idea. Avoid the dinner altogether and rid himself of how weird it might seem, that was doable. “We still have a grown man to blame for his terrible communication skills, remember?”

Mydei wished he could blame Phainon for a lot, actually. “Of course. Wouldn’t miss throwing him under the bus for the world.”

The woman laughed, taking a seat with Clara beside her. They fell into a conversation of their own, and Mydei grabbed his things before finally making his way to the door.

If he spent the entire ride thinking about everything Cyrene had said, that was between him and him alone. It was understandable that she didn’t know who he was, but to automatically assume it was because he was involved with Phainon? Cyrene no doubt knew her brother well enough, which meant she had said it all with full confidence.

Was that really what it looked like?

Mydei could handle being the babysitter that lusted after his boss. It’s been happening for a month, there was no way it would stop now. What he couldn’t deal with, however, is the idea of him being obvious about it.

Maybe it just looked that way at first. Mydei was standing in Phainon’s living room while the man was at work, and he clearly didn’t give off the vibe of a typical babysitter. Now that Cyrene knew the truth, hopefully she wouldn’t have to question it any further.

A long breath fell from Mydei’s lips. There was no telling how dinner would go.

Phainon felt pretty good after his conversation with Hyacine.

His issues weren’t entirely resolved, of course. He’d still go home and see Mydei, probably in front of the stove making dinner, while imagining the filthy things he’d like to do. Phainon would like to wrap his arms around the man’s torso, snaking his hand down. Just to see if Mydei could keep his composure long enough to finish the food.

Yeah, nothing was actually resolved.

But, at least he knew what he could do. It was the same thing he’s been doing the entire time, ignoring his own needs to keep everything the same. His daughter would be happy, Mydei would be happy, and all would be well.

Unfortunately, as soon as Phainon pulled into his driveway, he realized he fucked up.

Big time.

He would’ve been fine if it had been any other car, any other person, because now he was reminded of the fact that he kept such a big secret from his own family.

Cyrene was going to give him an earful.

It’s not as if refraining from telling her was personal. Phainon just didn’t know what to do when yet another babysitter he hired ended up being his best one yet. Part of him felt that voicing it out loud would jinx everything, and the situation was too good for him to risk that.

Unfortunately, Cyrene wouldn’t take that. Especially not when she’s finding out a month later.

He winced as he stepped out of his car, taking his sweet time in actually going inside. He wondered what his sister and Mydei had been talking about. Phainon had a feeling some of it would be about him, that wasn’t something Mydei just had in common with Clara. He’d definitely be outnumbered once he entered his house.

Bracing himself, he finally opened the door.

He couldn’t see anyone at first, but the faint smell of food told him where he needed to go. Any other time, he’d be fighting a smile at the idea of Mydei cooking dinner in his kitchen.

Now, he just carefully walked to the kitchen. Trying to make as little sound as he could until they inevitably noticed him.

Once he stood in the entryway, all pairs of eyes fell on him.

Great.

Phainon did his best to fake a surprised gasp. “Cyrene!” The woman remained seated, crossing her arms. Mydei just simply glanced back before focusing on the food. “It’s so good to see you. Oh! Did I mention I found a new babysitter? This is Mydei, he’s pretty great.”

Cyrene deadpanned. “What is wrong with you.”

Clara chimed in. “A lot.”

Phainon dropped the act. “I’m sorry. Before you get mad at me for not saying anything, it wasn’t on purpose.”

His sister shook her head. “I’m just trying to understand why you have a man so good he cooks for you, and this is the first I’m hearing about it.”

Phainon’s eyes went wide. Mydei looked back once more as they shared an awkward, but quick, look. Phainon didn’t know what to say to that. Cyrene had it completely wrong, Phainon didn’t ‘have’ Mydei at all. The latter just started cooking for them in the first place because Clara wanted it.

“Should I apologize again?”

Cyrene rolled her eyes. “Shame. Here I thought we told each other everything.”

How was he supposed to respond? ‘Sorry I didn’t tell you about my new babysitter, I was too busy craving him with every inch of my being?’ Like that would bode well, especially with Mydei present.

“I think the important thing here is that you two finally met, right?”

Mydei finally decided to speak. “Do you ever think.”

About you, all the time. Phainon smirked. “Of course, dear.” Mydei shook his head at the teasing. “My brain works just fine, how do you think I make all this money?”

“Oh, so you’re more than just your face?”

Phainon failed to notice the absolute confusion Cyrene displayed. “What, are you calling me pretty?”

“Idiot,” Mydei mumbled. “You sure do love hearing what you want to hear.”

What I want is to hear you. Loud and whiny, saying my name. Screaming it. “You haven’t told me no yet.”

Mydei looked back with a scowl. “Because you act like I’ve committed a grave offense when I do.”

The sound of a short cough snapped them out of their banter, reminding Phainon that Cyrene had heard everything. It didn’t mean anything, this was normal for them. She wouldn’t see it the way he did, that this was just another typical after work evening.

Mydei cleared his throat as well. “The food is done.”

On the bright side, at least Mydei was okay having dinner with Cyrene. That had to count for something.

They quickly set the table up, fixing their portions before finally allowing themselves a chance to eat. Phainon didn’t plan on the evening going like this, so he discreetly watched every interaction Mydei had with his sister. No matter how small.

Cyrene seemed fine around him. Phainon didn’t know what all had been said before, whether she knew the full story or not, but at least they got along. If anything, it was only more proof that Mydei was generally a hard person to dislike.

In Phainon’s case, that was a severe understatement.

“This is amazing, Mydei,” Cyrene said, covering her mouth as she spoke. “Clara said you planned on opening a restaurant?”

Mydei gave a short nod. “Thank you, and yes. That’s the plan.”

“I’ll have to visit one day, then.”

Phainon grinned. He felt the same, though he was fully intent on being there everyday. Anything to see the man’s face and have a taste of his cooking, even if it couldn’t happen like this anymore.

“Mydei promised I’d get discounts on every meal,” Phainon added in, giving a simple shrug. Mydei slowly turned to him, eyeing him with disbelief. “What? You don’t remember our promise?”

Mydei didn’t look away. “I remember that you’re an idiot.”

“Aw, come on. You’d make everything so good for me, though.”

Phainon regretted the words the second they came out of his mouth. Not because he didn’t mean them, but because he could sense the slight shift in Mydei’s eyes. It was barely there, but it was also hard to miss considering he’s seen that look before.

It was a look that said Mydei would make everything good for him. He’d be so, so good.

Phainon averted his gaze. “He’ll come around.” The comment was more so directed towards Cyrene. He couldn’t face Mydei right now, not when his mind was feeling rather indecent and this was technically a family dinner.

“Right,” Cyrene drawled.

Fortunately, his beloved daughter chose now to change the subject. “Aunt Rene, are you staying with us until Saturday?”

Cyrene opened her mouth to speak before sighing, offering a sad smile. “Actually, I won’t be able to go with you guys this year.”

“You’re not?” Phainon asked with concern. “Is everything okay?”

“Busy work weekend, it’s going to be hectic.” Phainon understood that, and it made him appreciate his weekends off even more. “That’s why I’m here a little earlier. I thought I'd at least try to see you guys before then.”

Clara deflated in her seat. “It’s okay. Looks like I won’t get any prizes since daddy sucks at the games.”

Phainon slightly gaped in offense but before he could make a joke about it, Cyrene continued. “Hey, why don’t you ask Mydei to go with you?”

Phainon had never seen Clara sit up so fast before.

“What’s going on?” Mydei wondered.

Phainon remained silent.

“The end of the summer carnival,” Clara answered, growing hopeful at the idea of Mydei saying yes. “Aunt Rene always goes with us, but she can’t this year. Will you go?”

“Baby, he probably doesn’t–”

“I wouldn’t want to intrude–”

Phainon and Mydei made eye contact as they spoke simultaneously. Neither one of them continued from where they stopped, and it took Cyrene giggling for them to finally look away.

“This really is quite fun.”

How delightful that this was entertaining to her. Phainon ignored that for now, addressing Mydei once again. “You don’t have to, by the way. I know the agreement was that we had you for weekdays, so I’m cool if you say no.”

Truth was, he wasn’t cool with it at all. If anything, he wanted so badly for Mydei to say yes, which was a dangerous thought. He’d pretty much be sharing a tradition with him, and that alone was enough to make Phainon want to plead for Mydei’s compliance.

There were endless possibilities. They’d walk around the park, joking back and forth with each other. They might partake in the rides in Clara’s favor, before the evening was over and once she was asleep, Phainon would offer a ride of his own. Mydei would, he’d ride all night and they’d do their best not to make a sound.

Phainon wanted him to make all the sounds.

It was never going to happen, though, so Phainon had to be ‘cool’ with it.

Mydei shook his head. “I’ve never been to it before.”

That… wasn’t a no.

Clara picked up on it as well. “Does that mean you’ll go with us?”

Phainon almost felt bad for all eyes landing on Mydei, but he’d be lying if he said he wasn’t curious himself. He would be one hundred percent willing to go even if it were just him and Clara, but he would also jump at the chance of having Mydei join. It was safe to say that his daughter felt the same.

Mydei glanced at Phainon. “Is that fine?”

“Yeah!” His eagerness made Mydei blink, and he could hear his sister snort. “Sorry, I mean yes. That’s okay. Perfect, even.”

“Nice one,” Cyrene muttered.

Mydei shrugged. “Guess I’ll go. You owe me a candied apple, though.”

Fuck.

Images of Mydei licking the glazed treat popped up in his mind.

“Mhm,” Phainon forced out. “Sure. No problem.”

He was definitely going to get an earful from Cyrene later. He had zero doubt in his heart.

Clara beamed. “I’m so happy you’re going with us. Can you match my hair with yours again Saturday? I want everyone to see it.”

Mydei’s face softened. “Of course I will.”

So fucking cute.

Phainon had obviously noticed their shared hairstyle before, but thinking about it again? It made him feel so warm, the same feeling he got every time he was reminded of how much Clara loved having Mydei around.

He was glad Mydei ended up saying yes, at least for her sake too.

They continued to eat after that, with minor conversations here and there. Phainon was also given the chance to tell Cyrene how he met Mydei, and while she might have been skeptical of his ways, at least she knew him now. That meant Phainon could skip the part where he had to explain that Mydei was an amazing person and there was no reason to be wary.

Cyrene could see it for herself.

Phainon’s seen it all along.

Phainon fell back onto the sofa with a sigh.

He had just finished putting Clara to bed, now having the time to sit down with his sister. Mydei left not too long after dinner and despite it being clear how much Cyrene wanted to talk about everything, she waited for it to just be them.

In a sense, Phainon wanted to talk about it too. He had already done it with Hyacine today, another time wouldn’t hurt.

“So,” Cyrene began, looking over at him.

“So,” Phainon parroted.

She shrugged. “He’s cute.”

“He’s beautiful.” ‘Cute’ didn’t do any justice, not with the way Phainon tended to imagine Mydei. “How does a six year old just stumble upon him like that?”

“Let’s talk about the fact that the six year old’s father let her out of his sight.”

Phainon shook his head. “Moment of weakness, it happens.” An overused excuse he had when it came to Mydei, but she didn’t need to know that. “Seriously, Rene. Sorry for not saying anything. It wasn’t intentional.”

She waved him off. “It’s fine. I think I get it now.”

“What do you mean?”

“After seeing how you two are, I can understand why you didn’t say anything.” What did that mean? Phainon liked to think he and Mydei were acting pretty normal as far as their standards went. “I think it would’ve been more questionable if he was just your babysitter.”

Phainon pressed his brows together. “He is just my babysitter.” Clara’s, if they were getting technical.

“You called him dear.”

“It was a joke.”

“Okay,” she breathed out, clearly not buying it. “Then what about you looking like you want to jump his bones? Is that a joke too?”

Phainon’s eyes went wide. “Shit, you can see that?”

“Phainon. Why would you actually admit it?”

“You asked!” Besides, she would just call him out for lying if he tried to deny it.

Cyrene laughed. “All I’m saying is that I noticed something. It wasn’t just from you, either. Either that, or I’m reading Mydei completely wrong.”

Phainon shook his head, looking away. “No, you’re not reading him wrong at all.” Phainon knew a small part of Mydei wanted him too, that night was enough evidence for him to believe so. “It’s complicated.”

Cyrene looked around before lowering her voice. “Have you two…”

“No,” Phainon said quickly. Titans, how much he loved to think about it, though. “Not at all.”

“Hm. Is it Clara you’re worried about?”

He couldn’t be surprised that she picked up on that, not with how she seemed to grasp everything else. “He’s the best babysitter she’s ever had. I’d be a pretty selfish father if I made it about what I wanted.”

“You being able to say that makes you a pretty good father, then.” Phainon let out a breath of relief, knowing she wouldn’t lie to him about something like this. “I will say, you shouldn’t sell yourself short this soon. Mydei could end up surprising you.”

“He’s already surprised me. Just by staying here this long.” Especially after what almost happened between them, when Phainon was so sure that would be what drove Mydei away.

“Hm.”

Phainon turned towards her. “What?”

“Nothing. I was just thinking.”

That wasn’t helpful at all. “Care to share?”

“Not really.” If there was one thing she loved, it was to be cryptic. She knew how much he disliked that. “Enough about my thoughts, though. You have a nice little outing to plan for.”

As much as he wanted to brush it off, she was right. He never paid it any mind when they were plans that Cyrene was a part of, because it was something he was used to. A big part of him felt like he needed to map everything accordingly, anything to ensure Mydei would have a good time.

After all, Phainon was the one lucky enough to get him on the weekend too.

It wouldn’t be like their usual routine. Mydei wouldn’t strictly be the babysitter Saturday, because Phainon would be there with him. Mydei would just be someone accompanying them, someone that held a lot of importance in their life.

That was a pretty big step for Phainon.

Naturally, he had to make it worth Mydei’s while.

Part of him wondered what Mydei was thinking right now. He hoped the man hadn’t agreed just because he felt pressured, but Mydei also wasn’t the type to do something he didn’t want to. So that could only mean he said yes because he genuinely wanted to join them, because he wanted to be a part of it just as much.

If Cyrene caught Phainon smiling to himself, she at least cut him enough slack to not mention it.

The bustling park was exactly how Phainon remembered it to be, and he felt Clara squeeze his hand in excitement.

He double checked his right to make sure Mydei seemed fine, hoping it already wasn’t too much for him. He didn’t know where Mydei stood with carnivals, but Phainon would hate to kill his mood before he even had the chance to show him a good time.

Thankfully, Mydei appeared to be okay. Phainon reached over Clara, who walked in between them, before placing a teasing hand on the man’s shoulder.

“Having fun yet?”

Mydei kept his eyes on the gesture for the briefest of moments before brushing him off with a scoff. “We just got here. Are you done asking dumb questions?”

“He always does that,” Clara said. “Just ignore him.”

Phainon moved his hand away, dramatically placing it on his heart. “Rude.” He could see Mydei shake his head in amusement, and he was glad to know things were off to a good start. Everything was normal.

“Wait, look!” Clara exclaimed, pointing out in the distance. Phainon followed her gaze, his own landing on the distant hair coloring booth. “I think I want to do that one this time.”

Phainon cocked a brow. “I thought you never cared for the hair coloring.”

“I have a new color I want to try.” She began to tug on his hand, her other one reaching out to grab Mydei’s as well. The two men exchanged a humorous look before allowing her to pull them away.

They approached the booth, and fortunately the line wasn’t too long. It only took a few minutes before it was their turn and Clara stood in front of the woman behind the table, a bright smile on her face.

“Hey there, sweetie. Want to color your hair today?”

Clara nodded. “I do.”

Phainon leaned down slightly, just enough for her to hear him over the noise. “You should do yellow and purple. I think that would look cute.” Clara turned to him slowly, expressionless, before facing the woman once more.

“I want red on the ends of my hair. Like him.”

Phainon looked over immediately, noticing the pure shock on Mydei’s face. It was so cute, cute enough to where Phainon could ignore his suggestion being brushed off. If it meant seeing his daughter match with Mydei, more than she already was, it was already worth it.

Still, he feigned offense.

“I don’t know what to say.”

The surprise wore off and Mydei shrugged. “Accept defeat with grace, Phainon.”

Oh, how he loved to hear Mydei saying his name.

“When I win you a prize later, you’ll be eating those words.”

Clara let go of their hands to round the table, sitting beside the woman as she began. It left Phainon next to Mydei, the two silently stepping close together to fill the space Clara left.

Mydei furrowed his brows. “Last I heard, you weren’t that good at these games.”

“He’s not,” Clara agreed.

Phainon didn’t relent. It didn’t matter if he was good at the games or not, he’d keep trying if it meant Mydei calling him a winner. Phainon wanted to hear Mydei call him a lot of things, actually.

“It’s the hair color fumes messing with her brain. She doesn’t know what she’s saying.” Clara sucked her teeth at him but said nothing else. “By the way,” Phainon added, addressing the woman. “Is this stuff safe?”

She nodded firmly, focused on the task in front of her. “Absolutely. It’s temporary, too.”

“Dang,” Clara muttered.

“It’s okay,” Phainon assured. “We can buy some more later. Maybe we can get purple and yellow, too.”

Clara side-eyed him. “Mydei. Tell him to stop.”

Fine. See if he ever offers another harmless suggestion again.

Mydei snorted. “You heard her. Quit threatening people with your terrible sense of design. We’re trying to have a good time.”

This time, it was the woman who found amusement in the situation. “I hear a lot of conversations between families, but this is definitely one of my favorites.”

Despite how loud the carnival was, Mydei and Phainon remained silent.

Phainon didn’t see it at first, but he could faintly pick up on Clara smiling when she heard those words.

The silence didn’t last long when the woman had set the spray can down, slowly removing the cape she used to cover Clara’s clothes. She held a mirror out for the little girl to see, and Phainon’s heart swelled when he saw how ecstatic it made her.

“I look just like Mydei.”

“You do,” Phainon said. “You look pretty, baby.”

Clara looked at Mydei, almost nervously. “Do you like it?” Phainon faced him as well, picking up on the slight reddish hue of his face. Maybe it was the sun, it was later in the day but still pretty warm.

Or maybe it was the fact that Phainon essentially called Mydei pretty too. He wasn’t going to take it back, though.

Mydei nodded. “You make it look better than I do.”

Phainon exhaled dramatically. “I’m feeling a little left out, guys.”

Mydei and Clara shared a look before the former spoke. “Told you.”

Clara giggled, thanking the woman before returning to her spot between them. Phainon politely thanked her as well, paying for the service before they moved on to their next destination.

A lot of their stops consisted of things Clara laid her eyes on, which Phainon and Mydei were happy to comply with. As much as Phainon wanted to worry about Mydei feeling out of place, he never gave him a reason to and eventually, those doubts just stopped.

Now, they acted like this was the most normal thing in the world.

If Phainon was lucky, it could be. Cyrene would be able to join next time, and Mydei would officially be a part of the tradition.

It was a nice thought.

The three of them played whatever games they came across, having to buy more vouchers each time considering none of them had lucked out yet. The prizes weren’t all that worth it, but Phainon was determined to get something. At least that way he’d be proving the other two wrong.

They approached their next booth, and Phainon could already feel the dread. He hated ring toss, always thought it was rigged, and knew there was no way he’d win anything. He would just have to hope that the prizes didn’t interest Clara or Mydei that much.

Much to his dismay, that was not the case at all.

“Look, it’s a chimera.” Clara pointed to the plush, a large version of the ones she liked to collect. “That’s bubbles. You should get him”

Mydei tilted his head. “He is pretty cute.”

Great, because the idea of Mydei finding it cute was cute itself, and now Phainon felt obligated. His mouth moved faster than his brain.

“I bet I can win it.”

The two of them turned to him, unimpressed. Mydei huffed, crossing his arms. “You have flunked every single game up to this point. I highly doubt that.”

“Three rounds,” Phainon said simply, nodding towards the booth. “You and me. Can you handle that?”

Mydei’s expression had shifted. It was a faint thing, but Phainon noticed. It was difficult not to since this wasn’t the first time it’s happened. “I can handle three rounds, Phainon.”

Fuck, what were they even talking about anymore.

“Can you?”

Mydei took a step closer. “Maybe if you quit hesitating to start.”

“I’m not hesitating.” He was hesitating, but not about the game. If that’s what this was even about, it was hard to tell.

“Sure looks that way to me. Scared I might be able to handle you?”

Titans, Phainon wanted so badly to think about it. To wonder if Mydei could really back his words up, handling everything Phainon unleashed on him. His breath trembled when Phainon only touched his lip, Phainon was confident he could make him fall apart with more.

“Wait, so does the winner get the plush?”

Clara’s voice was enough to snap Phainon out of it.

Slightly ashamed, he shook his head. “Mydei can keep it, because I’ll be the winner anyway.”

“You’re on.”

They both took a step forward, deciding that Phainon would go first to start their competition.

After two rounds, it appeared as if neither one of them would be winning. Phainon blamed it on the game, surely Mydei could see it was rigged too. He hadn’t said anything, so it was either that or he was frustrated with himself.

It was cute watching Mydei look so focused.

“Last round,” Phainon announced, preparing his rings. “I expect high praise when all of this is over.”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “Quit yapping and just throw the thing.”

Phainon laughed, getting into position. He narrowed his eyes, carefully calculating the precision of his throw. He counted down in his head, partially confident that this would be the time he won.

“This competition looks pretty intense.”

Phainon jerked his head to the side the second he made the toss. There was no telling where the ring went, but all he could focus on was the man who now stood beside Mydei. Too close, too comfortable, like he had no regard for personal space at all.

Who the hell was this.

“Apparently not,” Mydei responded, gesturing towards Phainon’s excuse of a throw. The latter still hadn’t been bothered to check how he did. “He didn’t even hit a bottle.”

The unknown man sucked in a breath through his teeth. “Wow. Guess I’m cheering for the right side, then.”

Excuse him?

Phainon could care less about what some random man thought of his ring toss abilities. It was a rigged game that always had a higher chance of losing. What he cared about was Mydei seeming to share the same belief, and this stranger having the audacity to use that belief as a pick-up line.

Phainon’s jaw clenched and he forced a smile. “Alright, Mydei. It's your turn.”

Mydei looked at him in disbelief. “What about the rest of your tosses?”

Frankly, Phainon didn’t feel like being used for this man's joke. Especially when all he was trying to do was flirt. “Oh, come on. You know I could only win if I made all three.”

“I guess,” Mydei muttered, getting into position. “You were awfully competitive about the chimera a second ago.”

And now I just want to get you away from this man, who is still so close to you.

Phainon remained silent, watching as Mydei prepared to make his tosses as well. Just like the last times, they all missed, but Mydei didn’t seem bothered anymore. He simply shrugged it off, before turning to the man instead of Phainon.

“Hope you didn’t make any bets on me,” Mydei teased.

He’s teasing him. He’s teasing someone that isn’t Phainon when that’s quite literally all he does.

“Don’t worry about it,” the stranger said. “If I’m lucky enough to find you again tonight, I’ll still be rooting for you.”

Did Phainon say he hated ring toss? What he meant to say was he despised it, and if he never had the ability to participate in the game again, he would be considered lucky.

“Can we go to a different game?” Clara asked, and Phainon’s irritation dissipated long enough for him to look down in surprise. She grabbed a hold of his hand, giving an intent glare towards the man that stood beside Mydei. “I’m bored of this one.”

Ice cream for dinner for a year. He could promise her that right now.

Mydei eventually stepped away. “Yeah, let’s go.” Mydei gave the man a short nod as a farewell, and Phainon was forced to watch the pleased look that earned him in response. He wasted no time in leading them far away from the booth.

If Mydei could pick up on the sudden mood change, he didn’t say anything about it. If anything, he looked content with himself and part of Phainon wondered if that was on purpose. That Mydei miraculously had an idea of how it would affect Phainon.

How interesting.

Phainon stored that away, swallowing it down for now so that they could enjoy the rest of the night. It was him and Clara that Mydei was spending time with, no one else.

Especially not that stranger.

It didn’t take long for things to fall back into the normal rhythm. They played a few more games before moving onto rides, though Phainon and Mydei sat most of them out. A lot were catered towards children, so they didn’t mind standing off to the side as Clara had her fun.

The sun had already gone down by now, but they still roamed the area full of energy, trying to get the most of the experience. Phainon was relieved to know Mydei’s mood wasn’t dimming any, pleased that the man enjoyed the day as much as he and Clara did.

There wasn’t much else to do, they had already covered everything that interested them. It was clear that they were in no hurry to leave, so no one mentioned anything about it yet.

“Is that a photobooth?” Clara asked, letting go of Mydei’s hand long enough to point.

The blond hummed. “I think it is.”

Phainon chimed in. “Should we take a picture?”

“Yes,” Clara answered with zero hesitation, dragging them towards the booth. Phainon and Mydei simply let it happen. They pushed aside the curtains so they could step in, the bench inside only being big enough to fit the two men. Clara didn’t seem to mind, sitting in the middle atop both of their laps.

Phainon glanced over. “Are you photogenic, Mydei?” He already knew the answer to that himself, he was just too eager to mess with him. Phainon received a lot of pictures of Mydei with Clara, pictures that just so happened to end up in his camera roll.

“Hush. You’re distracting.”

The screen lit up, providing them with the countdown. They weren’t able to see a preview of themselves, so all Phainon could do was hope everyone was in frame. Even if it was only three pictures, he wanted everything to be captured perfectly.

The first one was normal, smiles on all of their faces. He assumed Mydei's smile wasn’t as big, but it would be visible enough for Phainon to tell it was genuine. On the other hand, he and Clara were grinning ear to ear.

The second picture was a less serious one. Clara and Mydei held up peace signs, Phainon doing so as well but behind his daughter’s head. He was sure she wouldn’t notice, not until the photos finally got printed.

The second the last count down appeared, Phainon allowed himself to look at their next pose.

Clara held her hands out in a clawing motion, and Phainon held back a laugh when Mydei did the same. They seemed to be mimicking cats, which is something he never envisioned Mydei doing. Phainon couldn’t look away, not when the two beside him acted so naturally with each other. Like their bond was more than just Mydei simply being Clara’s caretaker.

Phainon felt his smile slowly fade the longer he stared, realization washing over his face. Hyacine’s voice rang through his ears.

“What do you see when you look at Mydei?”

A future.

The camera shutter went off immediately.

Phainon quickly looked away, aware that they would see him failing to pose once the pictures came out. He didn’t care, because all he could think about was the fact that he just admitted, albeit to himself, that he wanted Mydei in his life for the long run.

Not just as Clara’s babysitter.

He followed leisurely behind as they made their way out of the booth, standing by the side as they waited. Phainon said nothing, watching as the slip finally appeared. Clara reached forward to grab the photos, and Mydei leaned down to get a look as well.

Phainon remained in place.

She huffed. “Daddy, you weren’t even looking at the camera in this one.”

Mydei noticed it too. Him avoiding eye contact was an indication of that. “Sorry,” was all Phainon could offer, giving a short laugh. “I wanted to see what pose you two were doing.”

Mydei finally looked at him, the two of them sharing a knowing look. Clara only kept her eyes on the pictures, like it was the most precious thing in the world to her. She brought them to her chest.

“I’m keeping these.”

His slip up aside, Phainon wished there was another copy. He’d jump at the chance to keep them, too. “Have at it. Hey Mydei, can you stand with her for a second? I need to find the bathroom.”

And to think about how this isn’t just lust anymore.

“Yeah, I’ll be here.”

Phainon wanted him to mean that in the general sense too.

He nodded, walking off to find the nearest restroom. He wasn’t sure if he actually needed to go, or to allow himself a chance to realize what had happened.

Phainon wasn’t expecting to suddenly figure everything out in a photobooth.

He wanted Mydei. Not just in the way where he craved him, he wanted Mydei in his life. To not only be the babysitter he hired, but someone who is a constant part of his future. Someone that continued getting close with Clara, being there for her when Phainon couldn’t. He wanted them to never stop poking fun at him. He wanted to always come home to Mydei, to have his way with him at night before waking up to him every morning.

Trying to brush all that aside would be damn near impossible.

He should probably reach out to Hyacine. Or even Cyrene.

Unfortunately, he wouldn’t get the chance to reach out to anyone. Not when the man from earlier was now walking up to him.

Phainon could have ignored it if it weren’t for the chimera plush in his hands.

“There you are,” the man said, approaching him with a laugh. “I’ve been looking everywhere for at least one of you.”

Come again?

Phainon feigned ignorance. “Have we met?”

“Uh,” the man drawled, slightly confused. “From earlier? At the ring toss booth? I remember the man who was with you wanting this plush, so a few games later, I finally managed to snag it.”

‘A few games later.’

Did he seriously keep playing just to win Mydei that prize?

Phainon eyed the plush with annoyance. He didn’t realize his feelings a second ago just to accept the stupid thing, willingly giving Mydei a gift someone else won for him. He could think of a hundred other things he would rather do.

“Wow,” was all Phainon could say. His expression was nothing short of dry and fake, praying to the Titans that the man could pick up on that. “You have a really good memory.”

“Thank you, I—”

Phainon’s face fell flat. “Get rid of it.”

The man went still, a dumbfounded expression on his face. “Excuse me?”

Phainon shrugged nonchalantly. “He doesn’t want it anymore. Sorry.”

The stranger shot him a look of contempt, one that failed to have its desired effect. “Did he tell you that himself?”

“No, but he hasn’t brought it up once since we left the booth.” Which was true, Phainon wasn’t lying about that. Mydei had probably forgotten about the chimera, and this was not the way Phainon would remind him of it. “Guess he didn’t care for it that much.”

The man scoffed, glancing down at the plush before shaking his head. “Whatever, dude.”

That was all Phainon got before he was left alone.

Oh well.

However, Phainon needed to do something. Screw his bathroom visit, he could save the thinking for later. If someone who Mydei didn’t even know could make an attempt like that, Phainon just had to do one better. He wanted to be the one to surprise Mydei.

His eyes caught what he was looking for, and he stalked towards the food truck intently.

“Hello sir, what can I get for you?”

Phainon didn’t hesitate.

“Two candy apples, please.”

Mydei held the picture in his hands as they waited for Phainon to return.

Back in the booth, he never realized Phainon’s eyes were on him and Clara. It was hard to read what they were saying, just that they were intense enough for Mydei to feel awkward. He couldn’t ask Phainon about it either, that would probably bring up a conversation that neither of them should have tonight.

It was a good thing Mydei didn’t notice Phainon looking before. That stare would’ve done things to Mydei that he didn’t want to consider right now.

He returned the photos back to Clara when he caught sight of Phainon coming back, his gaze narrowing in on the two objects in his hand. Phainon held them up, showing them off with a cocky smirk and Mydei couldn’t hold back his snort.

Of course.

“You seriously got candy apples.”

“What can I say?” Phainon handed one to him, before giving the other to his daughter. “I have a really good memory.”

Mydei ignored the photobooth incident, just until he could get home and think about it alone. “If it gets you to sleep at night.”

“So, what’s next?”

In all honesty, Mydei had been following them the whole time and he wasn’t looking to stop any time soon. Tonight had been a lot of fun for the three of them, giving Mydei a chance to experience how they were when he didn’t have to be a babysitter.

It wasn’t all that different.

He acted the same with them then as he did now, which meant lines were starting to blur and Mydei wasn’t sure what was going on anymore. He wasn’t sure if wanting more outings like this was right of him, because he wasn’t obligated to be included in their family. No matter how much Clara said he was.

No matter how much he wanted Phainon, either.

That’s why he was fine letting them call all of the shots. He didn’t know what to do.

Clara yawned. “I’m kinda tired.”

Phainon nodded, taking a step forward to squat down a little. “I figured. Up you go, boss.” Mydei’s lips parted when Phainon lifted her effortlessly, holding her up with one arm. He couldn’t help but wonder what else that big arm could do on its own.

Mydei had to look away. Seeing Phainon carrying her like that did crazy things to his mind.

“Are you fine if we head out?” Phainon asked.

Mydei would be glad to get home in the comfort of his own bedroom, yes. Very much so. “She’s the one in charge.”

Phainon seemed content with that answer, expression soft as he led them towards the parking lot. Mydei followed a few paces behind, giving himself the luxury to watch the man.

He wouldn’t be free of it yet. It was Phainon’s idea to take the same car, meaning he’d have to sit in the passenger seat just until they made it back to his house. With Clara half asleep, there was bound to be silence between them. Considering where Mydei’s head was at, it was also bound to be awkward.

Once they were all situated in the vehicle, Mydei turned his head and faced the window. He’d gladly stare outside if it meant avoiding a conversation.

Phainon didn’t seem to get the memo. After a few moments where neither one of them said anything, his voice finally filled the car.

“Did you have a good time?”

At least it was a question Mydei could answer. “Sure. Watching you fumble every game was a treat.”

“At least I got you that treat.” He pointed towards the candy apple in Mydei’s hand for emphasis. “You haven’t eaten it, yet.”

Last time Mydei ate something sweet in front of Phainon, it ended up with the latter’s thumb almost in his mouth. Mydei hasn’t touched a dessert in his presence since, and he wouldn’t start now. He was just lucky the apple was still wrapped up.

“Sweets make me tired. I still need to drive.”

Phainon hummed. “I didn’t know that.”

“Now you do. Don’t worry, it’ll get eaten.”

Phainon smirked. “How will I know?”

The nerve of this man. “What, am I supposed to show you proof?”

“Can you?” Phainon asked, clearly just trying to mess with Mydei more. What was he supposed to do, send Phainon pictures of him licking the apple when he got home? Absolutely not.

“You’re ridiculous,” Mydei muttered, though there was no malice in his tone. Just a deflection of his own thoughts, because now he imagined what Phainon would say if he did send that picture.

Warmth crept through him at the idea of Phainon potentially saving it to his camera roll.

Neither one of them said anything for the rest of the ride, which thankfully wasn’t that long.

Mydei had never been so glad to see Phainon’s driveway in his life.

They exited the car at the same time, Mydei standing idly by as Phainon picked Clara up into his arms again. She was sound asleep, she has been since the car ride, so Mydei made sure to make as little noise as possible.

“Are you leaving now?” Phainon whispered, securing his hand around his daughter.

Mydei shook his head. “Not yet. I’ll make sure she gets to bed okay first.”

Phainon froze, staring at him with an unreadable expression. Eventually, he nodded in response and made his way inside.

Mydei stayed true to his word and ensured Clara remained asleep before he left, witnessing firsthand what it looked like when Phainon put her to bed. He had tenderly caressed her head before he leaned in, planting a gentle kiss on top of it. Mydei could only stand there, feeling that all too familiar dizziness.

Once they had finished, it was Mydei’s turn to lead the way towards the door. He hadn’t planned on Phainon following him there, but he made no attempt to stop him as they walked in silence.

Not saying anything was worse. Mydei turned around before he could reach for the knob.

“Yes.”

Phainon paused, tilting his head. “Yes, what?”

Mydei sighed. “I did have a good time today.”

Phainon’s face softened. “Me too. I’m sure Clara would say the same if she were awake.” Mydei liked to think so too, he had enough confidence in their relationship by now. “Be careful getting home. It’s, uh… dark and all.”

“Your father instincts are showing, old man.”

As if they haven’t been showing all day, driving Mydei mad.

Phainon chuckled. “I’m not that much older than you.”

“But you still are,” Mydei retorted. “If you keep this up, I might have to start calling you sir.”

He could tell he immediately made a mistake.

Not entirely a bad mistake, but one he promised not to make again, because now Phainon’s demeanor had shifted. He took Mydei’s words the way Mydei partially intended for them to sound, and it was too late to take it back.

Phainon’s voice got lower. “I wouldn’t say no.”

Mydei’s breath caught in his throat. He tried his best to remain impassive about the whole thing, but with Phainon looking at him like that, there was only so much he could do. “That… wouldn’t be very professional of you.”

“You’re right.” Phainon took a couple steps closer, lessening the distance between the two of them. Mydei didn’t move, even when he knew the literal exit out of this conversation was behind him. “A small part of me did mean that, you know. About being unprofessional.”

Mydei never doubted that a bit. “And the other part?” He questioned, his voice barely above a whisper.

Phainon leaned his head forward just enough to position himself more in Mydei’s space, those dark eyes boring into his own. Mydei tried with every fiber of his being to look away, but something about the man kept reeling him back in.

“The other part is tired of acting like I don’t want to keep you here. All night.”

A gasp forced its way from Mydei’s lips. He finally managed to look up. “Phainon…”

There was nothing else for him to say. He was standing right here, and if this is what Cipher meant by letting Phainon make the first move? It was his for the taking. All he needed was for Phainon to let that other part of him win, so he could stop making both of them wait.

It was never going to be that easy. Not with how sudden Phainon looked away.

“Goodnight, Mydei. Be careful out there.”

He was running from it, it was clear as day. He told Mydei exactly what he wanted and while it was vague, Mydei gave him no other reason to hesitate.

Mydei didn’t trust himself to speak, only offering a half assed nod before opening the door. He could sense Phainon watching him as he left, but he didn’t have it in him to double check. It was late, and the last thing they needed was to have another moment in Phainon’s entryway.

His head wasn’t exactly in the right place either during the drive home. It was a wonder the trip had gone smoothly.

Fortunately, it did, and Mydei was back at his apartment in no time. He could go inside and recall everything that happened today, right down to Phainon’s implicit confession on something they were both aware of. Mydei knew he wouldn’t drop the unprofessional excuse so quickly, he just needed to hear Phainon say the truth out loud.

That he wanted Mydei just as badly.

Mydei flopped down onto his bed, growing wet at the thought.

Phainon should have acted on it. He should’ve made good on his words and kept Mydei there, having his way with him for the entire night. Mydei wouldn’t have been prepared for the impromptu stay, but it’s not like it hasn’t happened before. He would figure it out, he’d do anything if it meant feeling those hands on him.

And those big, strong arms.

Mydei turned towards the packaged candy apple that laid beside him.

How silly.

Yet, he picked his phone up immediately.

He shouldn’t say anything about it. He should save it for later, or maybe pawn it off to Cipher. She’d probably steal it from him if she were here anyway.

Mydei just had to know.

Mydei: still want that proof?

He doubted Phainon would answer right now. If anything, the man probably went to bed himself the second Mydei left. Phainon waking up to it wasn’t any better, but at least tomorrow was still the weekend. Mydei had a day break before he had to see him again.

A day break that evidently wasn’t needed. Mydei pursed his lips once he noticed Phainon started typing back.

It felt like forever had passed when the text finally came through.

Phainon: Go ahead and send that proof for me.

Fuck.

Fuck, Mydei was so weak.

Mydei: yes sir.

Cipher would hate him right now.

His arm shot out to grab the candy apple, opening the treat at a pace that could’ve been considered ridiculous. He didn’t care, because he got the go ahead and all he wanted to do was make this the best picture Phainon has ever received.

Mydei positioned himself, laying against the pillows as he held his phone camera above his head. The angle might’ve been a bit suggestive, but that seemed to be their thing anyway and he doubted Phainon would mind. He brought the apple to his mouth, tongue darting out to lick at the sugary coating.

Looking through the reflection, Mydei realized it was a bit too much. Phainon would be able to see his entire face, and they hadn’t made it to that point yet. Right now, they were just dancing around each other.

He brought the phone closer, only capturing the bottom part of his face. Deciding that this was the better choice, he stuck his tongue out a little more.

He could at least give Phainon that much.

Mydei snapped and sent the photo before he could change his mind, contemplating if he should shut the device off completely or wait. Phainon was quick to respond before, but Mydei didn’t know if he wanted to see the message yet. It could give him something to look forward to in the morning.

If Mydei even managed to sleep.

He decided just to wait, the typing bubbles preventing him from doing the opposite. He’s already made it this far, might as well see the kind of reaction it earned him. Knowing Phainon, it would be exactly what Mydei wanted.

Phainon: There you go.

Mydei squeezed his phone.

Phainon: Goodnight Mydei. Sleep well.

It was a sweet comment, really, but one that definitely was unnecessary because Mydei was right.

There was no way he’d get to sleep tonight.
