chapters.title: Chapter 5: Liquid Courage
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei had way too much to think about, and Phainon had way too much to contribute to that.

Chapter Notes

Uh oh is that plot in my dilf phainon babysitter mydei fic...

Normally, Mydei was someone who tried to live without regret.

He was fully aware of the choices he made, accepting responsibility for the result of any. There was no reason to consider what would happen if he chose something else, because there was no way to reverse the outcome. Would he often find himself wondering where he might have ended up? Sure, but that was natural and it’s not like it filled him with existential dread.

So yeah, Mydei was not that regretful.

Not even with how easy things were before he took this babysitting gig.

Maybe things would have been fine if Phainon wasn’t… Phainon. Mydei has never been drawn to someone like this before, so it was safe to say that anyone else wouldn’t have the same effect. He would be able to make it through a day, tending to his duties without ever mulling over things he shouldn’t. His boss wouldn’t be at the front of every fantasy he’s ever had since getting hired.

That just simply wasn’t the case, because Phainon was Phainon.

He was someone who could do terrible things to Mydei’s brain, whether it was intentional or not. Mydei never got a break, even when Phainon could be as ridiculous as the first day he met him. Even when he could sense Mydei’s sudden changes, dropping his own voice to match the mood.

Even when he was simply just himself, interacting with his daughter right in front of Mydei’s face.

It was a lot, more than Mydei could handle.

Phainon didn’t make it any better either.

He could indulge Mydei one day and act like it hadn’t happened the next, treating him as if he didn’t almost stick a thumb in the latter’s mouth. As if he didn’t receive a picture from Mydei of him suggestively licking a candy apple, because yeah, he never brought it up since. Despite the fact that it’s been a week.

Mydei still wonders what exactly Phainon did with the photo.

He’s also never going to ask.

It was easy when the rational part of his brain knew that Phainon was ignoring it for a reason. That his place as Clara’s father — and Mydei’s boss — came above whatever potential there could be for anything else. Mydei would never admit it out loud, but the other part of him grew rather selfish by hoping the man would do something.

By this point, it was hard to imagine Phainon making the first move.

It didn’t make it any easier that Mydei couldn’t see himself doing it either, knowing firsthand what Phainon could do when they had a moment. How quick he could pull away and brush it off.

The thing is, rejection and brushing a subject off were two different things. At least that’s how Mydei viewed it.

Which is why he’d never initiate first.

He had to remind himself that he wasn’t in this situation for Phainon. He wasn’t getting paid to constantly question what the hell they had going on. If that were the case, he would’ve considered walking away to save him the trouble. No matter how much he was drawn to the man.

Standing where he was right now, watching Clara as she ran around the playground, he knew he could never walk away. He had no reason to.

Because his relationship with Phainon — as blurry as it could be — wasn’t the only thing established right now. She was equally as important and Mydei had gotten so used to her presence that anything different wouldn’t feel right. Clara and Phainon were a packaged deal, so he’d gladly deal with the confusion if it meant spending more time like this with her.

He wasn’t sure if getting so attached was usual for babysitters.

Mydei kept his eyes on her at all times, watching with a small smile as she interacted with the other kids. She was Phainon’s daughter through and through, so it made sense why she was such a social butterfly. It was just another resemblance that the two of them had.

He seemed to notice a new one everyday.

Mydei couldn’t remember how long they had been at the park, though he was too content to pay it any mind. They had plenty of time to kill before Phainon got off work, so he would happily sit there if it meant Clara enjoying herself.

It would just be better if he could think about anything else, rather than blue eyes and stupid, white messy hair.

“Mydeimos…?”

Mydei really should be careful what he wished for.

He didn’t turn his head at first, not even as the person who spoke approached him beside the bench. He didn’t have to, he could recognize that voice from anywhere. No other sound could fill him with so much guilt as that one.

Even if he hasn’t heard it in three years.

Mydei looked to his left, slowly meeting eyes with his mother. She was exactly as he remembered. Not appearance wise, it would be hard for her to drastically change in just a few years. She was no different because she still looked at him with that same gentle expression. The one that never once faded from his memory.

Mydei felt a pit form in his stomach.

“Mom,” he whispered, hoping it hadn’t gone unheard beneath the sounds coming from the park. Saying the word alone was enough to have him feel speechless, he wasn’t sure if he could repeat it.

Gorgo offered him a smile. “My son. I can’t believe it.”

He couldn’t either, and why was she being so nice to him? Mydei left, cut contact just to prove a point to both his parents and himself. Granted she had only a small part to play, but why would she look at him with anything other than resentment?

Mydei opened his mouth to speak, but nothing came out.

Luckily, she took the incentive for him. “I come to this park almost everyday, it makes me wonder why I’m just seeing you now.”

That’s because Mydei didn’t visit the park frequently, only when Clara got the urge, so—

Shit.

Quickly averting his gaze, Mydei made sure Clara was still visible. He sighed in relief when he saw her small frame running around, laughing with two other kids her age. He couldn’t live with himself if something happened all because his mothers presence rendered him speechless.

Which brings him back to his current predicament.

He should probably say something else.

“Do… you want to sit?” He gestured towards the space beside him, unsure if she’d take his offer or not. Sitting implied talking, and frankly he didn’t know what they could discuss right now. As if a few minutes in the park would ever be enough to cover three years of radio silence.

Much to his surprise, she smiled again. “I would, actually.”

Maybe it wasn’t that much of a surprise. She was who she always had been, rejecting his offer would’ve been out of character. Even despite how long they had gone without speaking.

Mydei watched carefully as she sat beside him, tensing up all the while. There was a tiny voice in the back of his head telling him to relax, because this was his mother and he was never the kind of person to feel awkward in her presence.

In reality, he was just the kind of person who ran away from family.

He remembered the words Clara told him that day.

‘It’s okay. I'm sure it wasn’t your fault.’

She was too good to him.

“You can admit this is weird,” Gorgo said, giving him a knowing smirk. Everything was too natural for her, yet Mydei suddenly felt aware of every move he made. “I honestly wasn’t expecting an invite to join you.”

Mydei didn’t really expect it either. He shook his head, looking away. “It’s not weird.”

“Mydeimos.” That voice. That maternal voice that Mydei’s heard far too many times, the same one she used when she knew he was lying. Apparently a couple years isn’t enough time to break something like that. “At least try not to avoid eye contact if you want me to believe you.”

Besides Cipher and Castorice, she was the only person in the world who could pick up on something like that.

He couldn’t help but think about how fortunate it was that Phainon didn’t share the same ability.

“Sorry,” he muttered, rubbing his arm sheepishly.

Gorgo sat back, taking a deep breath. “It’s alright, I suppose. It’s one of the easier things I can forgive you for.”

Shit.

Mydei refused to meet eyes with her again. She was quick to notice. “It was only a joke,” she continued, and he looked up to see if her face could back the claim. She didn’t appear upset, she still smiled at him like he had done no wrong so maybe it was a good sign. Gorgo shook her head teasingly. “You always did have to have those explained to you. So serious as a child, and for what?”

In his defense, he felt too much guilt to even consider joking around. “Blame father. Got it from him.”

She laughed at that, but he was being one hundred percent serious.

“Don’t even get me started. That man can be a real buzzkill.”

Mydei didn’t know how to respond. He furrowed his brows, unaware of what she had been getting at. She knew the reason he left, clearly she wouldn’t try making a joke about his father at Mydei’s expense. He hadn’t even planned on discussing that man today.

Luckily, she was quick to notice the curiosity on his face as well.

“Mydeimos.” Her voice grew softer, and never once did that motherly expression falter, even when Mydei barely contributed anything to the conversation. “I’m not here to scold you. I didn’t sit down so I could make you feel guilty for anything.” Too late for that. “You don’t have to look at me like I’m a stranger.”

That was easier said than done. Mydei cut contact without considering how seeing her again would go, it was only natural for him to be wary of it. To approach it with caution since he never knew how she felt about his decision.

“Are you angry?”

Because he had to know.

Gorgo huffed in amusement. “Angry. Please, you did nothing for me to feel angry about.”

That’s not the way he saw it. Mydei excused the reasons for his own sake, but that didn’t mean his parents were bound to feel the same. “I left.”

“You did what you needed to do.”

What?

“I…” Mydei trailed off, a dumbfounded expression on his face. How long did it take for her to come to that conclusion? She never said much when all he felt was pressure from his father, so it was hard to believe that she always thought that. Hearing something like that back then could have saved him all the trouble.

Not that he hated where he ended up, but the small ‘what-if’ was there.

Mydei never got the chance to finish his thought when he heard the sound of his name being called out. He turned his head, watching as Clara ran up to him with a full grin on her face.

He could almost feel his mother’s eyes on him.

“Mydei, look,” Clara managed to get out through heavy breaths. She brought her arm up, showing off a singular flower she had picked up. “I was at the bushes and— Oh.” She stopped when she noticed Mydei’s mother, glancing back and forth between them. “I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to interrupt.”

Mydei smiled softly. “It’s alright.” Frankly, he could use the moment where things felt normal. “Is that an azalea?”

“It is!” Clara exclaimed, beaming once more. “You said they have different meanings, but one is family. So I want to give it to you.” Mydei felt a lump in his throat. Considering how he left his family once before, he didn’t deem himself worthy of it. “Lean down, I’ll put it in your hair.”

However, he could never say no to her.

Mydei leaned forward, slightly angling his head so that she could tuck it behind his ear. She made sure it was secure before stepping back to admire her work. “Pretty.”

“Thank you. I’ll cherish it forever.”

Clara shrugged. “You can just keep it for a while. It will wither away eventually.”

Most things tended to do that.

“For a while, then,” he agreed.

She nodded, her grin slowly fading when she met eyes with Gorgo again. Mydei could tell she wanted to ask about the woman, or maybe she already knew, but it never came. Instead, “do you want me to give you time to talk? I won’t interrupt again, I promise.”

She didn’t have to promise that. Nothing she did ever felt like an interruption. “Stay in my line of sight, okay?”

“Okie dokie,” she agreed before running back off

The seconds that passed after felt excruciatingly long. Nothing else was said for a moment, and Mydei still hadn’t faced his mother yet.

“Well,” she began. “I know it’s been three years, but I can’t say I was expecting that..”

Mydei’s eyes widened.

He finally turned to her, noticing the humorous yet endearing look she wore. He had no idea how she was perceiving his interaction with Clara, but he knew he should clear the air right away. It almost felt like an obligation to state what he was to the little girl.

What he would always be, at this rate.

Mydei shook his head. “It’s not— that’s just the kid I babysit.”

“Hey, I didn’t say anything.” She didn’t have to, he could tell she might have considered Clara to be his own. It wasn’t a shameful assumption, but it was one that he was in no place to even consider. It wasn’t his right, and would be no one’s right until Phainon was the one to make that call.

Mydei sighed. “It’s not a long-standing thing. It’s only been a little over a month.”

“I think it’s nice,” his mother said. “It’s sweet to see, I always knew you had a soft spot for kids.” Which was funny, considering he hadn’t even known that until he started watching Clara. “I will say though, the azalea is a bit… interesting.”

He furrowed his brows. Was it because of what Clara said? “I’m at their house everyday. It’s not odd that she associates that with family.” He wasn’t even sure why he was deflecting on this. Mydei’s never minded it before, and he certainly doesn’t mind it now.

Gorgo smiled. “It’s not that.” Mydei thought back to all of the meanings, his mind coming up blank on what could’ve caught her attention. “In some places, the familial meaning is more specific. Tied to parental-love, mainly motherly-love.”

Mydei didn’t know what to say, but staying silent wouldn’t help his case so he at least tried. “That… makes it interesting because she gave it to me?” Clara couldn’t have known that, Mydei only briefly went over meanings when they came across the flower in passing. If she ever learned that additional fact, then it wasn’t from him.

“Hm?” She questioned, tilting her head. “No, I don’t mean in your case. I found it interesting because I came across you in the park today. Bit of a coincidence, don’t you think?”

Right.

Mydei being associated with parental-love. Of course that wouldn’t even be a thought.

“Oh.”

She laughed to herself. “I’m surprised you don’t remember. You once put one in my hair when you were a child.” He didn’t remember, but he wasn’t going to voice that out loud and confirm her suspicion. “Anyway, I've taken enough of your time. I didn’t realize you were preoccupied.”

She stood from the bench, and Mydei was half tempted to reach out to stop her. It might have made him feel tense seeing her again, but the interaction had gone better than expected for him to want it over just like that. Unfortunately, he hadn’t been able to compose his thoughts at all regarding it.

So he let her stand.

“Mother, I—”

She cut him off before he could keep going. “It’s alright, son. You don’t have to force yourself to say anything.” It didn’t feel forced. He was just unsure of what the right thing would be. “How about we meet up for lunch sometime? I’ve missed you, I would hate for another three years to pass before I see you again.”

It was another thing meant to come off as comical, yet Mydei felt nothing of it.

He didn’t expect to see her today, which meant he definitely didn’t expect to even consider making plans to catch up. Mydei thought he had a while to go before that happened, at least long enough for him to do what he said he would. Make it in life himself so that he could prove he never needed anything else.

‘You did what you needed to do.’

That time hadn’t come yet, which is why he couldn’t give her anything else without telling the truth. If his mother could understand why he left, she could understand this as well.

“I don’t have a restaurant yet, mother.”

Gorgo’s lips parted slightly in surprise, before she relaxed and rolled her eyes playfully.

“That’s not what I was asking of you, Mydeimos.”

“I know,” he assured, not really believing it himself. “I just… wanted to tell you that.” He didn’t receive a response right away. If anything, she appeared to be studying him, articulating the right words for his sudden declaration. As out of place as it might have felt, Mydei didn’t regret saying it.

Because once again, regret wasn’t really his thing.

“I see,” his mother eventually said. “Alright, then.”

No comments about it. No questioning what the hold up was, just simple acceptance. Which meant Mydei wouldn’t have to explain himself, at least not today.

That also meant he could finally do something about her offer.

“About lunch.” Gorgo raised a brow but remained silent, prompting him to continue. “If your number is still the same, I’ll reach out. I have a busy schedule, as you can see, so I’m not sure when it will be.” She gave a simple nod, which was enough for now. Unfortunately, Mydei wasn’t finished. “I also don’t want you to mention it to father.”

Much to his surprise, his mother didn’t seem phased by the request at all.

“If that’s what you want, then I won’t push back.” It is what he wanted, and he wouldn’t beat around the bush trying to deny it. “For what it’s worth, he’s come around to a lot of things recently. I’m… sure you two could have a conversation.”

Mydei had too much on his plate to even think about his father.

“No.” Plain and simple, no room for hesitation. “Not now, at least.” He couldn’t remember how many lectures and arguments he’s gone through regarding his profession, or how it didn’t align with his father’s wishes. Even if Mydei managed to get lucky this year and successfully open a restaurant, that man would be lucky to even get a conversation out of him.

Gorgo made no efforts in changing his mind. “Alright. As long as you’re still considering it with me, I’ll respect that.”

Mydei saw no reason not to. If it went anything like it did today, it would be foolish to worry about it. “Thank you.”

She smiled, reaching out to adjust the flower that he could feel slipping from his ear. “I’ll see you later, honey.”

Honey. Three years without hearing that, all because he left. It took everything to remind himself that he did it for a reason.

“Bye, mom.” He barely heard his own voice, hoping at least she could.

The hand slowly fell from his ear and he watched as she turned on her heels, the distance between them growing with each step she took. Mydei could feel himself zoning out, the atmosphere around him blurring as he recounted the interaction in his head. It only took him down the memory of their last conversation as well, leaving him to wonder how their reunion could be so…

Strange.

He was too lost in thought to even realize Clara had run up to him.

“Dei?”

Reality hit him at once and his head turned to meet her big, curious eyes. It felt like a slap in the face, because for someone so adamant on her staying in his line of sight, he didn’t even know how long she had been standing there.

Mydei sighed. “Sorry, I was just thinking.”

Clara hopped on the bench, right by his side. With much less distance that was between him and— “Was that your mom?”

Amber eyes widened. “How did you…”

“She looks like you.” Mydei hadn’t even thought of that. He knew his resemblance with his mother was far greater than his father — thank the Titans for that. Still, he didn’t think Clara would make the assumption right away. “You also seem different. I remember you said you guys had a disagreement, so.”

What a smart kid.

He cocked a brow. “Different how?” He hoped it didn’t seem like he was upset, because he wasn’t. He didn’t dread the fact that he just saw his mother again. Mydei just didn’t know how he felt, and hoped Clara would give her insight so he could at least start somewhere.

“Worried.” Again, too smart for her own good. Worried wasn’t a far stretch. “Are you worried about something, Dei?”

Logically speaking, Mydei knew he shouldn’t start ranting to a six year old. He didn’t get paid to lay his problems onto her. Then again, he’s built up so much trust with her that it almost felt natural to show himself. In a way, it was easier with her than it could be with Phainon. “She wants to have lunch with me sometime.”

Clara tilted her head. “Are you?”

“Don’t know,” she shrugged. “Hm. What do you think?” This time, it wasn’t to strictly get her input. He only asked it in a lighthearted manner to make the conversation seem less serious.

“Do you miss her?”

Now it just felt more serious.

“Sometimes.” Mydei couldn’t lie. Not to himself, and definitely not to her. If he knew any better, he would say that she appeared not to believe him, either. “Yes. I do.”

Mydei worried he was being too insensitive making this a bigger deal than it needed to be. Phainon didn’t have the luxury of seeing his mom anymore, and Mydei didn’t even know the situation regarding Clara’s. Something like this probably seemed so pointless.

“Then yes,” Clara said, nodding firmly.

He frowned. “I’m the one who left. I’m a leaver.”

She punched his arm playfully. “I told you before that I’m sure it wasn’t your fault.” Mydei was lucky to have her stand by her opinion, he just wished it had more of an effect on how he truly felt. “And you’re not a leaver. You’re not going to walk out on me and daddy, right?”

Walk out on them? Mydei wouldn’t even dream of it. “Absolutely not.”

“Promise?” She held her pinky out, giving a pointed look. “Daddy says you can’t break a pinky promise.”

Of course he did. Mydei snorted, albeit bringing his finger to lock with hers. “Promise.”

Clara made sure it was secured before letting go. “Then you’re not a leaver. Actually, that just means you’re a stayer.”

Mydei didn’t need a pinky promise to ensure him sticking around. As much as Phainon could make things so confusing, Mydei has never felt more in place than he did with them. “Guess that also means you guys are stuck with me.”

Clara perked up. “Even with school?”

“What about school?”

“Well,” she said, fiddling with her hands. “School starts on Monday. You’re… still going to be here, right?”

Mydei immediately remembered what Phainon had told him when they first met.

The man offered the job for the summer, never once stating anything otherwise. Granted summer had been almost halfway over by then, but Mydei still never thought about what would come after. He saw no reason as to why he’d say no, but then again those were Phainon’s words and he couldn’t just make the decision for him.

“I’ll discuss it with Phainon,” was all Mydei could give.

Clara rolled her eyes jokingly. “He’s obviously going to say yes, Dei. Daddy always gives in with you.”

Not always.

Phainon could be real stubborn when he wanted to be.

Mydei huffed in amusement. “I suppose. Well, then I’ll listen to him tell me yes when I mention it to him. Deal?” He held his hand out for emphasis, aiming to secure another promise between them, this time with a handshake.

Clara ignored the hand completely.

In a split second, she surged forward and wrapped her arms around his neck. Just like when she first hugged him, Mydei was caught completely off guard, but he didn’t stay still. This time, he let his surprised expression morph into something more soft before returning the gesture.

He felt Clara squeeze him tighter.

At that moment, he couldn’t see any reason worth walking on them.

Mydei let himself fall to the couch, lazily reaching for his phone in his back pocket.

It’s been a day.

Between seeing his mother and having to deal with Phainon ignoring their issue, Mydei needed to do something. Talk to someone, anything to take his mind off of things he had no idea on how to handle right now.

It was now the weekend, which meant Mydei wouldn’t have to see Phainon for another two days. It didn’t miraculously stop him from thinking of the man, not to mention his lack of babysitting would only make him think harder. Not exactly an ideal way to spend his days off, so he’d happily accept defeat and reach out to someone.

Castorice, of course.

Cipher would give him hell. Not to mention he failed to listen to her, deciding once again to initiate something withPhainon instead of letting the man come to him.

He brought the phone to his ear after finding Castorice’s contact, contemplating on how he’d begin. He wouldn’t start with Phainon, he hadn’t exactly been open with his friends on how the situation made him feel. His mother seemed like the better topic seeing as they were with him when he made the choice three years.

She picked up after the fourth ring.

“Hello, Mydei,” she greeted.

“Hey, Cas.” He could hear how deflated his own tone sounded.

“Is everything okay?” Mydei wasn’t sure. It wasn’t awful seeing his mother again, quite the opposite, but it was a meeting that had no preparations. He had no chance to think of what to say, and she was the one who ended up doing most of the talking. As far as that being ‘okay,’ it was hard to tell. “Mydei?”

Right. Mydei hoped he hadn’t been silent too long. He didn’t apologize for it, as much as he wanted to, because there was only one thing that could come out of his mouth.

“I saw my mother today.”

This time, it was Castorice’s turn not to say anything for a couple of seconds. Then—

“What? You’re kidding me. Please say you’re joking.”

Mydei took a deep breath. Of course Cipher would be right there too, and he failed to hide his lack of surprise when he asked, “am I on speaker?”

Cipher ignored him. “I can’t believe you were seriously going to drop that without telling me too.” Mydei never said he planned on keeping it from her, he just intended to keep it from her now considering he was unsure how to feel about it.

“Hello, Cipher. I saw my mother today.”

“Little prince, I once had a dream that your mere presence didn’t piss me off sometimes. Then I woke up.”

“Please, don’t listen to her,” Castorice interjected, her gentle voice contrasting Cipher’s offended one. Mydei didn’t see why she felt so betrayed anyway, it’s something that just happened earlier. It’s not like he waited weeks to bring it up. “How did you see your mother? Did she come to you?”

“No,” he answered. “I was at the park with Clara and she was too. Next thing I know, she’s sitting beside me and we’re talking.” Correction, she talked. Mydei just sat there unaware of how to even approach the conversation while giving his best.

Castorice hummed. “She wasn’t upset?”

“Not at all.” At least that’s how it seemed, but his mother was always the type to let her feelings be known. If a part of her was upset, Mydei couldn’t have known. “She said she understood, because she knew it was what I needed to do.”

“She couldn’t say something like that three years ago?”

“Cipher…”

Mydei couldn’t argue with her, though. “Cipher’s right. Could’ve made a difference.”

“Wait, wait,” Cipher said with urgency. “Do me a favor. Repeat that.”

Mydei furrowed his brows. “It could’ve made a difference?”

Cipher sucked her teeth. “No, the part about me being right.” Mydei had never rolled his eyes so painfully slowly in his life. He wasn’t going to repeat it, and frankly he contemplated going back on his word just so she wouldn’t have the satisfaction. “Did Phainut finally dick you down so hard that you started agreeing with me?”

If it hadn’t been for Castorice being there too, Mydei would’ve slammed the red button and ended the call. His eyes widened in horror. “What did you just call him?”

“I said Phainon.”

Cipher sure did know how to say things that could stick. Now, instead of concerning himself with his mother, he couldn’t help but picture Phainon ‘dicking him down,’ as she so kindly put it. With his two main emotions right now, Mydei wasn’t sure whether he should cry or hang up to go take care of himself.

He had no idea he could be so versatile.

“Castorice.”

“I’m here,” she said, almost apologetically. “Look, all that aside, what if your mother really does understand? Even if she didn’t back you up much then, that doesn’t mean she never thought about it.”

There was no way Mydei would know, not until he made lunch plans and asked her himself. Then again, knowing that his mother always supported him might have made it worse. He wasn’t lying when he said it could’ve made a difference, no matter how small it was.

“So you think I should?”

She laughed endearingly. “I can’t tell you that. I can say that you once told us you didn’t make the choice because of her. If she doesn’t hold anything against you either, I think lunch could be good..”

“I agree, little prince,” Cipher added. “Your mom has always been more understanding. I’ll gladly accept the free lunch if you don’t, though. Plus, DILF’s aren’t the only thing these keen eyes of mine can notice. I can confidently say that your mother is a—”

“Finish that and I’m hanging up.” He could hear her snickering in the background, and he rolled his eyes despite the fact she couldn’t see. “Castorice, I offer my sympathy to you.”

Cipher’s humor fell. “Oh, come on. Cas probably thinks the same thing.”

“I think no such thing of his mother.”

“Whatever.”

On the bright side, Mydei felt less constricted about the matter. “Thanks for listening, Castorice.” Truth be told, he knew Cipher cared. He understood by now that joking was her way of concealing that. Still, he couldn’t resist poking the bear. “You always know how to cheer me up.”

“Dude,” Cipher complained, and Mydei smiled in triumph. “I’m ignoring that for your sake, because I was going to mention hitting the town tonight. You know, taking the edge off and what not. Worry about your troubles no more, little prince.”

“When did you decide that?” Castorice asked her.

“On a whim.”

Mydei scowled at his phone. “Your ‘on a whim’ plans can be very hit or miss.”

“Come on,” Cipher drawled. “Work was awful today, and you’re clearly stressed about something. You can’t go to your D appointment because it’s the weekend so you need a way to let loose, too. I’m literally trying to kill two birds with one stone here.”

If Mydei heard one more implication of Phainon fucking him, it would be too soon. It was bad enough that the reality was him dealing with a man who had too much willpower. Dreaming of what could happen was not in his best interest right now.

Still, his mind went there anyway. Any mention of Phainon had Mydei’s head reeling, for better or for worse.

“Take this up with Cas.”

“I’m not opposed,” Castorice said. “Only if you aren’t. It’s understandable if you want to stay to yourself right now.”

Making sure he had his phone on him, Mydei attempted to do exactly that.

He heard nothing as he stepped into the living room, assuming the man was still asleep. Phainon hardly cooked breakfast, so there was no other place for him to be and since Mydei found no trace of him, it was safe to say he’d get lucky this time around.

Once he made it to the entrance, his hand reached out towards the knob with precise movements to keep from making any noise. He knew he’d have to explain his leave eventually, Phainon would ask, but he didn’t worry about it too much. Not when he was seconds away from finally getting out.

“Where are you going?”

Mydei went still.

He closed his eyes and exhaled deeply, finding it hard to be surprised. He couldn’t recall a time he’s truly gotten lucky when Phainon was concerned.

Mydei didn’t bother to turn around.

“Because if you say ‘home,’” Phainon continued, “I should probably remind you that I drove you here, so it would be a pretty lengthy walk.”

One he would willingly take, especially right now. Mydei clenched his teeth before speaking. “I’m not above walking.”

“Maybe not,” Phainon said. “But if you’re doing that, the least you could do is get some breakfast. You know, fuel for the walk.” Right, because having to spend another second in his vicinity was the perfect fuel he needed. If anything, it was the reason he wanted to start walking.

Mydei braced himself before finally turning around, brows furrowed. “What.”

Phainon smiled, shrugging. “You’re the foodie, I thought you’d know that.”

Mydei glared. “I meant what are you talking about, you’re insane if you think I even feel like cooking.”

“Good, because I wasn’t talking about you being the one to cook.” Perfect, because on top of everything else he had going on, he now had to subject himself to Phainon’s food. Food that Clara, and Phainon himself, said was mediocre at best. Mydei pinched the bridge of his nose, and Phainon was quick to pick up on it. “Come on, Mydei. I may not have a culinary degree, but I can make a simple breakfast.”

Breakfast was one of the easier things to mess up, but Mydei didn’t feel like reminding him of that.

Instead, he moved his hand away from his face and sighed. Phainon wouldn’t relent anyway, not on this. That didn’t mean Mydei had to talk about anything else. “Fine. I already feel terrible right now, what more harm can eating your food do.”

Mydei started walking towards the kitchen. Phainon trailed behind him. “Are you always this cranky when you’re hungover?” He teased.

“Not even going to play into your jokes.” Mydei sat down, resting his hand in his hands, blocking the light from his still sensitive eyes. “You and I both know I’m never hungover.”

“Yeah, I know.” From the noise, Mydei could guess that Phainon was getting everything ready to cook. All for a breakfast that Mydei didn’t have high hopes for. “Guess that leads me to my next question.”

Mydei glanced up, barely uncovering his eyes. “What, don’t tell me you don’t know how to make an omelet.”

Phainon looked back over his shoulder. “Quit deflecting.” Ironic, considering that’s all he’s done since he met Phainon. “What brought this on? You can’t just say you don’t drink one minute, and have Castorice calling me to pick you up the next.”

Mydei groaned. It’s not like he asked her to do that. He didn’t hold anything against her, of course, and would do well to remind her of that. It wasn’t her fault that his lack of composure had him doing and saying things he wished he hadn’t. Things he knew he meant. “I don’t want to talk about it.”

He couldn’t talk about it. Mydei couldn’t tell Phainon that he only started because of him. That would’ve made him look like he couldn’t handle this, shattering whatever they had built.

Even if Mydei was only so messed up because every time he gave Phainon an inch, the man took a mile in the opposite direction.

“Mydei,” Phainon said, his voice gentle. “You can talk to me about these things. I’m not just your boss.”

Then what else are you, because I surely don’t know. “I was letting loose,” he replied, stealing the words Cipher had used. “Enjoying myself.”

“By drinking?”

Mydei scowled. “How else would you suppose I do it?”

When Phainon met his eyes, it was clear he picked up on the unspoken message. Mydei’s head hurt too much to care, and it's not like he had been lying. He couldn’t just enjoy himself in the way he wanted to, but someone always stopped them.

Phainon said nothing else, turning his attention towards the stove. The longer he went without speaking, the more Mydei felt inclined to fill the silence. He definitely wouldn’t come right out and tell the truth, that wasn’t up for debate. This wasn’t how he ever planned on having that kind of conversation with Phainon.

But… he could give something.

“I saw my mother yesterday.”

Phainon glimpsed back, pressing his brows together. “Your mother? Do you guys not have a good relationship?”

Mydei grew confused. “Clara didn’t tell you?”

“No?”

Huh. Mydei had fully expected for her to have brought it up to Phainon by now, it’s not like he would’ve minded. “I haven’t spoken to her in three years.”

“Oh,” Phainon said, sounding more understanding. “Do you feel like sharing the reason?”

He didn’t see why not, it sure beat talking about the other thing. “Me and my father had different viewpoints on my career choice. If I was ever going to prove a point, I had to cut contact. With both of them.” It occurred to him that this was Phainon he was speaking with, someone whose mother had died. Mydei couldn’t even be mad if the man suddenly saw him as the world's biggest asshole.

However, this was also the same person who somehow could always see Mydei in a good light. No matter what.

“How did it go?” He asked. “Was she upset?”

As much as he’s heard the question, it didn’t make answering any better. “She wasn’t upset. She was fine with everything, even asked me to lunch.”

“Are you going?”

Mydei could say no, but truthfully, he didn’t see a reason why he would. He pretty much already made that decision when he spoke with Castorice and Cipher yesterday. “Maybe.”

Phainon nodded. “I see. It could be a good thing, at least that’s another person you’ll have back in your life.” It would take some getting used to, as much as Mydei hated to admit it. “You know, I don’t think I’ve ever mentioned it before, but my mother—”

“I know,” Mydei finished for him, sounding sincere. “Clara told me. You don’t have to say anything.” He wondered if Phainon wanted to say something about it, but the smile on his face afterwards showed that he was fine. He definitely didn’t seem bothered that Clara had already beaten him to the punch.

“She’s always one step ahead, isn’t she.”

Mydei huffed a laugh. “That she is.” He thought back to the conversation he had with her in the park, realizing this was yet another thing he could use to stray away from the previous topic. “She mentioned something to me yesterday.”

Phainon glanced over. “Should I be concerned?”

“Absolutely.” Phainon shook his head with a grin and Mydei continued. “She mentioned me sticking around once she started school.”

He could see Phainon tense up. There was no telling how the man felt about it, even when Clara assured him her father would say yes. Still, he promised he’d say something about it. If Phainon ultimately decided that he only wanted Mydei for the summer, the latter couldn’t argue against that.

“You… don’t have to.”

That wasn’t helpful. “I know.”

Phainon still appeared unsure. “I… know the deal was only for the summer, I could ask any more of you.”

“Phainon.”

The man turned to face him directly, completely ignoring the contents in the pan. Mydei would fear for the sake of their food later. “Yeah?”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “I don’t mind. Really, I think you underestimate how much I enjoy spending time with her.” Even if the schedule changes and he only sees her for a few hours, Mydei didn’t see why he wouldn’t say yes.

Phainon’s eyes lit up before his face softened. “Alright, then. To be fair, I’d hate to have to find a new babysitter in the span of two days.”

“Knowing how easy you picked me up, I’m sure you’d manage. Your judgement might be a little off, though.”

Phainon laughed at that, shifting his focus back to the food. Mydei couldn’t wait for Clara to find out, even if she already had a feeling her father would say yes. He knew she wasn’t here for the weekend, so he would have to trust that Phainon could give her the confirmation before Monday.

“Hey, Mydei?” The blonde raised a brow, remaining silent as he waited for Phainon to keep going. “About last night—”

No. He didn’t just stray away from it only to end right where he started. Mydei didn’t bother to let him finish that sentence, not when it was clear it was more about him simply drinking this time.

“I’m not talking about it.”

Phainon opened his mouth to speak, presumably to get him to change his mind, but decided against it. “Alright.” Good, Mydei thought. Thinking back to it was bad enough. “Can I at least ask one thing?”

Mydei knew he should refuse, that asking one thing went against his wish of dropping it completely. Maybe this was the only way of ensuring it did get forgotten, indulging Phainon just once before they moved on from it.

“Go ahead.”

A few seconds passed before Phainon finally continued. “Did you really show someone else that picture?”

Mydei averted his gaze, trying to jog his memory as he pieced together what Phainon was talking about.

Oh.

The moment in the car, when Mydei was taunting him. That’s what was bothering Phainon. A mere comment meant to rile the man up.

“No. I didn’t.”

He wasn’t lying, either.

Phainon nodded and relaxed. “Okay.”

Just as Mydei suspected, that was enough for him and nothing else was brought up.

When Monday rolled around, Mydei wished he could say he was grateful for the chance to sleep in. His duties as Clara’s babysitter didn’t come until later when he had to pick her up from school, Phainon having plenty of time before work to be the one taking her.

Unfortunately, sleeping in was not what had happened.

His body was already used to waking up early, and it was rather disappointing that their rhythm was changing. He wouldn’t be able to show up early, teasing Phainon with Clara before the man had to leave. Now, he would only see them once a day.

Mydei missed it already.

He reached for his phone, finding Phainon’s messages.

Mydei: tell clara i hope she has a good first day

The response was almost immediate.

Phainon: Mydei!!!

Then, a picture came through.

Phainon: I tried to do the hairstyle she likes. Does it look fine?

Oh no.

Titans, how could someone mess up a braid.

If anything, it was the concept of a braid. It was clear what he was going for, but the strands were uneven and there were pieces of hair included that should even be there. Mydei would seriously have to teach this man something so simple if it meant not ruining the integrity of their shared hairstyle.

Mydei: phainon. that looks awful.

Phainon: Yeah, Clara said the same :(

Mydei took another look at the image, nothing but pure disbelief on his face.

Mydei: how much time do you have to kill before you need to leave?

Phainon: Thirty minutes, why do you ask?

Then it was settled, he would save Clara’s hair. He definitely wasn’t using this as an excuse to see them this morning, like he usually would.

Mydei: get to my apartment asap. i’m fixing that braid.

Chapter End Notes

I lowkey sampled Mydei's 'five to nine' comeback from that one Ariana song. Okay and

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Testing Temptation
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

If you give a mouse a cookie, he’s going to try eating it in his office.

Chapter Notes

Huge shoutout to Khris for the beta read.

ALSO PLEASEEE check out this AMAZING artwork from chapter 4 of Mydei’s candy apple selfie ;) He’s so pretty, don’t tell Phainon we got to see it, guys.

As much as Mydei wished he could stall some more, with one final glance at the time, he realized that wasn’t possible. Not if he didn’t want to keep his mother waiting. It was bad enough he took two weeks before considering her request, showing up late would’ve just been rude.

So, here he was.

He couldn’t give a legitimate reason why it took so long to see her, because he didn’t have one. With Clara in school during the better part of the day, he had every opportunity. It would at least give him something to do while he waited to pick her up.

Truth is, Mydei missed their usual routine. A lot.

It wasn't so bad the first week. When Phainon had shown up on Clara’s first day of school, the two of them eager to have her hair fixed, Mydei was pleased. Seeing them in the morning again felt nice, especially since that’s all he had gotten used to for a month.

Mydei convinced himself that Phainon saw it the same way.

“You’re good at that,” the man said, smiling as Mydei finished the braid. “Makes me think you’ve been doing it your whole life.”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “Idiot,” he shot back, not bothering to glance Phainon’s way. “I have been doing it my whole life. You’d do well to watch and learn, instead of pointing out the obvious.”

“Why watch and learn when I can just have you do it every morning?”

For a week, that’s exactly what happened.

Mydei doesn’t remember who made the offer, or if an offer was even made at all. All he knew was that Phainon showed up the next day, and the day after that, giving Mydei yet another thing he looked forward to in the mornings. He didn’t mind it and none of them complained.

Of course, until Mydei realized he was being unfair. He knew he couldn’t hide behind the excuse of fixing Clara’s hair just to see them, so he did as promised and taught Phainon how to braid. That was almost a week ago and if the picture Mydei received recently was any indication, it was safe to say Phainon got the gist of it.

Therefore, Mydei wasn’t needed anymore.

What a thought.

Mydei saw no reason to throw himself a pity party right now, not when his mother was currently waiting inside the cafe for him. It was silly to consider anyway, he still saw Phainon and Clara in the afternoons, it wasn’t owed to him to have their mornings together as well.

With a sigh, he pushed the car door open and made his way inside.

He tried not to think much about how this meeting would go. It helped that they already had a conversation before, just enough for Mydei to know there wasn’t any bad blood between them. He could rest easy knowing that was the case, no matter how awkward he might feel.

Once he was inside, it didn’t take long for him to spot his mother.

She hadn’t noticed his presence at first, not until he began walking closer. Her eyes lit up at the sight of him and Mydei half expected her to stand up, arms out ready for a hug. Much to his surprise, she remained seated, likely assuming the gesture would go unreciprocated.

It’s not that Mydei would’ve left her hanging, he just hasn’t embraced his mother in three years. He might be stiff, but he’d still hug her.

“Mydeimos,” she said as he approached the table, slipping into the booth across from her. “You’re right on time.”

He didn’t bother to mention that he could’ve been earlier if he hadn’t been stalling. “Punctuality is one of my strong suits.”

She laughed. “Always has been. You get that from me.”

Mydei smiled.

It wasn’t off to a bad start. Granted it’s only been less than a minute, but at least the greeting didn’t feel forced. It was natural, reminding Mydei that there was no reason to feel weird about the whole thing because this was his mother. The same woman who made it clear that she understood him more than his father ever could.

He could do this.

“So,” Gorgo continued. “I hope it’s alright, I went ahead and ordered a drink for you.”

Mydei furrowed his brows, trying to recall his previous conversation with her when they made the plans. He came up blank, the only thing coming to mind being the name of the place. “But I didn’t—”

“Two cups of pomegranate juice, splash of milk.”

What?

Mydei’s eyes widened and he looked to his left. The waiter said nothing else as he placed the mugs on the table, before walking away. Mydei stared at the cups like he didn’t understand where they came from, almost missing his mother’s small laugh in the process.

“It’s been three years, Mydeimos, not ten. Though, I think I would still remember your favorite drink even after that long.”

Mydei knew how long it’s been, and he also knew his regular order was peculiar enough to stick out. It was just the sentiment of it all that caught him off guard, and his mothers full confidence that it would be the drink he planned on getting. It was nice, a rather comforting thought. “Yeah,” he agreed, lips tugging upwards. “Guess you’re right.”

Gorgo hummed. “I am.” She retrieved her own mug, encouraging Mydei to do the same. “It would be different if you switched to that bitter stuff. What is it with coffee, anyway? It smells great, but tastes like ashes.”

Like clockwork, Mydei immediately thought back to Phainon.

If there was one thing the man swore by, it was coffee. Mydei always told Phainon it would be the death of him, but the latter claimed the addiction was ‘too good to let go of.’ He even declared that one day, he’d get Mydei to come around to it as well. Mydei could only chuckle. “Cream and sugar. That doesn’t save it completely, just makes it bearable.”

“Bearable,” Gorgo scoffed. “That’s a health hazard waiting to happen.”

Mydei couldn’t say he disagreed. He entertained the thought of her telling Phainon the same thing, until he realized that was ridiculous because how would the two of them ever interact? This might be Mydei’s first time watching a kid, but he was almost one hundred percent sure that babysitters didn’t introduce their parents to the person who paid them.

He couldn’t help but wonder what she would think of him, though.

Mydei shrugged. “I suppose.”

“Enough about coffee, though.” Good, Mydei would hate for the one thing they managed to talk about end up being a beverage he didn’t even like. Not to mention he still started thinking back to Phainon when he really shouldn’t have. “I take it your free days mean the little one is in school.”

Don’t remind me, is what Mydei could’ve said. Instead, he simply nodded. “I’ll still see her after. Just until her father gets home.”

“Ah,” she drawled, taking another sip of her drink. “I’m lucky, then. Getting some of your time.” Mydei frowned once her words registered. He didn’t take her up on the offer solely because his schedule changed, it only helped him do it sooner. His mother picked up on it right away, tilting her head forward slightly. “Come on. I’m only messing with you.”

One could never be too sure. “I’m here because I wanted to be.” It only took enough convincing, sure, but that much was the truth.

“I’m aware, Mydeimos. You’ve never been the pushover type.” That’s because she's never seen him in the presence of Phainon Khaslana, a man who could no doubt reduce him to a shameless version of himself. Not that Mydei could know for certain, the latter would never indulge him long enough to find out.

Just when he was sure he stopped thinking about Phainon.

He had to change the subject, or at least talk about someone else.

“I can’t take all of the credit.” Gorgo raised a brow in question and Mydei smiled, a genuine thing. “Castorice and Cipher encouraged me to do it, too.” Even beneath Cipher’s unnecessary comment regarding his mother, he could understand what she was trying to say.

That seemed to please the woman. “Glad to know those girls never change. Have they been okay?”

“They have,” Mydei confirmed. “Living together, finally. Castorice still writes, and Cipher is still the same menace she was at nine years old.”

His mother chuckled. “You’re not any better yourself, son. You can have your moments.” Castorice liked to say that as well, but Mydei never saw it. In fact, he whole heartedly believed Cipher only acted out of pocket because it irritated Mydei to no end. Not to mention she knew her comments got in his head. He probably wouldn’t be so bent out of shape over Phainon if she never referred to him as a ‘DILF.’

But once again, this shouldn’t be about him.

“So if they’re good, does that mean you are too?”

Mydei blinked, unaware of how to answer her question. It should’ve been easy enough, he hasn’t been awful. Lonely, maybe. A little confused? Definitely. Still, that couldn’t stop him from averting his gaze before answering, “I am.”

“Mydeimos.”

He realized his mistake the second he looked away. “Sorry,” he breathed out, turning towards her.

His mother shook her head. “Don’t apologize. I’m just concerned why you’d be lying about being okay.”

He wasn’t lying, per se. ‘Being okay’ just wasn’t the full truth in how he really felt. “It’s hard to explain.” There was no way she’d want to hear about his complicated feelings regarding his boss, so he hoped that would suffice for now. “Understanding it in its full extent would be difficult.”

A mother’s curiosity, however, could not be brushed off that easily. “How so?”

Mydei didn’t say anything, not right away. He wanted so badly to move onto another topic, promising himself that this would be the final time he thought of Phainon, but he couldn’t do it. Not with that gentle expression on her face, the one from his childhood that told him he could always open up to her. If he truly wanted to.

In a strange way, he did really want to.

He wouldn’t have to worry about his friends portraying both sides of his own feelings. He could get an outside perspective from someone who would be honest because if there was one word to describe his mother, it would be upfront. Besides, talking to someone who understood how being a parent worked would help too. At least that way he could try and resonate with Phainon some more.

After a few seconds, Mydei finally sighed. “I met someone.”

Even if he already saw it coming, he couldn’t have been prepared to see her face soften.

“You just continue to surprise me.”

Honestly, Mydei continued to surprise himself as well. He would’ve never seen himself in a position where his own feelings put a strain on his job. He liked to think he had more resolve than that, but Phainon’s mere presence chipped away at whatever was left. “It wasn’t planned.”

“The good ones never are,” his mother said. Mydei huffed in amusement, though it was more so in irony. It was hard to call what he and Phainon had ‘good’ when he wasn’t sure what the other man felt at all. “Is it leaning into something more?”

Mydei would never voice it out loud, but he wished he could say yes. Instead, he looked down, eyes locked onto his untouched mug. “It’s not really that simple.”

Gorgo tilted her head. “Is he married?”

“What?” Mydei quickly glanced up, shocked by the question while his mother remained neutral. “Of course not, I would never break up a happy marriage.”

“I didn’t say it had to be happy,” she muttered. Even still, Mydei couldn’t imagine what he’d do in that given scenario. Then again, the idea of Phainon being married in general made his stomach twist so he’d rather not give it any thought. “Well,” his mother continued, lips curling upwards. “He’s a parent, then.”

If her first assumption caught him off guard, there was no way to mask how the second made him feel. “How did you…”

She gave him a pointed look. “Mydeimos. If it’s not marriage making a situation complicated, it’s a child.” Mydei believed there were multiple things that could make a situation complicated, and that she shouldn’t have been able to guess it immediately. “Which leads me to my next question. The little girl you babysit, is she his?”

It should’ve irked him how easy it was for her to put everything together. It should’ve irked him more that he couldn’t lie about it, seeing as she would automatically know. “She is.”

“Figured,” Gorgo nodded. “That ‘family’ comment gave it away.” So she didn’t believe him when he tried deflecting on that? Why would she take a six year old's words literally when she’s never met Clara before?

Mydei slightly sunk in his seat. “A babysitter can be considered family.”

“She looks at you like you hung the moon.” He couldn’t help but smile at that. He’s never been one to hide how Clara’s admiration for him made him feel, and there was no point in starting now. Upon noticing, his mother held her pointer finger out at him. “That right there. That tells me she’s more than just the kid you babysit, too.”

She wasn’t wrong. ‘Just the kid he babysits’ implied he only watched Clara for the money, putting up with her like her previous babysitters had done. As long as he continued to be in her life, that would never be the case.

“It doesn’t matter how good our relationship is.”

She picked up on his unspoken words instantly. “The father.”

“The father,” he repeated. “And I don’t know what to do.”

His mother’s brows furrowed. “What makes you think you have to do anything?”

“Because he won’t,” Mydei answered, exasperated.

The second the words left his mouth, Mydei froze. He hadn’t expected to actually voice it out loud.

He couldn’t say it didn’t feel nice.

Everything that happened between them was always up to Phainon. Mydei would lean in, practically giving him the go ahead, and it would be Phainon who cut things off before they could progress. Things wouldn’t even get as far as they did if Mydei never aimed for it too, so what he said wasn’t exactly a lie.

Gorgo’s expression remained gentle, but there was a hint of understanding beneath it. “Well, son, sometimes parents don’t do anything so that they can keep their children’s best interest in mind.” She then smirked. “Not that I’m speaking from personal experience, of course.”

Right, her silence when Mydei pretty much ghosted them three years ago. He chuckled. “I see.”

She gave a short laugh as well, growing serious right after. “It’s a tough situation to be in. Is the mother in the picture?”

“No.” Mydei would never ask why, either. Not unless Phainon started that conversation himself.

“Well, that makes it more manageable." He supposed she had a point. He didn’t know the full story, but Mydei would certainly feel awkward if he were in a co-parenting situation. Then again, they would likely have no need for him if that was the reality of it. “That doesn’t mean it’s easier. He’s still a single parent, he’s probably balancing a lot.”

As selfish as it sounded, Mydei would’ve hoped he took some of the load off Phainon. Even if it was a little bit, because it was something he never minded doing. Everything that had been done was ofn his own free will, because he wanted to.

“Probably,” Mydei shrugged. “We’ve been toeing a line between professionalism and unprofessionalism recently.” Mydei didn’t make that any better, not with sending Phainon that flirty picture or failing to conceal his lust every time the atmosphere between them shifted.

“Mydeimos,” she began, acknowledging him sincerely. “If you can establish something like that, then you might be closer to crossing it than you think.”

Mydei thought about it, how incredibly wrong she was. At this rate, they would constantly be bordering that line until something snapped. The only problem was, Mydei didn’t know what that would be and Phainon never gave any hints for him to figure it out.

“You should make a gesture,” Gorgo suggested, and Mydei cocked a brow. He liked to think he'd been making them all along, because willingly cooking dinner almost every night was a pretty big gesture. No matter how much he thoroughly enjoyed it. “Take the initiative.”

She must not understand the nature of the situation. Mydei taking the incentive didn’t automatically ensure Phainon giving in. Frankly, it ended up having the opposite effect. “As in?”

His mother frowned. “Mydeimos.” Was there something he was missing? What other initiative could he take that he hadn’t already? Phainon already knew Mydei lusted after him, it was the thought that loomed over both of their heads. “All you do is see him when you’re watching the kid, right?” Mydei nodded. “So plan for something outside of that, maybe while she’s at school.”

Like… a date?

“I’m confused.”

She clicked her tongue. “Son, if you guys only see each other because of your job, that’s going to hold him back.” How else was Mydei supposed to see him? Before Clara started school, the only time Phainon even had a break was the weekends. Time he spent with his daughter, might Mydei add, and there was no way he’d interfere with that.

“He has a job.”

Gorgo stared ahead, dumbfounded. “Twenty-four seven?”

“No,” Mydei replied, his voice small. “But… it’s still a priority.”

“A relationship is also a priority.”

Mydei exhaled deeply. “It’s not—”

“Yet,” she finished for him, though he hadn’t planned on saying that at all. It wouldn’t be wise trying to speak something into existence knowing how his luck went. “Job this, job that. Are you two incapable of seeing each other past your careers?”

Phainon’s job wasn’t the problem at all. It kept him busy, yes, but they were only in this situation because of what Mydei was to Clara. “I wasn’t—”

“Don’t lie to your mother, Mydeimos.” A faint pout made its way on Mydei’s face. He wasn’t even going to lie. “You can’t think of one thing you could do? One small, tiny, miniscule thing.”

Not really, and he didn’t exactly have a lot of options either. He couldn’t plan for something on the weekend, that meant Phainon would have to find someone to watch Clara and Mydei didn’t want to put him through the trouble. Especially when Mydei was the person who they hired specifically to do that.

Mydei looked off to the side, thinking it over some more.

He could always plan something for lunch. Phainon was never shy in sharing his work schedule, so Mydei knew the man got a pretty lengthy break from work during the day. He’d be eating with Hyacine today, but with tomorrow being Friday, nothing would stop Phainon from saying no.

Unless, of course, his stupid restraint had a part to play.

“You’re deep in thought over there.”

Mydei still hadn’t turned back towards her. “I might have an idea.”
