Stupid Phainon. Clara was giving her sympathy for a situation that wasn’t even true, he should be ashamed of himself. He definitely shouldn’t be grinning as if he found it humorous, but that didn’t seem to stop him.

Clara perked up. “Wait. Does this mean every time I get in trouble at school, Mydei will spend the night?”

“Yes.”

“No.”

They did it again, though the shock factor was far more evident with Mydei this time. He scowled at Phainon before shaking his head. “What is wrong with you?” Instead of waiting for a response, he shifted his body so that he could address Clara directly. “Listen. Your father didn’t mention it yesterday, but hitting someone does not fix anything.”

Ironic, considering he’s been plotting Phainon’s downfall since the man threw him off the bed.

She pouted. “Even if they’re wrong?”

“Especially if they’re wrong,” he clarified. “Trust me, I’ve heard a lot of mean things directed to me, too. And as much as I wished I could’ve done something about it, I was the bigger person.”

Clara’s eyes widened, her expression morphing into concern. “People were mean to you?” Mydei nodded and she appeared as if she couldn’t accept that answer. “But… you’re one of the best things that happened to me and daddy. Why would anyone be mean to you?”

It was Mydei’s turn to be surprised.

Mydei could only stare, brows raised as he let it all sink in. His eyes moved on their own, shifting his head slightly so that he could look at Phainon. It was hard to confirm or deny if what Clara said was true, seeing as Phainon averted his gaze the second Mydei turned his way.

Hm.

Mydei’s attention was back on Clara, finally allowing himself to give her a soft smile. It was faint, but enough for her to pick up on it and return the gesture.

It didn’t get brought up again.

“So,” she continued. “Since Mydei is here, that means daddy doesn’t have to cook.” Through his peripherals, Mydei could see Phainon’s mouth part in offense.

Mydei huffed in amusement. “Sure. At least that way, it will actually be edible.” He was only saying it to be dramatic, anyway. He’s had Phainon’s cooking once and it wasn’t the worst.

Then again, he was also hungover at the time and would have settled for anything.

Still, he got the response he was looking for when Phainon shook his head, walking towards the table in defeat. “I’m outnumbered in my own house.”

“You’re just now noticing?” Clara asked. Mydei smirked.

The first thing Mydei did when he got home was shower, because he desperately needed one after last night. Not to mention he had still been in Phainon’s clothes and while it wasn’t that big of a deal, he couldn’t keep them on for what he had planned.

Because the second thing he did was call Castorice and Cipher.

…And his mother.

It was a shot in the dark to ask all three of them out to lunch, especially when this would technically only be his second outing with his mom. Then again, Cipher and Castorice openly advocated for him to seek her out a few weeks ago. They never said anything bad about Gorgo either, even during the three year separation.

So it shouldn’t have surprised him when they agreed.

He knew his mother would’ve been on board the moment he brought it up. Her mentioning his friends previously was proof of that, plus the conflict had never been between her and the girls. They had an amazing relationship initially and it only faltered because of Mydei.

He would have felt more guilty about it if they weren’t laughing with each other right now. Conversing like nothing had changed.

“You know,” Gorgo began, addressing Cipher and Castorice. “I was shocked when Mydei told me you two would be joining. I wasn’t aware our previous lunch made that much of an impression on him.”

It was an amazing lunch, and Mydei could’ve sworn he made that known when it ended. Even if he didn’t say it explicitly, but being able to read him was her thing.

It’s not like he had planned on letting weeks pass before reaching out to her again. Selfishly enough, the only reason it happened so soon was because Mydei needed to talk about recent events. His friends needed to be here considering they represented both parts of him, and his mother needed to be here because…

Well, because she was the one who sort of made it all happen. Unknowingly.

Castorice smiled. “I knew Mydei would enjoy it. Cipher did, too.”

“She’s right,” Cipher agreed. “He was in his head about it, whining about not knowing what to do.” Mydei shook his head, the action going unnoticed. “As if I didn’t constantly remind him over the years that you could never be mad at him.”

Mydei pressed his brows together, frowning. “No you didn’t.”

Cipher shot him a look. “We're having a conversation here.”

Mydei rolled his eyes and Gorgo laughed. “We’re only messing with you, Mydeimos,” his mother said. “Believe me, I knew something was up the moment you sent the text. If you wanted a simple outing with all of us, you would’ve planned for that.” She wasn’t wrong, not when it took him two weeks just to have lunch with her.

He hadn’t realized how abrupt his offer sounded today.

“Nothing’s wrong,” he clarified, shifting his attention to his mug. “I had recently left Phainon’s when I reached out.”

“What do you mean you ‘recently left Phainon’s?’” Cipher asked, cocking a brow. It then raised in an instant, followed by a quick gasp and Mydei braced himself for the worst. “Wait a second. Today is Saturday, meaning you’d have no reason to be there. If you left Phainon’s so early in the day, then… holy shit. No way you actually hopped on that!!”

Mydei hissed, “Be quiet.”

He failed to see his mother’s narrowed eyes, how she was silently trying to piece everything together. All he could focus on was Cipher’s smug expression. “I didn’t think you had it in you, little prince. All that talk about how it’s ‘not professional,’ yet you’re leaving his house early in the morning. Mydei, were you a booty call?”

Gorgo interjected before he had the chance to respond. “Mydeimos, did I misunderstand you the other day?” Great, now he had to address both his personal feelings and his sexual attraction towards Phainon. As if the situation couldn’t get any more complicated. “When you said you wished something would happen between you, I wasn’t aware you meant it… that way.”

Cipher turned her head. “Huh?”

Mydei was in a losing game right now. He sighed in defeat. “I guess it was both.” Because he wasn’t going to deny his feelings for Phainon, this entire lunch was so he could talk about them, among other things. “And I did use your advice as intended.”

Gorgo eyed him suspiciously. “But…”

“But it obviously had the opposite effect,” Cipher finished for him. “And our little prince got laid.” How she could say that so shamelessly in front of his mother, Mydei didn’t know. “Mydei, do you have some unknown romantic connection with Phainon that I wasn’t aware of?”

Mydei said nothing.

Unfortunately, that was a dead giveaway.

“Unbelievable!” Cipher exclaimed, throwing her hands up in the air. How dramatic. “People thirst over DILF’s, not fall in love with them. You just happen to be the exception yet this is the first time I’m hearing about it?”

That was way too presumptuous, Mydei never said anything about love.

“I knew,” Castorice shrugged and Cipher gaped. She wasn’t the only one stunned, because now Mydei was silently asking when she could’ve possibly found out. “What? I did. I knew when Phainon came to pick Mydei up from the bar.”

When Mydei was drunk? His memory from that night wasn’t vivid, but he at least could remember not saying anything revealing as far as personal feelings went. “What does that mean?”

Castorice shook her head with a laugh. “Mydei, you went to get a drink after saying nothing would happen between you two.” He was only responding to Cipher back then, who explicitly meant it in a sexual way. “No one reacts like that if they’re only thirsting.”

Mydei hated that she had a point.

Cipher deflated, crossing her arms. “Could’ve fooled me. I really thought the idea of not getting any would break his heart.”

He wasn’t that far gone. Even if Phainon never indulged him, he’d still continue with his job like it was just another day. It would only worsen his thoughts, yeah, but it wouldn’t devastate him.

“I have many questions,” Gorgo chimed in. Mydei hoped he didn’t have to recount that situation to her, considering it happened the same day he saw his mother in the park for the first time. “But I won’t ask. I’m only curious if you two are still on good terms. An intimate night is bound to change the dynamic.”

Mydei internally cringed at the phrase ‘intimate night,’ and how it almost turned into an ‘intimate morning.’ “We’re on good terms.”

“How good?” Cipher wondered. “Like, good enough for night two? Or…”

Castorice sighed. “Cipher.”

Seriously, because Mydei wasn’t exactly jumping at the chance to reveal his bedroom plans with his mother present.

Plus, it was hard to acknowledge her question when Mydei didn’t know the answer to it himself. He and Phainon never really had the chance to talk about what it meant for them. Mydei was too busy trying to wrap his head around the fact that it actually happened.

If past situations were any indication, he had a strong feeling things would continue normally. Just until either one of them brought it up first.

“All I’m saying is he’s still Clara’s babysitter.” Like Mydei really needed the reminder, but he let Cipher keep explaining herself. “Having a relationship with Phainon pretty much makes him… okay, look. I’m just going to say it.” She folded her hands, looking at Mydei seriously. “Little prince, you’re a step-mom.”

Gorgo covered her mouth in awe. “Ooh!”

“Not ‘ooh,’” Mydei said quickly. “You do know the only person who can declare that is Phainon himself.”

“Call him up,” Cipher offered. “Make sure to put him on speaker.”

Castorice held her arm to stop Mydei, as if he really considered calling Phainon. How ridiculous. “We shouldn’t. Mydei, the first thing you need to do is have a conversation with him. Alone. You work for him, so you’re allowed to speak about the relationship just as much as he is.”

The only problem was Mydei wasn’t sure how to approach it. What he had the right to do and what he actually wanted to do were two different things. He already took the initiative that put him in Phainon’s bed, it was the latter’s turn now.

Gorgo placed a reassuring hand on his shoulder. “Castorice is right. Trust the process, Mydeimos, but don’t take too long. You both care about the well-being of your job and your relationship with Clara, avoiding this could put a strain on that.”

Mydei thought back to Clara’s words that morning, how she said Mydei was one of the best things that happened to her and Phainon.

He never wanted to do anything that would end up changing her mind.

“I will.”

Maybe it would be good enough to ease the discussion for now.

Cipher pointed at him. “By the way, what happened to me telling you to let Phainon make the move? Did you happen to forget about that amidst all of your thirsting?”

Mydei frowned. That text felt like forever ago, which was the first time he and Phainon ever had a moment together. It started to get a little blurry once it became a reoccurring thing. “I realized you give terrible advice.”

Cipher’s mouth dropped in offense and his mother tilted her head. “Am I missing context?”

“Oh,” Cipher drawled, shaking her head in exaggeration. “Mama Gorgo, where do I even begin?” Whatever she would give away next was likely to get back at Mydei, all for saying her advice was bad. He sat prepared in case he needed to cut her rambling off.

So much for easing the conversation.

Almost a week later, Mydei and Phainon still never had the chance to talk about it.

They acted the same around each other, the only difference being Phainon’s lingering touches. He’d allow himself to make his need for Mydei known, yet as far as speaking on what that actually means for them?

They didn’t.

Mydei knew he should be wary, his mother’s reminder ringing in the back of his head. Truth was, he couldn’t see it as a bad thing at all considering everything was fine between them. Phainon was still the same person around him, as if being inside of Mydei wasn’t enough to shift their whole dynamic.

Naturally, it made sense that Mydei didn’t mention it either.

It also made sense why Mydei agreed to spend the weekend with them. It wasn’t the first occurrence and Clara was already aware of it last time, for whatever reason. The worst that might happen is her questioning Mydei’s choice of sleeping in Phainon’s room. He’d just let her father come up with an explanation.

Then again, considering how terrible his explanations could be, maybe Mydei should start thinking.

He’d do it later, seeing as he was too preoccupied with the grocery bags he carried inside. Phainon followed alongside him, the three of them just getting back from the store to prepare for the weekend.

Clara ran past them, almost knocking herself over in the process. “I’m going to go make something for Mydei, be right back!”

Mydei and Phainon had zero chance to respond when she had already closed her bedroom door behind her. Phainon snorted. “Guess we’ll have to wait.”

Mydei huffed, setting the bags down on the counter. “Surprised you’re not upset that she doesn’t have something planned for you.”

“It’s okay,” Phainon shrugged. He took a step closer, leaning in Mydei’s space before his voice dropped an octave lower. “I’ll get my present tonight, and I can’t wait to open it.” Phainon’s hand landed on Mydei’s waist, barely using any strength to pull him closer.

Mydei reached back, gripping the edge of the counter ground himself. “Cut it out,” he ordered through clenched teeth.

Phainon chuckled, eventually letting go. “Fine. We’ll have our chance later.”

A point Phainon already established when he asked Mydei to stay for the weekend. Still, it didn’t make him shiver any less.

Phainon’s attention was caught at the sound of his name, turning towards the direction Clara had called from. He abandoned the bag in his hand, presumably to go see why he was needed. “One second.”

Mydei remained silent as Phainon left the kitchen. He picked up where the man left off, putting things in their respective spaces to clear the mess. He fell into the groove of things until his phone vibrated in his pocket, causing him to retrieve the device to see who was ringing him.

He furrowed his brows when he read the screen. There was no way Cipher knew he was staying the weekend, right?

Mydei already began walking towards the front door as he answered the call. He brought his phone up to his ear, ensuring he was on the porch before deciding to speak. Whatever Cipher wanted, it shouldn’t take long and he’d be back inside before Phainon even made it to the kitchen.

The first thing Phainon noticed upon making it back was Mydei’s absence.

He could care less about the discarded grocery bags, Mydei wasn’t obligated to take care of them. He was only curious as to where the man could’ve gone, seeing as Phainon only stepped away for a minute.

He walked into the living room, glancing around before he caught sight of the front door. Surely Mydei didn’t just leave. Maybe he left something in his car, or needed a breath of fresh air. He would have said something if he really had to go.

Just to be sure, Phainon stalked towards the door. He immediately realized it was unlocked, which wouldn’t mean much if he didn’t vividly remember locking it when they got home.

Out of curiosity, he opened it slowly before peeking out. Mydei stood off on the far end of the porch, oblivious to Phainon’s presence. The man began to make himself known until he saw Mydei was on the phone, and Phainon held his tongue.

“Cipher, don’t be ridiculous,” Mydei said. Phainon should really go, it’s rude to pry on people’s conversations. Especially when Mydei clearly went outside for a reason to take the call. Before he could pull away, Mydei continued. “That’s a big commitment to think about right now. In fact, I don’t even want to think about it. I’m twenty-three.”

Phainon froze.

He could feel his stomach drop the second the words left Mydei’s mouth.

He should’ve already been inside by now, waiting for Mydei to return. Now he couldn’t move, unable to leave until he received some sort of clarification. Anything to ease the guilt creeping inside of him.

“Uh huh,” Mydei nodded. “Still, one year isn’t enough time to consider something like that.”

One year.

Mydei mentioned assisting Phainon for at least another year, just until he could get access to his future restaurant. That was clear as day, and all of that talk about big commitment…

Mydei was talking about them.

It was the only way, because Phainon was aware of that fact before they even indulged each other. It was why he fought so hard to keep up his professionalism, because it wouldn’t be right to put any more responsibility on Mydei. Phainon knew from personal experience how big the commitment actually was, especially at that age.

Yet he still went against his word, allowing himself something for once.

Just because Phainon saw a future with Mydei, that never meant the feeling was reciprocated.

He felt terrible. He was never being fair to Mydei.

He could hear Mydei finishing up his phone call, but he didn’t tune in on much of the specifics. All he could do was silently close the door, dragging himself to the couch as he waited for the man to come inside.

Mydei sighed, sliding his phone back into his pocket.

Cipher’s call hadn’t been anything dire. He made the mistake of bringing up his future plans last week, telling his friends and mother of the building that awaited him. His mother would send him theme suggestions, Castorice would send him potential chefs that he should reach out to, and Cipher?

Cipher apparently became an entrepreneur overnight.

She called to merely make a suggestion, insinuating Mydei look to create a chain restaurant instead. Something that wasn’t solely in one place.

Which isn’t his biggest concern right now.

Fortunately he was able to cut the conversation short. She was sure to mention it again at some point, but as long as he could finally get back inside, that’s all that mattered.

Once he stood in the living room, he immediately saw Phainon sitting on the couch. Whatever Clara needed must’ve already been taken care of, though it didn’t explain why Phainon was here. They still had groceries to put up.

“Ice cream melts, you know,” Mydei commented. “Probably shouldn’t leave it on the counter too long.”

Phainon didn’t smirk.

In fact, Phainon didn’t say anything at all.

Interesting.

Walking closer and noticing the serious expression on the man’s face, Mydei took a seat beside him. “What’s wrong?” Did something happen with Clara? She had been fine when they made it home, he wasn’t sure what could’ve changed in the span of ten minutes, if even that.

“Mydei,” Phainon began, staring straight ahead. “I… didn't realize how unfair I was being to you.”

Mydei pressed his brows together. Unfair? What was he talking about? Surely he wasn’t bent out of shape because Mydei was putting his groceries away. Mydei wouldn’t have done so if he truly didn’t mind. “It’s just groceries, Phainon.”

Phainon shook his head. “It’s not groceries.” Then Mydei would really love to know where this was coming from. “I should’ve known what would happen the moment me and you did something. The kind of impression it would give you.”

What?

“What are you saying?”

Phainon finally looked his way, giving Mydei a chance to see what was hidden behind his eyes. There was worry, along with something else he couldn’t quite place. “I don’t want to drive you away. You're the best babysitter that Clara has ever had and I don’t want to make you think I’m expecting any more from you.”

The words felt like a sudden blow to the chest.

‘You’re the best babysitter Clara has ever had.’

Babysitter.

That’s all.

Mydei’s heartbeat sped up and he swallowed. “I still don’t understand.” Or he did, but needed to hear the words come directly from Phainon’s mouth.

“I… never meant to make you feel like you owed me commitment. Us being together that night, it was just a simple thing. You don’t have to worry about anything else.”

Mydei genuinely felt like he could be sick. He refused to give Phainon that sort of reaction though, forcing it all down while he kept his impassiveness. “So that’s all it was? Us fucking?”

“Wasn’t it?” Phainon asked slowly. Carefully.

No. It was more than that, Phainon has always been more than that. “Right,” he answered quietly, forcing himself to sound as normal as possible. He stood from the couch, not bothering to spare the man another glance. “I have to go.”

“Wait,” Phainon interjected, his tone changing. “What? Mydei, talk to me.”

Mydei didn’t want to talk to him right now. Not after hearing that he was foolish enough to worry himself over his relationship with Phainon. A relationship that never existed, apparently, seeing as the man was basically telling him not to expect anything else.

There was no way he could stay the night. Mydei had gone through a lot of days with Phainon where he swept his own personal feelings aside. This was not one of those days.

He needed to leave now.

“I have to go,” Mydei repeated, grabbing his overnight bag.

“Mydei, wait,” Phainon pleaded. Any other time it would’ve worked, but Mydei was too embarrassed to even consider giving in to him right now. “Just talk to me. Why are you leaving, what happened to staying the weekend?”

That was before Mydei was essentially rejected.

“I don’t want to talk, I’m leaving,” Mydei said simply, heading towards the door. He never made it, not when the sight of Clara stepping into the living room appeared through his peripherals.

Mydei went still.

He slowly turned to her, watching as her bright smile fell as she made sense of what was happening. There was no way she didn’t know, Mydei was seconds away from walking out the front door with his bag in hand. That could’ve only meant one thing and she picked up on it immediately.

The look on her face pained him, nothing short of hurt. Her eyes watered the longer she stared at Mydei, what could’ve been the fatal hit to his already aching chest. She had been so excited for the weekend, eager to spend time with Mydei where she usually wouldn’t. Now what did it turn into?

Mydei walking out.

He knew he’d be disappointing her by leaving, and he specifically promised her that he would never do so.

But the embarrassment trumped whatever else he felt right now. It was only for the weekend, he’d see her again Monday. He'll make a new promise, one where he’d make it up to her. He just needed some time to think, to wrap his head around the fact that Mydei had been nothing but a good time to Phainon.

Without another word, he walked out of the door.

As soon as Mydei left the house, Phainon was forced to watch Clara run off to her room.

The note she had prepared for Mydei fell from her hands.

Phainon didn’t know what happened. He only started the conversation because he thought that’s what Mydei needed to hear. He was on the phone overthinking it with Cipher, Phainon was only trying to ease his worries so that they could enjoy the weekend.

Even if he didn’t mean it. Even if his words were far from true.

But they didn’t help Mydei at all. In fact, nothing Phainon could’ve said in that moment would have prevented him from leaving. That still didn’t stop him from trying, or even hoping that Clara’s presence would have changed his mind.

But it didn’t.

Phainon didn’t know when he’d hear from Mydei next.

He couldn’t think about that right now. Not when he needed to go be there for his daughter.

Phainon picked up her note that had fallen, taking slow and hesitant steps towards her room. He wasn’t sure what to tell her. He didn’t know how to explain why he was the reason she could no longer look forward to this weekend. Phainon might have been unfair to Mydei, but he was being even more unfair to her.

Once he approached the door, he gave a soft knock. “Baby?” He called out gently. “Can I come in?”

After a couple of seconds, she answered. “Yeah.”

It was faint, but Phainon heard it.

He stepped inside, chest tightening at the sight of her sitting on the edge of her bed. She held the picture from the carnival in her hands, unable to peel her attention away from it. Phainon began to approach her.

“Where did he go?”

Phainon exhaled, taking a seat beside her. “I don’t know.”

“Is he coming back?”

“I… don’t know.”

He didn’t know anything, apparently. She finally looked up at him, revealing her eyes that had been watering. It pained Phainon to see the tear roll down her cheek. “Did he leave because of me?”

It was the same thing she asked when Phainon told her the story of her mother.

It didn’t hurt any less.

“No, baby.” He reached forward, wiping the tear away. “It wasn’t because of you at all, don’t think that.”

“Then why?” She asked, voice cracking. “He promised he wouldn’t. Why did he?”

Phainon bit at the inside of his lip. He couldn’t let her believe it was something she had done, not when she was just the bystander in all of this. He shook his head. “Mydei left because of me. I said something to him and… I don’t think he took it the right way.”

She stared at him incredulously, another tear rolling down her cheek. Her bottom lip trembled. “How could you do that?”

Phainon didn’t know. He could say he thought he was doing what was needed but considering what it earned him, maybe his perception skills weren't all he made them out to be. “Come here,” he whispered, pulling her to his chest. He rubbed the back of her head, delicately brushing through her hair. “I’m so sorry.”

Clara sniffled against him. “What if he doesn’t want to come back?”

It was Mydei, he had to come back. Otherwise, Phainon would have to consider the alternative and he never wanted to do that. So, all he could say again was, “I don’t know.”

“I don’t want another babysitter. I just want Mydei.”

Phainon brought her closer, holding her while he remained silent. The words he wished to say went unspoken.

Me too. I just want him, too.

Chapter End Notes

For as long as he could remember, Mydei’s never doubted his perception skills.

He liked to think he was rather intuitive in that sense. He always felt like he could connect with people the most whenever he’d study their behavioral patterns. Their emotions, demeanor, everything they failed to say. He would connect all of those dots in his head, something he considered a great feat.

In hindsight, maybe Mydei just didn’t understand Phainon as much as he believed himself to.

He used to tell himself that there was a reason Phainon never mentioned anything of importance between them. That his relationship with his daughter came first before everything, even over a babysitter he swore was like no other before. Mydei never questioned it either, because it wasn’t his place to insinuate that they should ever push for anything else. Not when Phainon had responsibilities of his own.

It hadn’t occurred to him that it was never mentioned on the basis of unreciprocated feelings.

Mydei wished there would’ve been a sign. Anything that told him their relationship was purely physical, which would’ve saved him from the emotional turmoil he’s subjected himself to. It wouldn’t have stopped his lust completely, but Mydei would’ve never torn himself up over a man he knew he couldn’t have.

Us being together that night, it was just a simple thing.’

What a joke.

Mydei would’ve torn himself up regardless.

Phainon was more than just a simple thing. Phainon was the promise of what he’s never had the chance to feel, what he’s swallowed down for years due to his own stubbornness. He was admirable, living proof to Mydei that one could overcome a challenge and make the most of it. Phainon was passionate, devoutly loyal to those he cared about and would not think twice before making such a fact known.

But Phainon was also out of reach. Further than he’s ever been before.

Which should’ve been — no, was — a ridiculous thought. Mydei will be right back at the Khaslana house tomorrow, sending Phainon off to work like nothing had changed. Acting like they never fucked was one thing, but acting like he didn’t feel the way he did? Like there wasn’t disappointment seeping through him every time he thought back to that day?

Mydei always said he liked a challenge, but he never meant this kind.

On the bright side, Phainon wasn’t the only person Mydei had to worry about. On the not so bright side, the other person was Clara and Mydei knew a simple ‘sorry’ wouldn’t fix walking out like he did. Quite frankly, he refused to even consider settling for an apology, especially when the look on her face tore at his heart even more.

At the very least, he could focus on that first. Clara’s school had an off day tomorrow, meaning he’d get more time with her. Far more than he would with Phainon and he knew where his priorities should lie.

He had an entire day to think about it, as well as the help of his friends on his side.

It was doable.

“Let me ask you something, Mydei,” Cipher said, flopping down on the unoccupied sofa. Mydei took up the other, the length of his body lying across it while his head rested on Castorice’s lap. “Why are you forcing yourself to go tomorrow? Even the best babysitters can take a needed break.”

Among the options he’s weighed out already, that was never a consideration. His loyalty towards the family prevented it from even being a thought. “If I do that, I might as well tell him I’m avoiding him.”

She scoffed. “Not if you say you’re sick. Even you aren’t immune to the common cold.”

Obviously. Mydei didn’t know what she was getting at there, he’s been sick a handful of times. He sighed, shaking his head. “I already walked out on the weekend plans. I can’t do this too.”

“Weekend plans that you didn’t tell us about, by the way.”

“I didn’t know I was obligated.”

“Of course you’re obligated.”

“You’re not obligated,” Castorice chimed in, running her hands through Mydei’s hair as she played with the strands. “He’s a grown man with his own schedule. We can respect that, Cipher.”

“Boo,” Cipher drawled, rolling her eyes. “I’m just saying. I called Mydei out of the blue because I thought he wasn’t busy. If I would’ve known he was seconds away from being in Phainon’s bed, maybe I would’ve waited.”

First of all, Mydei was not seconds away from Phainon’s bed. They hadn’t even gotten through dinner at that time, tending to other matters. Hell, grocery bags were still sitting atop the counter when Phainon initiated their talk. Second of all, “there’s no point in worrying about it. Your phone call isn’t the reason Phainon got serious, so who cares?”

What the reason truly was, Mydei wished he knew.

“The point still stands,” Cipher said. “At the very least, you would’ve been inside to figure out what brought it on.”

Even if he had been inside, he doubted it would do much. Phainon had been in Clara’s room before Mydei found him on the couch. Whatever inspired him to have the conversation, there was no way Mydei could’ve known, much less prevented it.

Meaning it was always bound to end like that. The second Mydei began to wear his heart on his sleeve, Phainon would be there to hit him with the harsh truth. To throw the reality check that Mydei deluded himself would never come.

“It’s my fault. Next time I won’t lust after a single father.” As if Mydei would ever be put in this position again. If fate was really on his side, this would’ve been one of those predicaments that people loved to say happened for a reason.

Cipher frowned. “Well I wouldn’t say it’s your fault.”

Mydei huffed. “Then I’ll blame you.”

She sat upright, pointing to herself in disbelief. “My fault? What did I do? You just said my phone call had no impact.”

Mydei was obviously messing with her, only throwing out the accusation to lighten up and make himself feel a little better. “You’re the one who referred to him as a DILF. You corrupted me, made me think of things I shouldn’t have.”

Castorice snorted above him. “You know what?” Cipher asked, her smile thin. “Let’s go back to the part where you said it was your fault. Remember that?”

“It’s no one’s fault,” Castorice clarified.

Cipher cocked a brow. “Not even Phainon’s?”

“I mean…” Castorice trailed off and Mydei glanced up long enough to catch her in thought. Whatever was going through her brain, he’d prefer that over the brooding that he was doing in his own mind. “I can’t say for sure. Mydei, are you sure you understood him correctly?”

What was not to understand? Phainon sat him down and told Mydei that what they had was purely physical, that he shouldn’t bother to consider anything more. Even if it wasn’t that blunt, he could read between the lines to understand what Phainon was trying to say. That he must’ve sensed Mydei’s feelings from a mile away, shutting them down before they ever became an issue.

If there was another way to take that, Mydei would love to know.

“Loud and clear,” Mydei breathed out, finally sitting up.

Cipher stroked her chin. “Hm. Run it by us one more time.”

“I’ve already run it by you three times now.” There were only so many times he would openly relive his disappointment. “If you guys still can’t see it for what it is, then I don’t know what to say.” He appreciated their concern, he did, and appreciated even more that they were trying to turn it into something hopeful. Even if he couldn’t share the same sentiment.

Castorice took his words lightly, acknowledging him with a gentle look. “I’m only questioning it from what I’ve seen. You may not remember that night when you were drunk, but Phainon was really worried. The first thing he asked when I called was if you were okay.”

Mydei sucked his teeth, crossing his arms. “Probably because he didn’t want his favorite babysitter dying of alcohol poisoning.” The bitter emphasis was for his own good, as well as a reminder for them both.

“That was before I told him you were drunk,” Castorice countered.

Cipher nodded. “He also showed up fast. Like, really fast.” She then looked off to the side with furrowed brows. “Actually, I don’t know. I was also drunk, so maybe it only felt fast.”

Castorice tilted her head. “You’re not helping. Yes, Phainon did show up quickly. He also promised you were in good hands. You may perceive that how you like but at the end of the day, there was something else to it.”

That's exactly what Mydei had believed as well. All of those times Phainon extended an invite for dinner, or when Phainon allowed Mydei to join them on an annual tradition to the carnival. Mydei thought there was something else then too, but what he thought held little weight when he’s already heard the truth.

“He’s had bad experiences with babysitters,” Mydei said, deflecting. “Like I said, me dying from alcohol poisoning wouldn’t have been ideal. His daughter happens to like me.” Which may not be true anymore, considering Mydei practically broke her heart when he left. For all he knew, she could now see him as someone who had no qualms in going back on a promise.

Cipher sighed, a long and exaggerated thing. “No offense, but maybe you wouldn’t be in this situation if, you know, you two had a proper conversation. Like adults. Preferably after you woke up in his bed a week ago.”

In his defense, Mydei was too busy thinking about what that meant for him and Phainon. Not to mention Clara caught them before they even had the chance, and any time after just didn’t feel appropriate. Still, he looked in Castorice’s direction, hoping she would at least try to come to his aid.

Unfortunately, she didn’t budge.

“Well, I’m not going to say she’s wrong.”

Cipher’s eyes widened. “Wait, say that again.”

Castorice ignored her. “Your mother and I both mentioned that it would be wise to speak with him. If I would have known you’d let it pass for a week, I might’ve pushed for it more.”

It’s not like he ever intended for it to happen that way. Things just didn’t work that easily with Phainon, and would always get brushed aside before they ever had the opportunity to come up. If Mydei would’ve known that was for a reason, then he would’ve never been so open about what he felt. Even if it meant lying to his friends.

“I’d like to change the topic now.”

“Oh no,” Cipher retorted, shaking her head. “Don’t get all dismissive. It’s time for you to own up to your actions, little prince.”

He scowled. “What actions? Communication works both ways, I don’t see you giving Phainon a hard time about not mentioning anything.” Because how many times did Mydei have to reiterate that there was only so much in his control?

“That’s a good idea, actually. Send me his address.” As much as Mydei would love to do so, it wasn’t fair to hold anything against Phainon. Allowing everything to be in the man’s control meant allowing himself to receive rejection. Even if he didn’t like it. Cipher continued, “I still think you should’ve listened to us, though.”

“‘Us?’” Mydei parroted in disbelief. “You mean my mother and Castorice? You were too busy calling me a step-mother and asking if I’d be getting a round-two.” Which was a no, by the way. Clearly.

Cipher threw her hands up in defense. “And now I’m saying you should’ve talked to him.”

It didn’t matter now. Mydei knew Phainon’s true feelings and the former had to show up at his house in the morning, pretending it didn’t bother him. Listening to old advice wouldn’t undo any of that. He was better off doing as he previously planned, mulling over what he’d say to Clara. At least he could still enjoy his job if their relationship stayed the same.

Mydei barely noticed the pointed look that Castorice sent Cipher. The latter exhaled and continued. “Look, just go about your life and do what you get paid for. Maybe this way you’ll finally listen to my words of wisdom and let Phainon be the first to come to you.”

Those words had little effect considering they were built on Mydei’s improper thoughts. Thoughts that slowly molded into real feelings and while Mydei was coming to terms with it, Phainon was only in it for his own fantasies.

Needless to say, Mydei didn’t really feel like considering her ‘words of wisdom.’

“Sure. Now can we change the subject?”

Cipher rolled her eyes.

Five minutes. Mydei has been sitting in Phainon’s driveway for five minutes and despite it all, he’s yet to find the will to get out of the car. To walk in and do his job, something he’s done several times over. Where this would be second nature, it now only felt like impending doom.

There was no telling how Phainon would react upon seeing him when the last thing he said to him were pleas for Mydei not to leave. As much as he wanted to prolong that reaction, avoiding it would only make him look incompetent. Mydei couldn’t start slacking off just because Phainon told him what he didn’t want to hear.

So, he stepped out of the car, slow steps leading him closer to the porch. The key felt out of place in his hands as he retrieved it from his pocket, before carefully inserting it into the lock. He wasn’t sure if it was due to his own hesitance, or simply because he didn’t want to bring a lot of attention to himself.

Considering he’d make his presence known eventually, it was rather pointless.

Any other time, Mydei knew what awaited him on the other side. He’d find Phainon standing in the mirror, adjusting himself while throwing a sly comment Mydei’s way. Or, he’d be seated on the couch with Clara by his side, the little girl beaming once Mydei stepped inside.

Today, Mydei would be lucky if he even got a smile from her.

He finally pushed the door open, taking a deep breath before passing the threshold.

Much to his surprise, the living room was empty. No one stood in the mirror and the couch was completely unoccupied, save for the remnant memory of the conversation he had with Phainon that day.

This wasn’t the time to think about that. Before he could even wonder where anyone was, the first sound of footsteps forced him to turn around.

The moment he and Phainon made eye contact, he felt his body stiffen. Phainon’s reaction wasn’t any better, freezing in his tracks as surprise slowly began to wash over him. Neither one of them said a word at first, allowing the heavy silence to loom over their heads as they remained in place.

Then, Phainon swallowed, his next words almost forced.

“You came…”

Mydei wanted to question it. He wanted to ask when he could have given the impression that he wouldn’t, but Mydei wasn’t naive. He left their house without so much of an explanation and to anyone else, that would’ve no doubt come off as if he never intended on returning.

Mydei had done that before. It happened with his parents and if Mydei didn’t run into his mother in the park, it might have stayed that way.

But Mydei didn’t leave this time. He stayed, and no amount of indirect rejection would have ever caused him not to come back.

“Of course I did.”

Phainon still seemed taken aback, before his expression shifted into something else. Shock had turned into concern and if Phainon was really considering offering his pity, then Mydei would prefer if he kept it to himself. It was one thing to be reminded of their conversation, but to relive it was another.

“I just…” Phainon trailed off, shaking his head. “I don’t… I mean, you–”

Mydei never gave him the chance to finish. “I don’t want to talk about it.”

He knew he had to talk about it. This just wasn’t the time, not before Phainon had to go to work and definitely not before he had the chance to fix things with Clara. He would just have to keep disappointing Castorice and Cipher by putting it off.

Phainon frowned. “I don’t know what to say then, Mydei.”

Mydei didn’t want him to say anything, that was the whole point in not talking about it. He would rather focus on something else, like how ironic it was that Phainon was so shocked by his arrival. If he truly never expected Mydei to be here today, then there’s no way he would’ve left without finding another sitter. Either he did and they hadn’t showed up yet, or–

“You knew I would be here today.”

Phainon furrowed his brows. “What?”

“You knew I would be here,” Mydei repeated. “Otherwise, someone else would be.”

Unless Phainon planned on taking Clara with him, which wouldn’t be ideal considering his work place wasn’t the most entertaining spot for a six year old. Mydei didn’t think Phainon would subject her to that.

“I didn’t know,” Phainon said, his voice growing quiet. “I just really hoped.”

Mydei eyed him skeptically. “You? Or…”

Phainon looked offended. “Yes, Mydei. Me.”

Mydei could never be too sure. After all, Phainon made it a point to bring up how he was the best babysitter Clara has ever had. Maybe he had just been looking out for his daughter, voicing what she wished for instead.

“Well, I’m here,” he said simply, barely masking his impassiveness. It wouldn’t have been fair to take his feelings out on Phainon, anyway.

Phainon nodded slowly. “And… you don’t want to talk about it?”

‘It,’ being the sole reason Mydei left in the first place. Of course he didn’t want to talk about it. “I do not.”

“Alright,” Phainon agreed, albeit reluctantly. It was for the best, this wasn’t the time for him to act on instinct and be persistent, as he usually would. “I’ll respect your wishes.”

“Thank you.”

Once again, silence enveloped them. Phainon no longer made an attempt to joke with him, in fact, there was no banter to be had at all. Mydei was fortunate enough that it was Clara he was spending the day with.

Clara, who softly padded into the living room, stopping when her eyes landed on Mydei.

She looked just as surprised as Phainon did. The only difference was, she said nothing at all.

Maybe he wasn’t so fortunate.

“I’m about to head out, baby,” Phainon spoke softly, addressing his daughter. She barely acknowledged the comment, giving a small nod while she continued to look at Mydei. He wanted to say that she was also relieved to see him, that she had also hoped he would be here just like Phainon did.

It was hard to tell when the only thing Mydei could sense was hurt.

Mydei watched as Phainon made his way to the front door, unsure if he should say anything else. He’d normally poke fun at him with Clara’s assistance, teasing the man before he could step outside. Now, he didn’t think he could get a word out until Phainon was gone.

Phainon took the initiative instead, halting long enough to glance over his shoulder. “Call if you need anything?”

Phainon didn't have to tell him that. Since the first week, that much has always gone without saying. If that was the only thing the man could think of at that moment, then salvaging what they had would be harder than Mydei thought.

Mydei didn’t offer anything in response. Instead, he turned his head and listened as Phainon left the house.

Clara’s eyes were still fixed on him.

He couldn’t start with an apology. Mydei already convinced himself that a simple ‘sorry’ wouldn’t fix what he did, that she still lost a weekend she clearly looked forward to because of him. He didn’t expect to automatically make it up to her within the first ten minutes and even if an entire day didn’t fix it, he had to start somewhere.

So, he gave her a small smile. “Hey.”

She didn’t return the gesture, but she did finally speak. “Hey.”

That was something. At least he could rest easy knowing he wasn’t getting the silent treatment. “How are you feeling?” Part of him likely knew the answer to that, but he couldn’t outright joke with her as he usually would. He would have to earn that back if she chooses to forgive him for leaving.

“Okay,” she shrugged. “No school today, so I’m happy about that.”

Mydei huffed in amusement. She didn’t sound light-hearted by any means, but it was enough for him. “I bet. You’re lucky, you’ve had a lot of days off here lately.” Considering three of those days were due to her suspension, that wasn’t luck at all, but a step was a step.

Clara didn’t laugh. In fact, she ignored his statement completely. “Are you mad at daddy?”

The words hit Mydei like a truck.

There were a lot of questions Mydei imagined her asking. They were mainly along the lines of his reasoning for leaving, or why he would break the promise he made with her. Mydei thought he was prepared for any of those, because he valued his relationship with her enough to plan for things like that. He only spent the better part of his night thinking it over.

Oh, how wrong he was.

“Should I be?”

It wasn’t the best he could give her and while he knew the truth, that he wasn’t mad at Phainon, he’d like to know why she’d come to that conclusion.

She shrugged once more. “Daddy said he hurt you. That’s why you left.”

Phainon was aware his words affected Mydei. Phainon was aware he didn’t handle it well. If Mydei thought about it too long, that could arguably be worse than rejection.

Mydei sighed. He stepped closer to the couch, taking a seat before gently patting the space beside him. Much to his relief, she plopped down. “I’m not upset with him,” Mydei began, shaking his head. He couldn’t tell her everything, but he cared enough to at least be honest with what he could say. “Phainon and I had a… disagreement.”

Chalking their different stances on personal feelings didn’t feel right. Then again, none of this did and it was all he could offer.

She looked down at her lap. “You’re supposed to talk about your disagreements.”

Castorice and Cipher said the same thing. “You’re right, we should have.” There was nothing at the time that Mydei wanted to discuss, his embarrassment already pushing him out of the door, but he couldn’t say she was wrong.

“I’m not mad at you.”

Mydei looked over, brows raised. “You’re not?”

“No,” she replied, firm enough that Mydei didn’t even have to question it. “I don’t think I could ever be mad at you.”

They were reassuring words and Mydei was lucky enough to hear them right now, but that didn't make them hurt any less. He ruined the weekend that she had been excited for, yet she still held the same admiration towards him. He almost wanted to say he didn’t deserve that much, but all he could do was force a smile.

“I’m glad to hear that.”

“Daddy didn’t mean to hurt your feelings,” she continued. Mydei’s face slowly dropped, uncertain if he wanted to hear what exactly Phainon thought about him. He’d like to say that he’s heard enough. “He would never hurt someone he loves on purpose.”

Mydei froze.

She hadn’t looked at him yet, too focused on her lap to do so, but Mydei stared at her as the words failed to register in his mind. They played on a constant loop and he knew he shouldn’t take it too seriously, it wouldn’t be far-fetched to assume she didn’t understand the weight of what she said.

But Mydei had always known she was smart. She would never thoughtlessly say something she believed to be untrue.

“What did you just say?”

She finally glanced up, her face twisting into confusion as she picked up on Mydei’s surprise. “What? He didn’t mean to hurt you.”

“No,” he said, shaking his head. “The… other thing.”

“He wouldn’t hurt someone he loves?”

Someone he loves.

Loves.

It was a word thrown out by a little girl who had only ever used it in the familial sense. Mydei should be taking it lightly, focusing more so on the fact that Phainon held no hard feelings towards him.

Someone he loves.

That was all he could hear.

“Why do you look shocked?” Because he was, because Phainon’s feelings were making themselves known from the one person who knew him better than anyone. He could dismiss it due to her misunderstanding or age, but she had never been wrong when it came to her own father.

There was only one of two ways she could have meant it. In the way she was familiar with, or the way Mydei had never considered being a possibility. His conversation with Phainon three days ago only solidified that belief.

“I just didn’t expect it,” he admitted, his throat going dry.

“You didn’t already know?”

No, he didn’t. And he wasn’t aware he was supposed to. “I… haven’t heard that from him, no.”

Clara looked away. “I thought he told you.”

Every response that came from her mouth caught him more off guard than the last and Mydei had no time to process any of it. This entire conversation had gone the exact opposite as he planned, which would’ve been a good thing if his head weren’t reeling right now.

“He never told me either,” she said, filling his silence. “But daddy never had someone like you in his life. He looks at you differently than everyone else.”

Phainon would look at him a lot, actually. Partially when Mydei wasn’t looking, but mainly when he knew the blond was aware. He had no shame in being caught. Mydei used to say it was for a reason, convincing himself that he knew what it was.

After their conversation, Mydei just assumed it had always been out of attraction.

He didn’t really want to talk about this anymore, he’s already been wrong about Phainon’s feelings once. Even if she picked up on him changing the subject, at least he’d be doing himself the favor.

“Hey. I remember there was something you wanted to give to me that day.” If Mydei recalled correctly, there had been a piece of paper in her hands.

If he was lucky, she hadn’t thrown it away by now.

“Oh. Right.” He didn’t know how to take that. He didn’t have to wonder too long, though, when Clara began to dig through her pockets, pulling out a folded slip of paper. “Here you go.”

The corner of his lips tugged upwards. “You were prepared.”

“I didn’t know if you would be here today.” She looked down at her lap again, fiddling with her hands. “I wanted to always keep it on me in case I saw you again.”

Mydei was no longer smiling. Instead, he felt nothing but the same guilt he had when he watched her expression fall in realization that day. With slow hands, he began to unfold the paper.

“Wait,” she said, grabbing onto his arm to stop him. “Don’t read it now.” Mydei did as he was told, refraining himself from opening the note any more. He folded it back, safely securing it into his own pocket. “Thank you. I’ll let you open it when the time is right.”

Mydei could live with that. He had always trusted her judgment. “Just say the word.”

“I will,” she confirmed. “Promise.”

She didn’t hold up a pinky this time. He hoped that wasn’t for a reason, that he didn’t ruin it when he broke the last one.

“Well,” he said, brushing it aside for now so that he wouldn’t grow curious. “Is there anything you want to do today? You said it yourself, you don’t have any school to worry about right now.”

Clara looked off to the side, thinking about it. “Hm. Can we go to the park and try to spot bunnies?”

It was like nothing had changed.

Mydei wouldn’t want it any other way.

“You got it. I even have a trick to attract them, so we can buy them snacks.” Her eyes lit up. Before she had the chance to express her excitement, uncertainty clouded her eyes. Mydei couldn’t help but worry, assuming his attempts wouldn’t be enough.

“Can you… also braid my hair?”

Mydei could’ve let out a relieved sigh. Instead, he smiled. “Yeah. Of course I can.”

“If you zone out any harder, I’ll start thinking you hate our weekly lunches.”

Phainon’s eyes shot up, his focus becoming clear as he took in the curious expression on Hyacine's face. He relaxed immediately, though the long exhale that fell from his lips could only be in shame. It wasn’t the first time he spaced out during one of their meals and with how things were going with Mydei, it wouldn’t be last. That still didn't ease any guilt.

Besides, Hyacine wasn't the only person at the table he was ignoring.

Aglaea shook her head. “Haven’t I told you it’s rude to tune people out?”

He fought back a wince. When the woman offered to join them for lunch, claiming she had the free time, the least he could’ve done was prepare for it. Not sit there, wallowing in his own thoughts. “Sorry,” he said. “I was—”

“Thinking?” Hyacine finished for him, smirking.

He forced an amused huff. “What gave it away?”

“Gee, I wonder.” He was grateful Hyacine hadn’t taken it the wrong way, because it wasn’t her fault that he wasn’t fully present at the moment. “You have this certain look when you’re thinking really hard about something. Makes you look like you’re going to pop a blood vessel.”

“Is that possible?” He asked.

She deadpanned. “Don’t redirect. Seriously, what’s wrong? You were in a good mood last week, what changed?”

That was because Phainon had the memory of an amazing weekend to get him through the week. He would start every day reminding himself that he had Mydei in his bed, that his dreams become a reality in the span of a day. There was nothing that could have dimmed his mood, because nothing could hold a candle to the man he was allowed to share a night with.

This week, Phainon had a different weekend memory and unfortunately, it wasn’t one that could get him through it. It was one that invoked many questions within him, as well as awkwardness with that very same man.

There was bound to be a contrast in his behavior.

He couldn’t openly share that, though, and it wasn’t their responsibility to deal with his inner turmoil. He knew he could confide in them, but would have only done so if he could make sense of it in his own head. He was sure he had done the right thing but until Mydei explained why he left, there was no way that would happen.

“I’m fine,” he lied. “Just work.”

Hyacine hummed, not buying it for a second. Phainon couldn’t blame her, he was very open when it came to his problems at work. “Would I be presumptuous to assume it’s about Mydei?”

Aglaea raised a brow. “The babysitter?” The babysitter. As if Mydei could ever be narrowed down to such a title. Ironic that Phainon had done exactly that three days ago, when he knew Mydei would always be more than that. “Though I believe the correct term is ‘nanny.’”

“Really?” Phainon asked, unaware that he hadn’t acknowledged either of their questions.

She nodded. “I won’t get into the logistics of it all, but yes.”

It didn’t matter what the term was. The logistics were that Mydei would never be Phainon’s, so the correct use of any word didn’t mean much right now.

“You’re changing the topic again,” Hyacine chimed in. He was only doing so because there was so much he had made known to them. He wouldn’t choose now to reveal that his attraction towards Mydei evolved into something more, if they couldn’t pick up on it already.

Phainon sighed. “It’s not about Mydei.”

It was about Mydei. It was always about him.

“If you say so,” Hyacine muttered.

Aglaea took a quick sip of her drink. “Am I to sit here and assume you have feelings for this man?”

Hyacine waved her off. “Don’t bother asking. He’ll never give anything away.” Well, that was arguably untrue. He’s just never outright admitted it because doing so made it real. It meant he would have acknowledged wanting more, when Phainon whole-heartedly believed it wasn’t fair for him to do so.

Phainon was prepared to at least try and defend himself when the sight of two people in the distance caught his eye. He wouldn’t have spared them another glance had it been anyone else, but there was no mistaking what was in front of him. Even if his interactions with Castorice and Cipher were limited, Phainon was certain of what he was seeing.

“No way,” he whispered, more so to himself.

“Nuh uh,” Hyacine refuted, making no attempt to follow his line of sight. “I’m not falling for it.”

“There’s nothing to fall for,” he said. “Mydei’s friends are here.” He hoped she wouldn’t turn around, or at least draw too much attention to the table. He wasn’t actively avoiding the two of them, but with his conflicting emotions concerning Mydei, he wasn’t sure how he would fare in their presence.

However, there was no use in hoping. Cipher had already noticed him before Hyacine had the chance to confirm Phainon’s observations.

Cipher’s eyes widened once she realized it was him. He couldn’t hear what she was saying to Castorice, though he could see the latter attempt to hold her back. Phainon assumed she was doing so in courtesy, Castorice seemed like the type to avoid any intrusion. Even if it wouldn’t be an intrusion at all, just an awkward encounter on Phainon’s part.

Her efforts had little impact, the two of them gradually closing in on the table. Hyacine and Aglaea sat expectantly, waiting for them to join while Phainon quietly considered what he would say.

Or better yet, what they knew.

“Look who it is,” Cipher greeted, smirking as she crossed her arms. Phainon had only seen her twice, once in the shoe store and the other while she was drunk, though he’s never had a full conversation with her. “Small world, huh?”

Castorice tugged on her arm. “Cipher, let’s not bother them.”

“You’re not bothering us,” Hyacine assured, smiling at the two. “Phainon said you’re Mydei’s friends, right? This is Aglaea, I’m Hyacine.”

“I see,” Cipher responded quietly. She narrowed her eyes, glancing back and forth between Phainon and Hyacine. “Girlfriend?”

“Cipher,” Castorice muttered in warning.

“No,” Phainon answered, a little too hastily.

“Absolutely not,” Hyacine added, shutting it down as well. Phainon was also too focused on getting the point across to take any offense from her implication. “No, Phainon and I are just friends.” At least he could count on her to save the situation. “Besides, Phainon sort of has his eyes on someone else right now.”

Never mind.

He shot her a look, barely noticing Castorice and Cipher share one between themselves. Phainon forced a laugh. “Let’s not start airing my dirty laundry, now.”

“Hey, I wouldn’t say Mydei is considered ‘dirty laundry,’ Cipher said.

Phainon shook his head. “Of course not, I just mean…” He trailed off, eyes widening in horror once he realized what he had done. He could’ve questioned how Cipher had come to the conclusion, but he wasn’t any better considering he fellt right into her trap. “Wait, I didn’t—”

“I knew it!” She exclaimed, turning towards Castorice. “See? See??”

The latter sighed. “Please keep your voice down.”

“What do you mean, you ‘knew it?’” Phainon asked, his subtle attempt of moving the topic away from his slip-up. As if he’d get off that easily. “You just assumed me and Hyacine were together.”

“To catch you off guard.”

“You okay?” Phainon asked. Mydei lifted up just enough to slide his pants back into place, giving himself at least some modesty. Phainon took the chance to do the same, covering himself with his own bottoms.

“Fine,” Mydei breathed out. He was, despite the range of emotions he was forced to feel today. Phainon may have initiated the conversation against Mydei’s wishes, but he wouldn’t lie and say he regretted it when this was the outcome.

Phainon nodded. “Good. Now we can talk.”

“If you treat what happened earlier as pillow talk, I might actually kill you”

“If you must,” Phainon shrugged. “I’m serious, Mydei. Before we got a little… distracted…” That being an understatement, considering Mydei had his third orgasm at the hands of Phainon. “We still need to talk about us.”

How cruel of him, to bring it up when Mydei didn’t feel like moving at all. He didn't have the energy to do so. “Whatever. Go ahead.” At the very least, it beat any awkwardness they would’ve dealt with tomorrow and things had partially cleared up before they ‘got distracted.’

“Did you… take my words as a rejection?”

Mydei scoffed. “They were a rejection.”

“No they weren’t,” Phainon countered. “I would never reject you. I could’ve driven myself crazy with how badly I wanted you, and not just like this.” Mydei avoided eye contact, unable to say anything as Phainon continued to pour his heart out. “You’ve always meant a lot to me.”

Mydei swallowed, forcing an even voice. “As the babysitter, of course.”

Phainon laughed. “Well, Aglaea would refer to it as a ‘nanny,’ but no. Not even that. As someone who is special to me, who I trust with my life and trust even more with my daughter. Someone that she can look up to.”

Mydei didn’t know how to respond. He wasn’t used to Phainon being so open and before today, he had only known the opposite. They never delved into their own feelings and he knew he should give something back, even just to assure Phainon that he wasn’t alone in this. That nothing was truly unreciprocated.

“I feel the same,” he said, still not looking at Phainon. “You and Clara hold special places in my life as well.”

Phainon allowed himself a moment of shock before he smiled, leaning into Mydei’s space. “Say it again, I didn’t hear you.”

“Don’t push it,” Mydei warned.

Phainon chuckled before addressing Mydei slightly more seriously. “Speaking of Clara, she wanted me to tell you to read the letter now.”

Mydei narrowed his eyes. “So she knew you were coming here.” It wasn’t a question, but an observation.

“She did,” Phainon confirmed. “Told her I’d fix things with you. That’s why she’s giving you the go ahead.”

“Rather confident of you.” Seriously, Mydei could have closed the door in his face and none of this would have happened. There was no way he could’ve known they’d start spilling the truth out, before Phainon was spilling onto his thighs.

Phainon smirked. “I made her a pinky promise. You know how I feel about those.”

“Idiot,” Mydei mumbled. He dug into his pockets, retrieving the paper from earlier. He shot Phainon one final glance before undoing the folds, rotating the note accordingly so that he could read it straight. He seemed to have no issues making out the words, finding it to be rather eligible.

‘Dear Mydei,

Daddy is helping me write this so it is perfect. Thank you for everything you do for me and being the best person I know. I love every single day that me and you spend together. I love making jokes about daddy with you. I love going to the park and I love when you cook for us. I love when you braid my hair like yours because I love looking like you. I love when you teach me new things and I love when you put me to bed. I love all of those things but what I love the most is you Dei. I hope you are always in my life.

From your best friend,

Clara.’

Mydei knew the small, wet dot that appeared in the middle could’ve only been one thing. Phainon was quick to realize it, too.

“Mydei, are you crying?”

He probably was. Mydei was too busy smiling at the letter to care. “I’m just reading.”

“You’re crying.”

Mydei snapped his head to the right. “Phainon.”

“Sorry,” Phainon said quietly. “It’s okay. I might have teared up helping her write it, too.” Mydei’s chest swelled with warmth. He remembered how excited Clara had been as she ran to her room, preparing Mydei’s surprise for him. How he wished he could’ve received it that day, in place of him letting her down.

Mydei scoffed, though there was no malice. “And you still sat me down on the couch to have that conversation with me.”

“In my defense—”

“Yeah, yeah,” Mydei waved him off, reading the letter again. He knew the second that he saw her tomorrow, he owed her the biggest hug yet. One that he would initiate this time, not the other way around.

Phainon hummed. “And the phone call?”

“Restaurant chains. It was about restaurant chains.”

Phainon looked off to the side. “Damn.”

“Yeah.”

He could feel Phainon watching him as he read, allowing Mydei enough time to finish before carefully speaking. “Mydei, what does this mean for us?” Mydei glanced up, holding the letter close to his chest as he studied Phainon’s face. “Because I’d be lucky to share my life with you, but I want you to want it too.”

Mydei thought he had been pretty obvious by now.

“I want it, Phainon.”

He’s never been more sure about anything in his life.

Phainon relaxed, and if Mydei didn’t know any better, he would assume Phainon would be the one to start crying now. “You don’t know how happy that makes me.”

Mydei narrowed his eyes. “You know this means I can’t work for you anymore, right?” Fortunately, Phainon had paid him enough for Mydei to start saving. He could use that for the time being as he found something else. If he was going to be a part of Phainon’s life, it would no longer be something he received money for.

Phainon nodded slowly. “Right. Because it would be unethical for your boss to get you pregnant.”

“Hey, Phainon?”

“Yes, dear?”

Mydei shoved him off of the couch.

Chapter End Notes

Shoutout Cipher?
