Chapter Summary

A year and a few months later

Chapter Notes

First of all, I want to preface this by apologizing for the late update. I mentioned on my Twitter that I had a pretty serious health emergency, so it killed me not being able to be there for Dilfnon Friday.

Anyway, I can’t believe the story has finally come to an end T_T Each week has been such a fun ride, from watching you guys point out their obvious sexual tension to you guys calling Phainon the fumbler of the century. I’m so beyond thankful for the love and reach this fic has gotten, and I hope this last chapter is a good finale for our fav family of destruction :’)

I also want to thank the artist who have gone out of their way to recreate certain scenes. You guys are INSANELY talented and I’m so lucky that talent was extended towards this fic.

Shoutout to my beta reader as well, for not just this chapter but every chapter before. They were pretty lengthy so it means the world.

Again, thank you all for taking the time to read <3 Currently working on another story that should be published soon, so if you’re there, I hope you can also enjoy that as well.

You guys are the best, love you all <3

The longer Mydei stood off to the side, the harder it was to find the words.

There’s been countless moments in his life where he was rendered speechless, oftentimes in the face of something so sudden that he could not prepare for. Things that he’d never given any thought before and amidst his surprise, he’d conjure up the right thing to say eventually.

That had gotten easier over time, Mydei was not the kind to make a fool of himself and being speechless didn’t equate to being unable to think.

Until now.

Now, Mydei was unable to process anything that was right in front of him.

He should’ve been able to, he had only dreamed of this moment for so long and one would think he would have a proper idea on how to handle it. Then again, Mydei’s never had a dream this big come true, thus making it hard to pull from any experience.

But this was real. For the first time in his life, Mydei could say he owned a restaurant.

He owned a restaurant, it belonged to him.

Of course he wouldn’t be able to wrap his head around it yet.

He had managed to keep his personal feelings in check, remaining his calm and collected self as he greeted the guests of the unofficial launch. Public access wasn’t for another three days, but still seeing the building occupied and full was a surreal thing.

The opening party wasn’t anything extraordinary, just a few family and friends to celebrate the milestone. Phainon was responsible for the majority of the guest list, even extending invites to his respected colleagues under Mydei’s approval. Besides his friends and parents, Mydei only invited the people who needed to be there; his cooks, his sponsors, and anyone else he had to thank for the future of the place.

In hindsight, it was a good thing his boyfriend was more of a social butterfly than him.

Said boyfriend who was currently nowhere to be seen, presumably ensuring everyone else was enjoying themselves. Phainon promised he would take that much off Mydei’s shoulders, as if Mydei really would’ve minded it. He was already finished with the hard part, this was nothing.

It didn’t matter, it gave Mydei the chance to step back and savor everything for a minute.

Everything was exactly as he imagined with the restaurant capturing the perfect amount of class he aimed for. Gold lighting created an ambient atmosphere that was both cozy and elegant, which was sure to encourage patrons to relax longer. Crimson, velvety booths lined the walls of the room, accompanied by a rounded bar centered in the middle.

The floor rose into another platform towards the back, leading customers to a more spacious area, with maroon curtains draping as an entryway. The event tonight didn’t call for any need for that particular room, but he’s already walked many people through it as he gave a tour of the place.

Additional accents were scattered among the walls, to further emphasize the reds and golds. They weren’t overdone, only enough to bring life to the place without overwhelming anyone who might look.

In short, it was perfect. Exactly what Mydei had wanted. By the way everyone around him seemed to admire the place, it was safe to say they were also satisfied.

Through his peripherals, Mydei caught sight of his mother. She stood at a booth that Aglaea currently occupied, chatting with the woman about who knows what. Mydei wouldn’t let his curiosity get the better of him and besides, they weren’t alone. Mydei’s father stood right there with them.

Because yeah, that happened too.

Much to anyone’s surprise, Mydei mending his relationship with Eurypon was on his own accord. His mother kept her word and never pushed for them to meet up, only assuring Mydei that the man wasn’t who he used to be.

After a while, Mydei gave in to see for himself.

Talking with his father after so long went much differently than it had with his mother. Where she was blunt and teasing, Eurypon was reserved and hard to get a read on. As if he were the one who ghosted Mydei for years rather than the other way around. The two men were stubborn when it came to expressing their feelings but were lucky enough that Gorgo was there to ease the tension.

It was only thanks to her that Mydei started to open up more.

He was rather brief when he did so, but he revealed everything to his father. His relationship with Phainon, his upcoming business plan, anything else that meant everything to Mydei. Eurypon had been supportive of it in his own way, which meant proposing a collaboration between their businesses.

Mydei couldn’t say he was surprised. Instead, he only huffed it off and declined. His father understood and his feelings remained the same.

Mydei had Phainon to thank for a lot of his change in perspective. It was his man that presented him with multiple opportunities that changed his life, rendering Mydei to become more open minded than he had been. As much as he loved to poke fun at Phainon, that was a fact he would never deny.

Mydei searched for Phainon next, finding him conversing with a coworker as he grinned ear to ear. There was no telling what prompted the emotion, not when he had been happy for Mydei the entire night. The blond sighed and hoped he continued to see that reaction.

Especially considering there was one last thing Mydei had to tell him tonight.

Speaking of, he looked for Cipher next. He found her immediately, arm slung around Castorice while they stood off to the side with Hyacine.

He braced himself and began walking their way.

“Oh, look,” Cipher announced, crossing her arms. “The host finally makes himself known after I was just saying that you were probably hiding in a corner. Thanks a lot.”

Mydei furrowed his brow. “I’ve been out here the whole time.”

“Dude. Did you come here to contradict me or did you have a reason?”

He rolled his eyes and Castorice piped up. “Everyone’s having a great time, Mydei. You should’ve seen Clara, she’s running around with more samples so she can pretend she works here.” Mydei couldn’t help but smile at that, recalling how excited the girl had been during the remodeling process.

“I’ll have to compensate her. Maybe even give her a raise afterward.”

Cipher looked around frantically. “That’s all it takes? Quick, Cas, go find me a sample platter. I have work to do.”

Castorice simply shook her head and Mydei rolled his eyes once more. “Look, about Clara, I have a favor to ask you. Any of you, actually.”

“Is everything okay?” Hyacine asked.

Everything was perfect, exactly how it needed to be. There was just one final thing Mydei had to do to finalize that. “Everything is fine. I was wondering if any one of you could watch her tonight. If not, I can ask my parents.” And if that didn’t work, Aglaea was always an option, too.

Cipher wiggled her brows. “Let me guess, you and Phainon are going to be celebrating all night?”

If he assumed correctly, then yes. He knew his boyfriend through and through, so she wasn’t wrong. It still didn’t stop him from scoffing. “I have to talk with him tonight about something important.”

“Something bad?” Castorice wondered.

“Not exactly.”

“Something good?”

“You could say that.”

Cipher snorted. “What, are you pregnant or something?” Mydei froze. Then, he averted his gaze, looking anywhere else but the direction of the three women in front of him.

Which had honestly been his first mistake.

“Oh… my god,” Hyacine breathed out.

Castorice placed a hand over her mouth, followed by a soft gasp as her eyes trailed down to Mydei’s stomach. “Mydei, is it true? Are you really…” He could tell she was avoiding the word for his own secrecy and he finally turned towards them.

“Mhm.”

“‘Mhm?’” Cipher parroted in disbelief. “You drop a bomb on us this big and all you can say is ‘mhm?’ What the hell dude, at least say we’re the first ones to know!”

Mydei pursed his lips. “Can’t do that.”

“And why not?”

He shrugged. “Because Clara was the first to know.”

Mydei remembered the conversation vividly. Once he found out the news, he waited until Phainon had gone to work before sitting her down. He absentmindedly asked how she would feel about a baby sibling, severely underestimating how smart she was. The next thing he knew, she was picking up on the hint and jumping into his arms immediately.

The last time he remembered seeing her that happy was when Mydei revealed his relationship with her father.

“What?” Cipher exclaimed, jaw dropped.

“Hush,” he hissed, looking around to make sure they hadn’t drawn any attention to themselves. The last thing he needed was for anyone to accidentally find out. He wasn’t purposely hiding the news, only intending for it to be known after he finally told Phainon.

Afterwards? He would gladly tell anyone, because he was having Phainon’s baby. Something he’s dreamed of for the longest —literally — and was not ashamed to admit now that it had finally become a reality.

“I just can’t believe it,” Cipher said, shaking her head. “All that time I spent joking about him knocking you up and he actually did it.” It was only a matter of time, they stopped taking precautions once Mydei was reaching a good point in his career. That had been the only thing postponing them.

Once Mydei gave the go ahead, he could see the fire ignite in Phainon’s eyes. Their sex grew hungrier, the two of them chasing something they both desperately wanted.

Mydei shrugged. “It was always the plan.”

“Right,” Cipher nodded. “And I bet— wait a second.” She paused, narrowing her eyes before directing her pointer finger towards him. “Conception can take two weeks. Two weeks ago was Phainon’s birthday. Did you…” Mydei looked away. Again, his mistake. “You… have zero shame. Like, none.”

No, he didn’t. The sex the two of them had on Phainon’s birthday was enough to make Mydei’s legs weak just thinking about it. It wasn’t intended to be that rough, either. Mydei teased and called him an old man which resulted in Phainon proving himself to be anything but.

Needless to say, they fucked all night, until it was no longer the man’s birthday.

“Can you babysit or not?”

Cipher sighed. “Fine. Deflect all you want, I know the truth.”

“We would be happy to watch her, Mydei,” Hyacine offered. “Maybe we all can have a girls weekend. I do have to ask, if Clara already knows the truth, why would she need to be out of the house?”

Mydei said nothing. Unfortunately for him, that meant Cipher would take the reins. “Oh, sweetie. Obviously because Phainon’s going to defy the rules of nature by trying to plant another one in Mydei. Duh.”

And she said Mydei was the shameless one.

“Oh dear,” Castorice muttered.

“I…” Hyacine trailed off, blinking a few times before taking a deep breath. “Okay. Well I’m going to go think about anything else. Congratulations Mydei, I’m really happy for you.” Mydei gave a curt nod, a faint smile on his face. Hyacine knew him well enough to understand he meant it well.

Once she walked off, Mydei turned to Cipher. “You scared her away.”

“You’re the one admitting to having birthday sex.”

Mydei scowled. “You admitted to me doing it.”

“And you didn’t deny it, so.”

Right, because Mydei has already established he was done denying certain things when it came to Phainon. He may not openly admit everything, but he’d never be ashamed either.

Before he could get another word in, Mydei heard soft and quick footsteps to his right. His lips tugged upwards upon seeing Clara run up to them with a wide grin, stopping as she bounced on her feet.

“Mydei, look.” She held credits up and if Mydei had to guess, it was no more than ten thousand. “Look what I got from Grandpa Eurypon.”

Mydei cocked a brow. “He just gave you that?”

“Nope,” she said, popping the ‘p.’ “Cipher taught me how to pickpocket it from him so that—”

“Woah,” Cipher drawled, cutting her off with a forced laugh. She leaned closer to Clara, muttering beside her. “I thought we agreed that the old man willingly gave you the money.”

Clara covered her mouth due to her slip up. “Uh oh…”

Mydei gave a disapproving look to Cipher. “Why are you teaching my child how to steal?” He then looked down, a stern look on his face as he addressed Clara. “Anything aunt Cipher tells you, do the exact opposite. Okay?”

“Rude,” Cipher mumbled.

Clara nodded. “Okay. Does that mean I have to give grandpa his money back?” Mydei thought about it, glancing across the room at his father while he did so. Their relationship had already been mended, and Mydei figured this small act wouldn’t do much. It would be humorous, if anything. The man was well off enough.

“Keep it. He won’t notice.”

She curled her fist in victory, shoving the money into her pockets. “I have to go, I have other stuff to do.”

“It doesn’t involve stealing, does it?” Mydei asked.

Clara shook her head. “No. It’s something different.”

“Oh really? What’s that?”

“Bribery,” she beamed, before skipping off.

Mydei turned to Cipher. The woman had the audacity to shrug and smirk. “Kids and their imagination, huh?” Mydei made a mental note to give Clara a proper conversation next time she spends time with her aunt. “But let’s not talk about that! Let’s talk about how Phainon has been skirting around your father all night.”

He knew she was only baiting him in changing the topic, but it worked anyway and Mydei couldn’t help but grow amused. “Has he now?”

“Very much so.”

Castorice giggled. “I think your father is trying to speak with him about business.”

Of course. Knowing Eurypon, the man was seeking another potential partner and who better to turn to than the man high up in his job? “How unfortunate for Phainon.”

“What’s unfortunate for me?” A fourth voice asked.

Mydei acknowledged Phainon with a fond expression, preparing his own response when Cipher beat him to the punch. “Oh hey, who invited the forty year old man?”

Phainon frowned. “I’m thirty.”

“That’s what I said.”

“Don’t listen to her,” Mydei said. “She’s deflecting. She was teaching our daughter how to steal and bribe.”

Cipher’s eyes wandered around the room. “Do you hear that, Cas? I think Hyacine was calling for us.” She grabbed ahold of the woman’s arm before shooting Mydei a quick smile. “Gotta go!” She hurried off, making a clean getaway before Phainon could even respond to Mydei’s comment.

Go figure.

“Nice,” Phainon said. “How much did she steal?”

Then again, maybe it was a good thing Cipher left before Phainon could answer. At least Mydei wouldn’t have to worry about his ridiculous words enabling her. “Really? Our daughter stole and you’re asking how much?”

“Just making sure our little girl does a quality job.” And really, Mydei couldn’t say he was surprised. The disbelief was inevitable, but this wasn’t the first time Phainon’s leniency made Mydei sigh. “Besides,” the man continued, standing behind Mydei to wrap those big arms around him. “I don’t see you freaking out. If you’re calm, I’m calm.”

Mydei didn’t pry Phainon off, instead leaning into the touch as they both looked around the room. “Your perception skills are—”

“Terrible,” Phainon cut off. “So I’ve heard.”

“From who?”

His boyfriend chucked against the side of his neck. “You. Countless times.” That just meant Mydei knew what he was talking about, especially considering he trusted his own opinion the most. Phainon’s voice dropped barely above a whisper. “My perception skills aren’t bad when I say that tonight has been amazing, though.”

Mydei breathed out, his expression relaxing into something more soft. The more Mydei glanced around, observing the state of everyone else around him, the more he agreed with Phainon.

“Of course it would be.”

“I’m proud of you, Mydei.”

Mydei pursed his lips.

He should’ve been used to it by now. Phainon said that exact statement more times than he could count, primarily during the renovation process. Any small step the building made, Phainon would be there to remind him.

But hearing that voice, so low and close to his ears, it stirred something inside of him. Maybe it was the promise of what would come later that night that invoked such a reaction, but Mydei had to redirect the topic fast before his indecent thoughts controlled his mind.

Mydei angled his head slightly towards Phainon. “Hey. Have you been avoiding my father?”

Phainon eased his grip, looking around in a frenzy. “Why? Is he coming over here?” The blond snorted, shaking his head at the shift in attitude. “Look, I know he means well. I do! But I do not want to talk about possible collaborations right now. The weekend just started.”

“At least you know he likes you.” Which was a given the moment Mydei told his father about Phainon. Maybe it was the stable job that immediately brought his approval, or maybe it was Phainon’s ability to handle being a single parent for so long. Whatever it was, Eurypon was a fan.

Although, maybe too much.

“And that’s great, but can he like me without it being strictly business?”

“Business is his life,” Mydei said. Phainon should consider himself lucky that this wasn’t the same Eurypon from a few years ago. Mydei wasn’t sure what calmed the man down, but he was rather appreciative that he didn’t have to deal with it anymore. “Just tell him no. He can handle it.”

Phainon faked a pout. “Like you told me no when I asked to be a sponsor?”

Mydei scoffed. He did that for a reason, thank you. “Personal relationships don’t qualify for sponsors. I already told you that, plus you’ve done your part.” A lot of the money put towards the place was from Phainon, anyway. Mydei still had money saved from his ridiculously high paychecks back when he was simply working for him.

“Yeah, yeah,” Phainon muttered, nuzzling against Mydei’s neck once more. “Just want to support you all I can, baby.”

Fuck. Mydei was getting dizzy again. He needed to do something.

Fortunately for him — and very unfortunately for Phainon — he spotted the perfect opportunity. Right in the form of Eurypon passing their way.

“Father,” Mydei called out. He could feel Phainon tense, making a pained sound from behind him. Eurypon stopped in his tracks. “Phainon’s been looking for you.”

Mydei could’ve sworn he felt Phainon try to hide himself, as if he didn’t have Mydei beat in size.

Phainon unwinded himself from Mydei, taking a deep breath before acknowledging Eurypon with the brightest smile he could muster. “There you are, sir. You’re… not easy to find.”

Eurypon was none the wiser. “Really? I was just over there with my wife.”

“Phainon’s not perceptive,” Mydei chimed in. “Well, you two enjoy your talk.” He fought back a smirk when he noticed Phainon’s face, how the man fought to mask his betrayal. Dramatic, you ask Mydei, as if this was the worst kind of conversation he could have with Eurypon. He should’ve been there five years ago, then Mydei would’ve understood.

He left them on their own, eyes scanning the area to see where he was needed. Mydei assumed he already spent enough time standing off to the side. A proper host should interact with his guests to guarantee they had a good time, and that’s exactly what he intended to do.

Mydei exhaled, a very content thing, as he wiped the last of the tables. The cleaning process wasn’t too hasty, but even if it had been, he wouldn’t have minded much. Nothing could dampen his mood, nor his utter satisfaction with how the night played out.

As perfect as it had been, he still couldn’t process it.

“You’re awfully quiet over there,” his mother teased, setting her own cleaning rag down. He assured her that he could manage that part on his own, but she was rather persistent and ended up helping anyway. “Let me guess. You enjoyed the evening so much and you can’t find the proper words.”

Ever the observant one.

Mydei huffed in amusement. “Something like that.”

“I figured.” Gorgo took a few steps closer to him, placing a reassuring hand on his arm. “I know you’ve heard it all night, but I’m proud of you Mydeimos. More than you know.”

He smiled. “Thank you, mother.”

Despite Mydei being the one to leave all of those years ago, it meant the world to him that he could finally share this with his mother. That she had the chance to see him bring it all to life. As well as his father, who finally wrapped his head around Mydei’s ambition and decided to support him instead of fighting it.

“I heard Miss Clara is staying with her aunts tonight,” Gorgo said, playfully nudging Mydei in the side. “For no reason, I’m sure.” Her tone suggested otherwise, though luckily Mydei has grown accustomed to her playful comments regarding Phainon. They were almost no different than what he experienced with Cipher.

“For a reason,” he corrected gently. “There’s something I need to talk with Phainon about tonight.”

It’s not like he hadn’t been anticipating the conversation for two days, or anything.

“I know,” Gorgo nodded. Mydei looked at her with curiosity, watching as her face grew serious. Her smile remained. “And I’m incredibly happy for you, Mydeimos.”

The more he studied her, the more he realized that she did know. She understood what was up with him without even sparing a glance downward, to at least try and confirm it. Mydei spoke quietly, “How did you…”

“Mother’s intuition.” Mydei was aware her intuition was good, but he didn’t know it was that good. “And your reaction confirms it, so I mean what I said. I am beyond happy for you and Phainon.”

“And Clara.”

“And Clara,” his mother agreed. “I was wondering when you’d give her a baby sibling.”

Mydei chuckled. “You sound like Cipher. Except Cipher was surprised, but you’re not.”

“Why would I be surprised?” Gorgo asked. “You two have built a beautiful little family, I see it any time you’re together. Of course I wouldn’t be surprised that you’re deciding to expand it.” Mydei didn’t want anything more, something that was decided the moment he and Phainon got together. “Plus, Cipher and I placed bets. I’m relieved I won.”

Mydei pressed his brows together, mouth slightly gaping. “Mother.”

Just then, Clara decided to run in the building, preventing Mydei from acknowledging his mother’s laugh. “Deimy!” She called out, stopping right in front of him. “I’m leaving with Aunt Cassy and Aunt Cipher now.”

Mydei knelt so that he could be closer to her level. “Have fun, okay?”

“I will,” she said. “Are you telling daddy the thing?”

The corners of Mydei’s lips tugged upwards. “I am.”

Clara took that well, her face lighting up before she threw her arms around Mydei. “I love you.”

Mydei returned the gesture, placing a gentle kiss on the side of her head. “I love you, too. Be good for Cas and Cipher.”

She pulled away. “I will. Make sure daddy has a good reaction tonight, or I’ll be having a word with him.”

Gorgo chimed in, amused. “What would the state of that house be without you?” Without as much life, that’s for sure. Clara completed Mydei just as much as Phainon did and he couldn’t imagine having one without the other.

Clara put both hands on her hips. “In shambles.”

“I believe it,” his mother said. “Have a good time tonight, honey.”

“Listen,” Phainon quickly defended. “I know you said that personal relationships don’t qualify for sponsors.” Mydei tilted his head, a stern look on his face as he prepared for the worst. “But I had to do something, and I don’t want you to be mad.”

“Phainon.”

The man brought his phone closer, allowing Mydei to read the screen. “Just, look. I found you one last sponsor… And I think you’ll like this one.” Mydei was fine with the sponsors he had already, not wanting too much to start with, anyway. Still, he read what was on the phone, curious on why it meant so much to him.

Chaser’s Shoes.

A shoe store?

Mydei froze.

The shoe store. The same one he and Phainon met in.

His fiancé… truly was a cheesy idiot.

“You’re kidding,” Mydei said. “You… how did you even think of this?”

Phainon shrugged nonchalantly. “When you’re good, you’re good.” Mydei flicked him in the forehead, causing him to caress the spot with a soft laugh. “Seriously, though. I wanted to do something special. I know you would’ve achieved all of this even without meeting me, but I wanted to remind you that I have always supported you. I will continue to support you.”

‘You would’ve achieved all of this even without me.’

Even the mere thought of such a possibility brought a distaste in Mydei’s mouth. “You’re insane, you know.”

Phainon smirked. “But you’re marrying me.”

Mydei huffed, shaking his head as he wrapped his arms around Phainon’s neck. “That, I am.”

Nine months later

Mydei narrowed his eyes, observing the sight in front of him intently. “A little more to the left,” he said, nodding his head in the direction he spoke of.

Cipher groaned. “You know, I was going to ask if you’ve always been this picky but I think we both know the answer.” Cyrene giggled at her words, sorting through a strand of lights on her own.

“I can always just get on the ladder and do it myself,” Mydei countered.

Cyrene and Cipher spoke at the same time. “No.”

He figured as much.

Practically nine months pregnant and everyone kept a firm watch on him these days. Phainon especially, and if Mydei didn’t know the girls as well as he did, he would’ve assumed their strict nature was coming from Phainon himself. Obviously that wasn’t the case, everyone observed him like a hawk the closer he got to delivery.

Still, Mydei believed he could handle climbing a simple ladder.

There wasn’t much else he could do. Mydei couldn’t go back to the gym until all of this was over, not to mention his work load had lessened each month. He appreciated everyone’s coddling, he did, but he’s never been the type to sit around and do nothing. Of course it would be new to him.

There were some perks, though.

Phainon aided him a lot more these days; bringing him food, washing his hair, even going as far as to rubbing Mydei’s sore feet after a long day of walking. It caught Mydei off guard initially, but he grew quite fond of the attention considering he knew it came from a good place.

But right now? It was hard for Mydei to actually sit back, because how hard was it to correctly position a wreath?

“There,” Cipher grunted, leaning over slightly to rearrange the decoration. “How is that, prince perfect?”

Mydei examined it.

It was good enough.

“It looks fine,” he said. “For the love of the Titans, please get off the ladder now. You’re going to break your neck.” Mydei had a safer chance of standing on the damn thing than Cipher did, anyway.

Cipher climbed off, redirecting her attention to additional decor. Mydei hadn’t intended on doing much for the restaurant, but Clara mentioned creating a festive environment and he knew he couldn’t say no. Not with how excited she was when he said yes. It wasn’t all that bad, either, he wanted to own the kind of establishment to care about small things such as holiday decorations.

“So,” Cyrene began, shooting Mydei a smirk. “How did my brother feel about you doing this today?”

Considering the look on her face, Mydei could tell she knew the answer to that. Seriously, why did he end up surrounded by women who did nothing but read through him? “I didn’t tell him.”

Cipher looked back. “You’re kidding.”

“Nope.”

“Yeah,” Cyrene breathed out, shaking her head with a smile. “I thought so. Phainon would sooner call out of work and do it himself before he let you.”

Believe him, Mydei was aware. “I know. Can you fault me for not saying anything?” He stood up, walking to one of the unopened boxes of decorations. Grand Chrysos didn’t open for another two hours, but he needed to at least do his part. He didn’t show up today just to dump it all on Cipher and Cyrene.

“Better be careful, little prince,” Cipher warned, her focus trained in front of her. “Phainon’s too protective, he might lock you in the house until the day finally comes.”

Mydei snorted, preparing to half-absently agree with her when a strong pain froze him in place. He leaned forward, hand clutching the base of his stomach before his eyes began to widen. Mydei didn’t want to assume too quickly, but the pain hadn’t made any indication of subsiding and it felt like nothing he’d experienced before.

The women were too occupied with their own tasks to notice Mydei’s abrupt pause, not to mention the blond fought to not make a sound. He clenched his teeth, screwing his eyes shut the longer the cramps coursed through his body. Walking felt impossible, so he had no choice but to stand there.

“It was just a joke,” Cipher mumbled. “I doubt he’d actually lock you up.”

It was a wonder he could hear her so clearly.

“Mydei?” Cyrene asked. Mydei was unable to see her glance back, the concern plain on her face from his silence. Unfortunately, he failed to see the realization dawn upon her as well, her eyes remaining on him as her voice grew frantic. “Cipher. Call Phainon.”

Mydei finally opened his eyes. Cipher now faced them as well. “Huh? I— oh. Oh, shit.”

Mydei huffed. “I’m fine.”

Cyrene shot up, running over to him in an attempt to stabilize him. “You’re not fine, idiot,” she rushed out, walking him towards the door. “You’re going into labor.” As much as he suspected that to be the case, he couldn’t help but grow panicked. Mydei thought he had time, not to mention he had no idea how this would go and right now he just wanted Phainon there.

“Hello?” Cipher spoke as she trailed behind them, no doubt already on the phone. “Yes… no, you need to get your ass down to the hospital now.” Mydei couldn’t hear Phainon’s voice through the speaker, but he assumed the man was just as alarmed. “What do you think? Yes! Now quit yapping and get down there… Ugh, I'll tell you everything later… Okay, yeah. Bye.”

Mydei snorted. “What’d he say?”

Cipher sucked her teeth, running in front of them to hold the door open. “Way too much.”

Sounds like Phainon.

Mydei didn’t have it in him to ask for the specifics, too busy trying to bear the pain. Each step put a strain on his back, causing him to fall further into Cyrene. She didn’t seem to care, surprisingly managing to hold him up.

“I’m gonna call Cas,” Cipher added, pressing away at her phone. “She wanted to be there too.”

Cyrene quickly helped Mydei into the passenger seat. Mydei had to take deep breaths just to make it feel doable. “What about Clara?”

“It’s fine,” Cipher assured. “Phainon said he’s going to pick her up from school before coming over.”

Mydei groaned, clutching onto his stomach. “You guys… are far too worried about me.”

“Shut up, little prince,” Cipher retorted, climbing into the backseat. “You’re lucky this happened around us. I mean, were you really going to stand there and say nothing? You’re so stubborn, you know that.”

Mydei chuckled, breathless due to the ache inside of him. “Yes, because I feel extraordinarily lucky right now.” On the bright side, bantering with Cipher helped. It didn’t do a lot, or as much as he hoped it would, but conversing made it easier to at least try and focus on something else.

Cyrene finally situated herself into the driver’s seat, starting the car immediately. “Don’t worry. We’ll be there in no time, Phainon will too.”

Mydei hissed after another surge of discomfort, saying nothing as Cyrene began the drive.

The moment Phainon parked at the hospital, he grabbed onto Clara’s hand and the two ran towards the building.

He knew he could’ve gotten there sooner, but he and Mydei promised his daughter that she would also be there when the day arrived, so he saw being late as no issue. All that mattered was being there now, nothing separating him from his fiancé, who was no doubt in a lot of pain right now.

Which is why Phainon had to see him, now.

He luckily found Cipher and Castorice in the lobby, the two of them shooting up from their chairs once Phainon made himself known. They hurried over to him as well, the four of them huddling in the lobby.

“How is he?” Phainon rushed out, eyes darting around for any sight of a doctor. “Have you guys heard anything?”

Castorice reached out, her hand a gentle touch on his. “He’s okay. Delivery was quick, the doctor said we were clear to go in.” Phainon tilted his head, brows furrowing at the idea of them still being outside despite having the go-ahead. Castorice was quick to notice. “We knew you wanted to be here sooner, so we thought you should be the first to go in and see him.”

That… was really sweet of them.

Phainon felt the corners of his eyes begin to sting, his lips curling upwards. “Thank you.” Castorice returned the gesture and Phainon looked down, his soft eyes meeting Clara’s wide ones. “Ready?” She nodded rapidly, that being the only answer he received. Phainon squeezed her hand, listening to Cipher provide him with the room number before setting off.

It didn’t take long for him to reach the area, eyeing each numbered door until he stumbled upon Mydei’s. With a deep breath, and another squeeze of Clara’s hand, he pushed it open.

It took a few steps for Phainon to see Mydei clearly, the latter lolling his head to the side at the noise. It was clear his baby was exhausted, Phainon knew childbirth could be tedious, but Mydei still had it in him to smile.

Clara finally let go of his hand.

“Mydei!” She cried out, running over towards the bad. She threw her arms around him, briefly catching Mydei off guard before he hugged her back. “You’re okay.”

Mydei chuckled. “Of course I am. Don’t tell me your father was worrying you.”

“Uh,” she drawled, pulling away to look back at Phainon. “A little bit. He drove over the speed limit.”

Phainon began approaching the bed as well. “Hey, we agreed not to talk about that.”

“Wonderful,” Mydei muttered. “I’m giving birth and your first instinct is to break the law.”

Clara shook her head. “Him and his instincts.”

As nice as it was to know everything was okay, that Mydei could still have the energy to poke fun at him, he began looking around the room. It was only the three of them, leaving Phainon unaware of how long Mydei had been alone until they arrived. “Baby?”

“Yeah?” Mydei and Clara answered simultaneously. The two of them faced each other, eyes wide in shock before they let out a small laugh.

So freaking cute.

But really, “where is she?”

He could see Mydei open his mouth to answer, unable to get the chance when the door behind them opened. Phainon turned around, his concern slowly starting to drop as soon as two doctors walked in.

With his baby girl in one of their arms.

Phainon blinked, softly gasping.

The doctor only grinned before carefully entering the room. Phainon was unable to turn away, the sight of his newborn daughter leaving him utterly speechless, even as the doctor began to speak. “So, is this the father who worries a lot?”

Mydei pursed his lips. “That’s him.”

Phainon still couldn’t speak.

“Well,” the doctor continued, stopping by Mydei’s bedside. Even Clara couldn’t look away, her bright eyes watering the longer she stared at her baby sister. “You have a beautiful and healthy girl.”

“Yeah,” Phainon whispered, walking closer to get a better look.

He remembered the feeling all too well, it was something that never went away each time it happened. The moment he laid eyes upon Clara, he knew he would love her unconditionally for the rest of his life. The exact same could be said for right now as he gazed down at his new daughter, surrounded by the people who meant the most to him.

Phainon wanted to hold her, needed to hold her, but Phainon also made a promise to Mydei. One that was mutually decided, and it seemed Mydei needed no reminder as they both looked towards Clara.

Mydei spoke softly. “Do you want to hold her?”

Clara raised her brows, her expression almost scared. “Am I allowed to?”

“You are,” Phainon answered, with a lighthearted huff. “Come here.”

He led her towards the chair in the corner, picking up on the sudden excitement in her movements. Phainon could tell she was also nervous — hell, he was too — but she remained as calm as she could.

The doctor approached them before leaning down slowly. “Hold your arms out like that— Yes, there you go.” Phainon gave them space, glancing over his shoulder to ensure Mydei was okay. The latter only watched the scene with awe. “And just support her head like— See, you got it. You don’t even need me.”

Phainon dug through his pockets once the baby was in Clara’s arm, taking a picture of the moment so he could have it forever. Even though he was sure the memory would burn itself into his brain.

“I’m holding her,” Clara said, her voice low. “I’m doing it, Mydei.”

Mydei laughed gently. “You are. I’m so proud of you.”

Phainon continued to watch, and could faintly see the baby’s eyes flutter open. He narrowed his own, getting closer to confirm his suspicions. The triumphant smile was inevitable once he realized he was right.

“She has blue eyes.”

Mydei scoffed. “She’ll have blonde hair.”

Phainon shrugged. “Too soon to tell, dear.” Mydei shook his head, presumably because he was so certain the baby would take his eye color. It was one of the many things they’ve talked about regarding their daughter, thus reminding Phainon of the most important one. “Hey, what’s her name?”

Before the gender was revealed, it was agreed that Mydei would decide the name had the baby been a girl. Phainon would’ve gotten the luxury if it was the other way around, even though he didn’t mind Mydei being in charge of the choice at all. Just having a child with him was enough.

“Her name is Iris.”

Phainon froze.

Clara gasped, as quietly as she could. “That’s—”

“My mother’s middle name,” Phainon finished, his voice uneven. “Mydei…”

“I had the idea from the beginning,” Mydei said. “It was humorous, really. Watching you make lists of names while I already had mine picked out.”

“That’s also my favorite flower,” Clara added, a tear rolling down her cheek. She wasn’t sad, though, far from it if the look of adoration on her face was any indication. Phainon knew because it was exactly how he felt as well.

Mydei pointed towards her. “That’s another reason.”

Clara giggled at that before acknowledging Phainon with seriousness. “Daddy, do you want to hold her?”

Yeah, he really did.

Phainon simply nodded and approached her, carefully leaning down to bring the baby into his arms. Iris’s eyes fluttered once more, Phainon unable to focus on anything else as they eventually landed on him.

“I could get used to that,” Mydei commented smugly. Phainon didn’t look away, but he acknowledged his words with a smile of his own. He wasn’t sure how Mydei meant it, if it was pertaining to Iris specifically or the idea of having more children. Either way, it didn’t matter.

Because Phainon had already gotten used to it.
